Sources indicate that US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds have now suffered two consecutive weeks of withdrawals exceeding $1 billion, a remarkable reversal for products often treated as the clearest gauge of institutional demand. The latest weekly tally also extends the run of daily redemptions to seven trading sessions. That does not mean every institutional holder is selling Bitcoin, but it does remove one of the market's more visible sources of buying support.

Sources indicate that the numbers cover the trading week ending Friday, November 13, and are based on reported fund-flow data. They should not be confused with changes in fund valuations caused by Bitcoin's falling price.

Recent findings suggest that according to The Block's analysis of SoSoValue data, US spot Bitcoin ETFs registered approximately $1.07 billion of net outflows for the week. The previous week had already recorded around $1.28 billion, putting the combined two-week figure at $2.35 billion. Seven consecutive negative trading sessions accounted for roughly $1.91 billion of the retreat.

The daily pattern is revealing: withdrawals were not limited to one frightening session. Monday through Friday each ended in the red, with Wednesday and Thursday particularly heavy. NewsBTC covered the earlier five-day outflow streak, but the completed week's figures show that investors had not yet turned the tap back on.

BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust, IBIT, accounted for about $143.5 million of Friday's approximately $185.5 million in net withdrawals. Fidelity's FBTC made up roughly $41.9 million, while the other funds tracked reported no net flows for the session, according to the same dataset. It is tempting to read that as a judgement on either manager, but the more plausible interpretation is that investors use the largest and most liquid vehicles when adjusting exposure rapidly.

Industry observers note that the fact that a particular ETF experiences redemptions does not tell us whether shares were held by hedge funds, retail brokerage customers or other institutions. Nor does it reveal their reasons for selling. Portfolio rebalancing, risk limits and macro hedges can look identical in an aggregate daily flow table.

In a recent development, bitcoin trades around the clock on spot exchanges and in derivatives markets. US-listed ETFs operate during market hours, and their creation-and-redemption processes connect the share market with underlying Bitcoin exposure. ETF data therefore offers a useful window, not a complete map, of demand. Large holders outside the products can still buy while funds lose money, and vice versa.

There is also a distinction between a withdrawal and a loss. If Bitcoin falls while ETF shares are held, the value of assets declines even without net redemptions. Conversely, a fund can experience inflows during a falling market. Keeping those measurements separate makes analysis much more useful than treating any red number as interchangeable.

Industry observers note that the first signal to watch is whether the next US trading week brings even a modest return to positive daily flows. A second is the distribution across products: broad-based inflows would suggest more than one investor cohort is stepping back in. Finally, price stability without significant ETF buying would show whether the market has found demand elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that the broader institutional picture is not limited to daily flows. Changes affecting companies such as Strategy and Metaplanet underline how benchmark decisions and portfolio rules can influence crypto-linked exposure. For now, the sustained outflows are a warning about current appetite, not proof that the long-term ETF market has failed.

Bitcoin Breaks Below $63K as Market Panic Intensifies

📅 15 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/bitcoin-breaks-below-63k-as-market-panic-intensifies/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, bitcoin breaks below $63 on Sunday, November 15, even briefly falling toward $62,000 as selling pressure spread across the cryptocurrency market.
  • Recent findings suggest that bitcoin (BTC) dropped to approximately $62,080.91, according to CoinGecko data, marking its weakest price in four months.
  • The downturn also affected other major digital assets.

According to recent reports, bitcoin breaks below $63 on Sunday, November 15, even briefly falling toward $62,000 as selling pressure spread across the cryptocurrency market. Although BTC recovered above $65,000 after reaching its lowest level since July, the rebound did little to ease concerns about deteriorating market sentiment and weakening institutional demand.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin (BTC) dropped to approximately $62,080.91, according to CoinGecko data, marking its weakest price in four months. Despite recovering some losses, the cryptocurrency remained down nearly 15% over the previous seven days.

The downturn also affected other major digital assets. Ethereum (ETH) declined 19.5% over the week, while Solana (SOL) recorded a 20.7% loss. The total cryptocurrency market capitalization fell approximately 4% over 24 hours to $2.26 trillion, reflecting the scale of the broader correction.

Bitcoin’s latest decline follows its move below $70,000 on Friday, extending a correction that has increasingly affected the wider digital asset market.

It has been revealed that the drop toward $62,000 represents a significant deterioration from the levels BTC maintained earlier in November. Although buyers stepped in after the latest decline and pushed the price back above $65,000, the recovery has not yet reversed the broader downward trend.

It has been revealed that the weakness is not limited to Bitcoin. Ethereum and Solana have both recorded losses exceeding 19% over the past week, indicating that investors are reducing exposure across several major cryptocurrencies rather than concentrating their selling on BTC alone.

The broader market has also lost substantial value, with its capitalization declining to approximately $2.26 trillion. This reflects the combination of falling token prices and increasingly cautious investor positioning.

For Bitcoin, the ability to maintain levels above the latest low will be notable in determining whether the market can stabilize or whether another wave of selling could follow.

Industry observers note that investor sentiment has deteriorated alongside prices. The Crypto Fear & Greed Index dropped to 10 on Sunday, down from 13 on Saturday and 20 on Friday.

The reading places the market firmly in the extreme fear category, highlighting how quickly confidence has weakened during the latest correction.

Industry observers note that such low sentiment levels suggest that investors are becoming increasingly defensive and less willing to take risks. While extreme fear can sometimes coincide with potential market bottoms, it does not necessarily mean that prices have reached their lowest point.

The continued decline in the sentiment index also reflects uncertainty surrounding institutional investment flows and liquidity conditions across the cryptocurrency sector.

Institutional investment activity has added another source of pressure to Bitcoin’s recent decline.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds recorded approximately $2.35 billion in combined net outflows over the two weeks ending November 13. The funds lost around $1.07 billion during the latest week, following $1.28 billion in withdrawals during the previous week.

The withdrawals extended Bitcoin ETFs’ negative streak to seven consecutive trading sessions. BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) also recorded its 11th consecutive session of outflows on Friday.

Persistent redemptions suggest that institutional investors have become more cautious about maintaining their Bitcoin exposure amid the deteriorating market environment.

ETF flows are an vital indicator of institutional demand, and continued withdrawals can make it harder for Bitcoin to attract the buying interest needed to reverse a sustained decline.

Industry observers note that bitcoin’s decline toward $62,000 has placed the market at an vital point in its current correction. The recovery above $65,000 offers some indication that buyers are still active, but the cryptocurrency remains significantly lower over the past week.

The next challenge will be whether BTC can maintain its rebound and attract enough demand to establish a more stable price range. Continued ETF withdrawals and extreme fear sentiment could make that difficult, particularly if selling pressure spreads further across the market.

Altcoins are also facing considerable weakness, with Ethereum and Solana recording steeper weekly losses than Bitcoin. This suggests that a broader improvement in market conditions may be necessary before a sustained recovery can develop.

For now, investors will be watching whether Bitcoin can hold above its latest low or whether deteriorating sentiment and institutional outflows will push prices toward another downside test.

Do you think Bitcoin has reached a local bottom near $62,000, or could the sell-off continue?

Will institutional investors return to Bitcoin ETFs once market sentiment improves, or are the recent outflows a sign of a longer period of reduced demand?

The market slipped toward $63,000 during Saturday's trading after a difficult week for digital assets, leaving traders debating whether the move represents a final flush or simply another stage of a broader retreat.

It has been revealed that the distinction matters. A sharp fall can produce attractive entry points, but it can also expose how quickly leveraged positions and thin order books amplify one another. The latest numbers are a snapshot of trading on November 14, not a live quote or a forecast for the week ahead.

Industry observers note that coinDesk reported that Bitcoin traded down to roughly $63,400 on Saturday, with its weekly decline exceeding 15% at that point. Ether and several major altcoins had experienced even larger weekly percentage losses. That broader weakness is worth highlighting because it suggests the pressure was not confined to a single Bitcoin-specific headline or one isolated exchange.

Weekend trading can be particularly unforgiving. Liquidity providers may quote less aggressively, while automated liquidation systems do not take Saturdays off. A relatively modest amount of spot selling can therefore travel further through the order book than it might during busier weekday sessions. It is a possible amplifier, though not proof that liquidations caused the entire move.

The decline also arrives against a more cautious institutional backdrop. US spot Bitcoin funds have recorded a prolonged run of net withdrawals, extending the selling discussed in NewsBTC's earlier report on Bitcoin ETF outflows. These products do not dictate Bitcoin's price, but their flows provide one measurable indication of whether an important group of investors is adding exposure or reducing it.

There is an notable mechanical distinction here. A fund's net outflow is not necessarily a direct measure of total Bitcoin sold in the wider market, and changes in assets under management also reflect price movements. Still, a sustained absence of fresh fund demand can leave the spot market with less of a cushion when other holders decide to sell.

Sources indicate that on-chain analyst James Check has described the environment in terms of capitulation, according to CoinDesk. That captures the emotional side of the market: investors who tolerated earlier drawdowns finally decide they would rather hold cash than wait for a rebound. But a capitulation narrative is not a timestamped bottom signal. Markets can experience several waves of forced or reluctant selling before stabilising.

Sources indicate that A more useful test is what happens after the initial bounce. Does Bitcoin hold its recovery on increasing spot participation, or does the rebound fade as soon as volatility eases? Are funding rates, exchange balances and ETF flows telling a consistent story, or are they pulling in different directions? Answers to those questions carry more weight than a declaration that the market looks cheap.

Traders are also processing a changing interest-rate outlook and the implications of recent US inflation figures. NewsBTC's analysis of October CPI and the rate backdrop offers useful context: Bitcoin can behave like a high-beta risk asset when expectations for borrowing costs change abruptly, even when the longer-term investment thesis is framed around monetary independence.

For the coming week, watch whether trading volumes improve as US markets reopen and whether Bitcoin can defend its weekend range without relying on a short-lived derivatives squeeze. The latest slide deserves attention, but it does not, on its own, settle the argument about where the cycle goes next.

Naturally, the question becomes — Can the move increase capital inflows by allowing people to use Bitcoin as collateral and therefore increase stablecoin volumes?

In essence, could this be the much needed catalyst for a DeFi resurgence?

In a recent development, Aave [AAVE] has gained DAO approval to add support for using Bitcoin as collateral.

It has been revealed that the proposal will allow holders to lock up their BTC to borrow stablecoins. Notably, the proposal was unanimously approved on 9th November. This means Bitcoin holders can gain new liquidity through Aave’s $21 million credit market by borrowing stablecoins using their BTC as collateral.

Sources indicate that as the chart below shows, Aave will be allocating $21 million to their credit products to five different stablecoins. The two largest stablecoins will be USDT and USDC which have been allocated $8 million each. These account for almost 76% of the total capacity.

It has been revealed that meanwhile, AAVE’s native stablecoin GHO will be allocated $1 million. The last $4 million will be split evenly between USDG and RLUSD with $2 million allocated to each.

Why does this matter? Well, this allocation shows that Aave is looking to blend both traditional stablecoins and newer assets to provide more options for borrowing. Consequently, this will allow Bitcoin holders to borrow against several stablecoin markets using their BTC as collateral.

As Aave Founder and CEO Stani Kulechov explained,.

According to recent reports, the Babylon-built Bitcoin-backed market on Aave V4 reveals how easily latest markets can be rolled out using the Hub and Spoke model. Native BTC collateral, without wrappers or custodians, unlocks a major new source of liquidity for on-chain borrowing and lending.

Crypto lending is slowing down as borrowers reduce their exposure amid market uncertainty.

According to Galaxy Research, the overall crypto-backed loan market fell by 16.78% during Q2, hitting a total value of $56.16 billion. This is the first time that all major lending sectors have fallen since 2022. DeFi lending also saw a sharp fall, with total active loans decreasing from $47.13 billion to $21.94 billion between April and July. In short, traders have lost interest in borrowing against their assets.

Sources indicate that however, Aave has seen an opposite trend, with the platform noting all-time highs in active loans on the Aave V4 platform, increasing by almost 100% in Q2 to $500 million. Against this backdrop, the addition of Bitcoin to the lending market could lend further growth potential.

In essence, by allowing BTC holders to use their asset as collateral, the market could see more capital flowing into DeFi, more collateral on Aave, and more demand for on-chain borrowing.

Aave V4’s Hub-and-Spoke architecture provides an isolated environment in which integrations can deploy both standard and custom Spokes without affecting other assets on the Hub.

The crypto market is facing its worst liquidity crunch since the 2022 bear market.

Industry observers note that the overall stablecoin market cap has fallen by about $14 billion over the past month. By 10th November, the total stablecoin market cap was around $290 billion, according to DeFiLlama. In fact, the last two weeks alone saw the most net stablecoin outflows ever in over four years. Over half of this drop came from USDT and a further 20% from USDC.

This pressure can be seen across the DeFi space. In fact, the total DeFi TVL fell to around $76.6 billion on 12th November, with stablecoin market cap sitting at $286.9 billion at press time. However, DeFi TVL also fell by 9.7% week-on-week.

Against this backdrop, Aave’s move could offer a newly introduced source of liquidity.

There is one technical distinction worth keeping though. This integration doesn’t automatically mean any fresh stablecoins will flow into DeFi. Instead, borrowers will have access to liquidity that is already sitting in Aave. For liquidity to grow, the protocol will also need to attract more lenders and fresh deposits.

As per the attached chart, there is still a long way to go before the lending market on Bitcoin hits significant levels.

Industry observers note that BTC-backed loans reached $3.58 billion in 2025, representing just 0.24% of Bitcoin’s market cap. So, by supporting Bitcoin as collateral, Aave could help unlock this largely untapped lending demand.

Aave’s move could also expose its lending market to greater risks.

Sources indicate that according to AMBCrypto, although this new borrowing opportunity on Aave will create new demand, it can also lead to greater speculation. People can borrow stablecoins using BTC as collateral and then re-lend them into leveraged crypto positions.

Consider this — Bitcoin Futures Open Interest increased by 12.1% in 19 days up to late-October, despite a 5.3% price decrease in BTC. This indicated that traders were increasing their leveraged exposure.

Sources indicate that this continued into November, with Bitfinex reporting that this was the fifth time traders added leverage to their positions while BTC fell. The previous 4 times this occurred, traders executed liquidations of long positions worth over $800 million.

For Aave, the concern is that easier access to Bitcoin credit could add another source of speculation.

In a recent development, ultimately, the move by Aave to integrate Bitcoin comes at a time where DeFi needs liquidity. However, its impact remains to be seen still. While the integration could entice early lenders and stablecoin deposits, there is a risk that high levels of demand could come from speculation and cause further volatility in the market.

Thus, Aave may unlock a latest source of liquidity. However, turning that liquidity into DeFi growth will be the test.

Attackers redirected customers’ Bitcoin mining power through Luxor’s Commander platform over the weekend, prompting its CEO to problem a warning to crypto businesses.

Bitcoin mining services provider Luxor has warned that AI-enabled cyberattacks are becoming increasingly difficult to defend against after attackers compromised its mining-management platform and redirected customers’ computing power to another mining pool over the weekend.

In an X post on Sunday, Luxor CEO Nick Hansen said the attack came through a “sophisticated AI-enabled vector,” without specifying how AI was used in the attack, warning that these types of attacks will only get more frequent over time.

It has been revealed that “At this moment, anyone running any sort of substantial business, especially in crypto, is inundated with AI-enabled attacks,” Hansen stated in an X post. “This does not seem to be slowing down; rather, it’s speeding up as models get better and more attackers enter the arena.”.

The warning comes as security researchers have documented the spread of AI-assisted hacking tools, raising the prospect of faster attacks against businesses holding money or controlling valuable infrastructure.

“Abliterated models are running 24/7 against your entire surface, looking for a little crack, which they then use to (almost instantly) expand,” added Hansen.

Hansen said Luxor has had to put the majority of its feature work on hold in order to harden its cybersecurity. The manufacturer has also acquired its own GPUs to run unrestricted open-weight AI models aimed at improving its security posture.

Recent findings suggest that “I urge anyone running a similar service to do the same. It’s your only defense in this newly introduced AI-powered dark forest. ‘The only thing that stops a bad guy with a gun is a good guy with a gun.’”.

Initial reports suggested that about 64,000 mining machines representing 13 exahashes per second were redirected to the OCEAN mining pool on Saturday.

Luxor has not confirmed either figure, saying the incident affected just over a dozen customer accounts using its Commander mining-management tool.

Industry observers note that luxor mentioned it patched Commander within two hours of detecting the unauthorized changes and began restoring affected machines to their original pool settings. It pledged to compensate customers in full for the redirected mining power and publish a post-mortem.

Cointelegraph contacted Luxor for comment.

Related: Coinone warns of phishing, identity theft after customer data breach.

It has been revealed that “We have explored the glitch extensively, and it was isolated to the Commander tool. None of Luxor’s other services (including Luxor Pool and LuxOS) were affected,” mentioned Luxor.

Initial reports suggested the attackers received no mining rewards. However, a Bitcoin address identified by CoreX as associated with the incident subsequently received two OCEAN payouts totaling approximately 0.162 BTC, worth about $10,500.

Hansen’s warning follows a string of reported AI-assisted intrusions targeting crypto businesses.

Earlier this month, India’s cybersecurity agency warned that a group called Crafty Falcon was using AI-powered tools to attack financial companies, including cryptocurrency exchanges, stealing wallet keys and siphoning funds.

Recent findings suggest that blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis disclosed in October that an attacker used what it called “offensive agentic techniques” to access its systems. The breach exposed password hashes, live tokens and other customer information.

Anthropic said in a September report that multiple groups had developed “automated exploit foundries” with AI, accelerating the pace of vulnerability research, testing, and exploit design.

Alaska is yet to be called, but the writing is on the wall for President Donald Trump and the Republican Party. The Democrats have seized control of both the U.S. Senate and the U.S. House of Representatives.

For all intents and purposes, this means that Trump is now a lame duck president.

That’s the least of his worries, though, as Democrats could now set their sights on investigating Trump’s crypto ventures. After all, this is a man who amassed a fortune of close to $1.5 billion from cryptocurrency ventures in the first year of his second term in office.

It has been revealed that donald Trump became the first sitting president to launch a memecoin, with OFFICIAL TRUMP [TRUMP] generating over $600M in licensing fees and royalties alone. All while a majority of the memecoin’s retail investors saw red.

He is also the “Co-Founder Emeritus” of World Liberty Financial [WLFI], a DeFi and cryptocurrency platform. According to public filings, the project, co-founded by Eric Trump, Barron Trump, and Donald Trump Jr., brought in $799M in 2025 alone.

According to recent reports, then there’s the matter of an Abu Dhabi-based fund buying $2 billion in USD1, WLF’s own stablecoin, to invest in Binance after the crypto exchange was fined over $4 billion for money laundering violations. Its founder, Changpeng Zhao, pled guilty and served a 4-month jail term before being pardoned by Trump.

It has been revealed that simply put, it can be argued that the president has used his position (and crypto) to monetize the presidency and enrich his personal fortune. Hence, the investigations.

Moving ahead, what should the industry expect now that the Democrats are in control of the U.S Congress?

Industry observers note that well, it wouldn’t be unreasonable to expect a gridlock. After all, many in the crypto industry have historically backed Republican candidates because they championed free market de-regulation and digital asset frameworks.

In a recent development, on the contrary, several prominent Democrats like Sen. Elizabeth Warren, who is also expected to chair the Senate Banking Committee from January, have often been vocal critics of the sector.

However, expecting the worst outcome possible here would allude to a very superficial reading of the situation. This is why it’s key to differentiate between what will happen, what can happen, and what won’t happen.

Yes, the likes of Warren haven’t been the most receptive towards the sector, but party-wide support has been growing over the years.

It has been revealed that consider this – following the latest midterm elections, there are a total of 50 pro-crypto senators against just 33 anti-crypto ones. Similarly, in the House, 241 are at the moment pro-crypto as opposed to 104 who are against crypto.

Those are significant numbers. More importantly, they also suggest that despite some historical bias, the sector enjoys some degree of bipartisan support.

Recent findings suggest that the example of Fairshake is a case in point. The Crypto Super PAC spent millions backing 33 House candidates during the midterms. 19 Republicans and 14 Democrats. At the time of writing, 29 of them had already won.

Industry observers note that legislative evidence from before the midterms is worth looking at too. As Andrew Nalichaev, CEO of HAIA Finance, pointed out,.

… support for rules concerning stablecoins has received bipartisan backing: the GENIUS Act passed the Senate 68 to 30 and the House 308 to 122. An vital glitch that led to the failure of the CLARITY Act in September was the ethics issue regarding officials involved in issuing or supporting tokens.

Likewise, Luke Jacobi, Founder and Editor at OptimistFi, told AMBCrypto,.

Our small comparison of two House final-passage votes on July 17, 2025 found that 102 of 212 voting Democrats backed GENIUS, compared with 78 of 212 for CLARITY: 48.1% versus 36.8%. Both attracted cross-party support, but the 24-vote difference shows why a single ‘pro-crypto’ label misses policy-specific disagreement.

Sources indicate that according to a recent report, over 30% of the population, or 70M people, now hold digital assets. It is evidence that despite some skepticism and vocal criticism, the industry has reached a level of financial integration that will be difficult to reverse right now.

It is also evidence that crypto is no longer a single-party issue. Both red and blue states have their own share of crypto holders. In time, their numbers will grow, and so will the degree of bipartisan support the industry enjoys from lawmakers.

Recent findings suggest that however, the concerns about a possible legislative gridlock and its potential impact on the regulatory clarity the industry desperately seeks aren’t totally unwarranted. In the current landscape, Democrats control the U.S. Congress, while Republicans control the White House.

And while he did suggest that he looks forward to working with Democrats, President Trump has also asserted that he will wield his veto power if need be, especially since Democrats don’t enjoy a veto-proof or filibuster-proof majority.

Industry observers note that this means that realistically, we can expect a certain level of gridlock across the board ranging from budgets, appropriations, and defense spending. Even crypto, if the newly introduced U.S. Congress is intent on investigating President Trump’s ventures.

Hence, the question: How major a concern could this be? According to Dmitri Mihhailov, General Partner at Prifinance,.

Investigations do not change laws already on the books, and the most key one for the industry is already there – The GENIUS Act.

Mihhailov also told AMBCrypto that in his view,.

According to recent reports, … gridlock hurts what is still missing: a federal framework for crypto trading markets. Until Congress passes one, firms rely on agency guidance and court rulings, and a future SEC or CFTC can change guidance much more easily than a statute.

In fact, it can be argued that it’s not the investigation itself that could be concerning for the crypto-sector. Instead, it’s the calendar that could be the problem. Especially since congressional investigations consume time, staff, resources, and political capital, all of which can be used to pass necessary crypto legislation.

The “Wild West.” That’s the reputation the cryptocurrency industry had once upon a time.

Gone are those days, though, as the sector became more mainstream and was embraced by institutions and people world over. Banks, lawmakers, and even nation-states. Heck, even Trump did that within years of calling Bitcoin “a scam.”.

Recent findings suggest that politics is a fickle game, though. It’s not unreasonable to contemplate that some legislators could turn on the industry if the congressional investigations into Trump’s crypto ventures go underway.

According to recent reports, the thing is, as an industry, crypto has well and truly arrived on the world stage over the last few years. Despite perceptions, it is too major to be defined by a singular person’s business interests. In fact, more than political scrutiny, THAT would be the biggest threat to the sector.

According to recent reports, the danger is that crypto as a whole becomes politically coded through its association with high-profile ventures like memecoins and politically connected stablecoins. If every crypto vote starts to look like a vote on a specific politician, moderates on both sides will find it easier to abstain or delay.

Then what could these investigations yield? Well, at the very least, clear-cut ethics, disclosures, and conflict of interest rules for public officials – proposals that were at the core of the CLARITY Act’s failure. And, at the end of the day, won’t that be a win for the industry as a whole?

So, no. While there might be some distancing, lawmakers won’t turn on crypto.

Recent findings suggest that 2026 hasn’t been a great year for the crypto sector so far. The markets aren’t exactly booming, billions have been lost to hacks, and the CLARITY Act failed to go through. Plus, the current President of the United States could soon find himself at the center of an investigation into his crypto dealings.

It is simply a matter of getting used to the latest balance of power in Washington D.C.

Recent findings suggest that the US Senate Banking Committee is preparing to examine nominees for positions at the Securities and Exchange Commission, a development that could eventually influence the tone and priorities of crypto oversight. A hearing scheduled for Thursday, November 19, puts personnel decisions back in the spotlight at a time when industry participants are seeking clearer rules on token offerings, custody and trading venues.

Hearings are part of the appointment process, not the end of it. An appearance before senators does not amount to confirmation, and nominees' eventual influence will depend on their responsibilities, the agency's composition and the laws it must enforce.

CoinDesk reported that the Banking Committee had scheduled a November 19 hearing involving SEC nominees Steven Levine and Kristin Johnson. The proceedings are expected to give senators an opportunity to question the candidates on their approach to securities regulation, though what they actually say should be judged from the hearing record rather than predicted in advance.

In a recent development, the same reporting discussed separate nominees for roles at the Commodity Futures Trading Commission. The CFTC's appointment process is not identical to the SEC's, and a hearing for one agency should not be read as an automatic timetable for the other. Both agencies affect digital-asset activity, but their legal jurisdictions and responsibilities differ.

Industry observers note that businesses building token markets often want to know which rules apply before launching a product, not after it has attracted consumers. Questions can include whether an asset or particular transaction falls within securities law, how intermediaries should register and what disclosures are expected. Regulatory staff and commissioners shape policy through rulemaking, enforcement decisions and public guidance, although courts and Congress also have key roles.

A change in personnel can influence priorities, but it does not instantly rewrite the rules. Existing statutes remain in force, earlier litigation can continue and upcoming policy proposals may need formal procedures. For a organization considering a US product launch, a nomination is therefore a signal to monitor rather than a substitute for legal advice or an enacted regulation.

Recent findings suggest that prediction markets and derivative instruments illustrate the difficulty of drawing clear regulatory lines. NewsBTC's earlier coverage of litigation involving Coinbase, Kalshi and the CFTC demonstrates how novel products can trigger disputes over oversight and market structure. The SEC and CFTC do not necessarily reach the same questions through the same legal framework.

It has been revealed that international developments also provide a reminder that the United States does not set standards in isolation. European tokenisation discussions covered by NewsBTC show regulators elsewhere trying to align traditional financial protections with upcoming technology. US appointees will face the task of balancing market integrity, investor protection and innovation against a global competitive backdrop.

According to recent reports, specific answers about custody, market intermediaries, token distributions and enforcement philosophy would be more informative than general pledges to support innovation or protect consumers. Written responses and subsequent votes are worth watching too. Yet even a persuasive performance at a hearing offers no guarantee of confirmation or a particular policy outcome.

Recent findings suggest that the near-term event is clear: November 19 provides a public checkpoint for the SEC nominees. What follows may shape the regulatory conversation over months and years. Treating a personnel hearing as an immediate market catalyst would be a much bigger claim than the available evidence supports.

It has been revealed that A quarterly US securities filing has put fresh numbers around JPMorgan's exposure to crypto-linked investments. The filing shows larger reported positions in both Strategy, the Bitcoin treasury tech giant, and BlackRock's spot Bitcoin ETF at the end of September. The figures are significant, but they need to be read with care: a Form 13F records reportable investment holdings at a particular date, not a continuous record of what a bank or its customers are buying today.

In a recent development, that nuance is especially important when headlines about large financial institutions are used as shorthand for bullish conviction. The disclosure tells us what was reported, but not necessarily who made each underlying investment decision or why.

In a recent development, the Block reported that JPMorgan's September 30 filing listed 848,932 Strategy shares, up from 624,387 in the previous quarter. The reported value was about $131.3 million. It also listed roughly 11.4 million shares of BlackRock's IBIT spot Bitcoin trust, with a quarter-end value around $540 million and a share-count increase of approximately 9.6%.

Those figures should not be mistaken for half a billion dollars of direct Bitcoin held in a wallet controlled by the bank. IBIT shares are securities that provide exposure through a fund structure. Strategy shares are equity in a company with a substantial Bitcoin treasury and its own operating and financing risks. Both can be influenced by Bitcoin, but neither is identical to owning a BTC coin on-chain.

According to recent reports, institutional investment managers disclose certain US-listed positions on Form 13F after a quarter ends. That means the most recent figures in this story reflect September 30 holdings, not positions on November 15. The filing does not show every asset or liability a reporting entity might have, and it cannot tell readers whether any listed shares were subsequently sold.

It also does not automatically establish that JPMorgan's own proprietary balance sheet made a particular directional bet. Reportable holdings may relate to investment management and other activities. Distinguishing those arrangements is essential before drawing conclusions about corporate strategy or client preferences.

Strategy provides a corporate route to Bitcoin exposure, but its share price also responds to debt issuance, financing terms, dilution and market expectations about its treasury model. NewsBTC's coverage of benchmark decisions involving Strategy and Metaplanet highlights a further variable: index rules can affect demand for organization shares independently of the Bitcoin price itself.

In a recent development, an ETF operates differently. Fund shares seek to track the underlying Bitcoin exposure subject to fees and market mechanics, without conferring ownership of the issuer's broader business. An institution holding both securities might be accessing two different kinds of risk, or serving clients with different mandates. The filing alone does not reveal that motivation.

According to recent reports, bitcoin's price and the appetite for crypto products have deteriorated markedly since September. NewsBTC's reporting on November's spot ETF redemptions is a reminder that institutional positioning can change quickly. A larger September holding can coexist with substantial industry-wide outflows in November without either dataset being incorrect.

The sensible next step is to compare successive filings and separate share-count changes from valuation changes. Readers should also watch how managers describe their exposures, rather than attributing motives from the raw totals. This 13F offers useful evidence of institutional participation in crypto-linked securities. It is not a real-time endorsement of the current Bitcoin price.

Scotland produces substantial amounts of wind power, yet parts of that generation are sometimes curtailed because the electricity grid cannot move it to the places where demand exists. A new policy argument suggests Bitcoin miners could provide a flexible buyer for power that might otherwise go unused. The proposal is attracting attention because curtailment is expensive, but the economics are more complicated than simply turning spare electricity into digital coins.

Recent findings suggest that the idea comes from industry advocates, not from an unveiled government programme. Whether it would reduce costs for consumers depends on location, grid rules, emissions and what miners would actually pay for the electricity.

Recent findings suggest that when transmission capacity is constrained, grid operators may pay generators to reduce output even when the wind is blowing. The system still has to maintain balance and ensure that power can reach customers safely. CoinDesk reported on an argument from the Bitcoin Policy Institute that flexible mining could help consume some of the energy affected by Scotland's network bottlenecks.

In a recent development, the reported cost of curtailment can exceed £1 billion a year, but that should not be mistaken for a pot of money miners could simply recover. Some payments arise from complex system constraints, and installing a new industrial load will not necessarily remove the need for other balancing actions. A credible proposal requires location-specific modelling rather than a national headline number.

It has been revealed that bitcoin mining machines can, in principle, reduce consumption quickly when electricity becomes scarce or valuable elsewhere. They do not depend on uninterrupted processing in quite the same way as many conventional businesses. That gives miners a potential role as interruptible customers, willing to operate when power is cheap and switch off at times of peak demand.

But the equipment needs reliable commercial arrangements to justify its capital cost. A facility operating only during unpredictable periods of curtailment may earn too little to cover machines, buildings, cooling and maintenance. The central question is how many hours of usable electricity would be available and at what total delivered cost after grid charges and other expenses.

Using energy that would otherwise be curtailed could be beneficial under certain conditions, yet it does not automatically make a mining site carbon-neutral. The actual comparison depends on the electricity mix, whether the latest demand changes generator behaviour, the facility's operating schedule and the alternatives for the power. Grid reinforcement, batteries and other demand-response projects may compete to solve the same problem.

Sources indicate that the broader mining sector is already weighing energy against newly introduced computing opportunities. NewsBTC recently covered MARA's Bitcoin sales and AI data-centre aims, while another report examined an AI-focused shift at Hyperscale Data. These moves show that miners are increasingly being judged as power and infrastructure operators as well as Bitcoin producers.

Before declaring success, any Scottish mining proposal would need transparent figures for curtailment hours, transmission capacity, tariffs, environmental impacts and the ability to curtail the mine itself. It would also need to explain who captures the benefit: the miner, the generator, the network operator or bill payers. Those answers could support a limited trial, or show that another use of the electricity is better.

The debate is worthwhile because renewable generation and grid capacity are growing at different speeds. Bitcoin mining could be one tool in a larger flexibility toolkit. Presenting it as a guaranteed cure for Scotland's grid costs would be several steps ahead of the evidence.

The Bank of England, Monetary Authority of Singapore and Bank of Thailand have completed a cross-border foreign-exchange settlement experiment designed to connect existing payment infrastructure with tokenised systems. The project might sound technical, but it addresses a familiar financial problem: two parties need to exchange different currencies without either being exposed to the risk that one side pays and the other does not.

In a recent development, the trial offers evidence that traditional central-bank settlement systems and distributed ledgers can be coordinated in a controlled setting. It does not mean a newly introduced public FX network has launched or that ordinary customers can use the prototype today.

In their joint announcement, the three central banks described work under the Meridian FX APAC initiative. The experiment tested how payment-versus-payment settlement could function across different systems, including a distributed-ledger environment and conventional real-time gross settlement arrangements. Payment-versus-payment means one currency leg is settled only if the other can be settled too.

According to recent reports, that principle is not new. What is new here is the attempt to apply it when separate technology stacks are involved. As the industry experiments with tokenised deposits and other digital representations of money, mismatches between systems can create delays or counterparty risks. A synchronised approach seeks to reduce that gap without requiring every participant to migrate onto the same ledger.

The trial also explored multilateral netting. Rather than having every participant settle each obligation individually, a system can calculate offsetting positions so that fewer funds need to move. In principle, this reduces liquidity demands and can make cross-border payment arrangements more efficient. In practice, netting depends on legal finality, settlement windows and clear responsibilities if a participant fails.

Partior developed the prototype used in the trial, according to reporting on the project. This was a test environment, not a new production service from the central banks. That is why central-bank experiments deserve attention even from readers who do not trade foreign exchange. European work on tokenisation standards covered by NewsBTC reflects a related concern: interoperable rules and infrastructure are needed if digital securities are to operate beyond isolated pilots.

The Bank of England has discussed a synchronisation interface with a target timeline in 2028. Multiple people confirmed Huang has been discussing the idea of returning with confidants, even though an independent probe by the board is examining allegations he was romantically involved with a Chinese spy who helped ferry chips to China.

The FT reported one ally saying that supporters have put together a “war room” to reinstate him. “Everybody that matters in tech outside the frontier labs loves Jensen,” the source noted.

A petition to reinstate Huang has garnered more than 100,000 signatures, including 5,600 current Nvidia employees, along with SpaceX boss Elon Musk and Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney.

The turmoil at Nvidia has weighed heavily on AI stocks and risk assets like cryptocurrency and the story still has a long way to run, with Congressional moves to investigate the issue and three bills being advanced to tighten AI chip export restrictions to China. According to the New York Time, intelligence officials reportedly briefed President Trump about the allegations Alice Huang was a Chinese spy a year ago, but he did not take any action.

Ethereum research group Ethlabs is withdrawing its Quick Slots proposal from the forthcoming Hegotá upgrade, and has urged core developers to urgently prepare the network for quantum attacks by 2027.

On Wednesday, the group outlined “pqai27,” a proposed roadmap that aims to protect Ethereum against threats from quantum computing and artificial intelligence.

At Devcon, researcher Justin Drake said he hopes to complete the transition in 2028 while the published roadmap still targets December 2029.

Industry observers note that index provider MSCI has confirmed Bitcoin treasury manufacturer Strategy will be removed from its global equity indexes, following months of debate over whether crypto treasury firms qualify as operating businesses. Japan’s Metaplanet and crypto treasury company Upexi are also marked for deletion, while Ether treasury firm Sharplink is on a watchlist. The changes take effect after market close on Nov. 30.

“Index inclusion meant ordinary passive investors, like someone holding a global index fund in their pension, were getting leveraged Bitcoin exposure they never chose. MSCI just fixed that,” Ryan Kirkley, CEO of Global Settlement Network, told Cointelegraph. Strategy fell 6.49% on Thursday and are down by more than one quarter over the past month.

US spot Bitcoin exchange-traded funds (ETFs) recorded $2.35 billion in net outflows over two consecutive weeks, as redemptions reached more than $1 billion each week.

According to Farside Investors data, spot Bitcoin ETFs shed $1.07 billion between from Monday to Friday, following $1.28 billion in outflows the previous week, the largest weekly redemptions since late June.

According to recent reports, friday marked the seventh consecutive trading session of net withdrawals, with about $1.71 billion redeemed since Nov. 5.

Sources indicate that at the end of the week, Bitcoin (BTC) is down 12.4% to trade at $65,116, Ethereum (ETH) is down 14.4% to trade at $1,822 and XRP (XRP) is down 13.3% to $0.96. The total market cap is at $2.2 trillion according to CoinMarketCap.

Among the biggest 100 cryptocurrencies, the top three altcoin winners of the week are Kite (KITE) with a 35.5% gain, Pieverse (PIEVERSE) on 33.8%, and Midnight (CRV) on 28.7%.

The top three altcoin losers of the week are Zcash (ZEC) which was down 25.4%, Uniswap (UNI) down 23.2% and Aero (AERO) down 23.1%.

According to recent reports, bitcoin Opportunity Fund co-founder Mark Moss states that with banks and ETFs widening access to Bitcoin he expects a fresh record high in 2027. Wall Street’s embrace of Bitcoin has created the “best buying opportunity ever,” he said.

Microsoft managed to restore Microsoft 365 services after a massive global outage disrupted Outlook, Teams and other applications for more than 24 hours, reiterating that the disruption was not caused by a cyberattack.

In a recent development, microsoft stated that the outage stemmed from a problem introduced during an earlier network capacity upgrade that emerged after a recent network change. “This was a technical problem not related to cyber or AI/agents,” the firm said.

MEGA, the organization behind Ethereum layer-2 network MegaETH, has reduced its workforce by 20% following months of restructuring as it expands into artificial intelligence products.

The layoffs come as MEGA shifts its focus toward developing products on the MegaETH network, including artificial intelligence services. The organization has committed $30 million to the initiative.

Metaplanet swung to a $170 million net loss in the first nine months of 2026, hit by a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings and a loss on the sale of 10,000 coins to demonstrate its ability to raise cash.

The Japanese firm, the world’s second-largest publicly traded corporate Bitcoin (BTC) holder, posted a net loss of 27.16 billion yen (about $170 million), compared with a profit of 13.53 billion yen ($84.6 million) in the same period last year. A 19.17 billion yen ($119.8 million) loss on the Bitcoin sale and an 8.04 billion yen ($50.3 million) loss from a decline in the value of its Bitcoin holdings outweighed gains in the operating business.

L1 blockchains Zilliqa, Gnosis and Ronin join the Ethereum ecosystem as the costs of going it alone grow, and the security and liquidity advantages become too hard to resist.

Ueno’s collapse exposed the fragility of digital banking in Paraguay, as customers scrambled for access to their money and stablecoins offered a lifeline.

It has been revealed that some Australian crypto investors are moving overseas to avoid the huge CGT increase from July 2027. But there are also less drastic ways you can pay less tax.

In a recent development, bitcoin investors may have witnessed the cryptocurrency’s final record-breaking rally, at least according to veteran trader Peter Brandt. The legendary chartist has sounded the alarm over a potentially massive bearish pattern emerging on Bitcoin’s weekly chart, warning that if the formation holds, the apex crypto’s October 2025 all-time high above $126,000 may never be surpassed in his lifetime. His alarming assessment comes as BTC reels from a brutal market downturn, adding fresh uncertainty to an already battered crypto market.

Peter Brandt has raised the possibility that Bitcoin may have already reached its ultimate price peak after spotting a potentially significant bearish formation on its weekly chart. In a November 15 post on X, the renowned chartist questioned whether BTC was developing a legitimate head-and-shoulders (H&S) top, a technical pattern often associated with a major trend reversal.

Brandt suggested that if the formation proves valid, he could construct a technical case that Bitcoin’s previous record high was its last, potentially remaining unbeaten for the rest of his lifetime. His warning is particularly striking given that Bitcoin reached a record of $126,080 in October 2025 before suffering a sharp correction.

It has been revealed that the H&S formation typically features three peaks, with the middle one (the head) rising above the two surrounding peaks (the shoulders). The pattern is considered bearish when the price breaks below the neckline, which connects the two troughs separating these peaks. Such a breakdown could signal weakening buying pressure and open the door to further losses. In Bitcoin’s case, the asset is approaching a crucial support zone between $60,000 and $65,000, which could serve as the neckline of the potential bearish formation.

However, Brandt has not confirmed that Bitcoin has completed this formation. His assessment remains conditional on whether the chart structure represents a legitimate bearish reversal, meaning traders will likely watch the potential neckline for signs of confirmation.

Bitcoin has extended its recent decline, with selling pressure intensifying on Nov. 13 as the flagship cryptocurrency dropped below the psychologically significant $70,000 threshold for the first time since August. The latest downturn has deepened its weekly losses to approximately 14.8%, highlighting the growing bearish sentiment weighing on the broader crypto market.

In a recent development, meanwhile, crypto analyst James Check has pointed to another worrying development, suggesting Bitcoin is experiencing its fourth capitulation event since reaching its all-time high. According to Check, daily realized losses have surged, doubling from about $420 million to more than $850 million in just 24 hours.

Check also offered a more optimistic perspective, arguing that Bitcoin has entered what he describes as a “deep value” zone. He noted that the cryptocurrency last traded in similar territory in February and late June this year, with the previous comparable occurrence dating back to the 2022 crypto bear market.

However, the pundit cautioned that entering this zone does not necessarily mean Bitcoin has reached its market bottom. Instead, he suggested that investors who begin gradually accumulating BTC at these levels could eventually benefit if historical patterns repeat, potentially turning the current market weakness into a long-term buying opportunity.

SpaceX made history with its latest Starship rocket launch, catching the spacecraft’s upper stage with its launch tower’s mechanical arms for the first time. Flight 15 lifted off from Starbase in Texas on Friday, November 13. The Ship returned on Saturday afternoon, about 22.5 hours after launch, and settled into the tower’s so-called chopsticks. SpaceX called the moment the holy grail of spaceflight. The mission fell short of a full double catch. The Super Heavy booster, which SpaceX has caught three times before, was diverted to a splashdown in the Gulf of Mexico after a low-fuel alarm. SpaceX looks to catch both stages on future operational flights to speed up inspection and reuse. Elon Musk is targeting 10,000 Starship introduces a year by 2030 to build a 100,000-satellite Starlink network and a planned one-million-satellite Starmind AI constellation. SpaceX has yet to reuse a Ship, though the one caught on Saturday could fly again.

💡 Key Takeaways

  • Decentralized derivatives exchange Lighter paused withdrawals and upcoming pool creation Monday after a security incident it linked to a leaked API key for a trader’s account.

Lighter has paused withdrawals after reporting a leaked trader API key, with Bubblemaps tracking $10.4 million withdrawn.

Decentralized derivatives exchange Lighter paused withdrawals and upcoming pool creation Monday after a security incident it linked to a leaked API key for a trader’s account.

Sources indicate that blockchain analytics firm Bubblemaps mentioned about $10.4 million in USDC had been withdrawn from the platform. It tracked funds being swapped into Ether (ETH) and Wrapped Monero XMR1, a token traded on Hyperliquid.

Lighter noted its protocol and smart contracts were unaffected. Lighter’s documentation indicates API keys can place trades, manage positions and transfer funds between accounts linked to the same blockchain wallet. Transfers to another wallet owner require an additional signature from the account owner’s wallet.

In a recent development, the exchange stated it activated Guardian mode as a precaution and that its security council would upgrade the contracts. It aimed to complete the work and restore withdrawals by the end of the day.

The security incident follows a string of high-profile cryptocurrency exploits this year, including the $6.3 billion Binance hack on Oct. 29, the industry’s largest to date.

Recent findings suggest that lighter and Bubblemaps identified wallet ‘0xb3f’ as the attacker’s address. Blockchain data platform Bitquery separately traced 10,393,057 USDC leaving Lighter’s Ethereum contract at 10:11 am UTC. It remarked most of those funds were converted into Ether through CoW Swap within minutes, followed by a series of 160 ETH transfers to wallets linked to XMR1 purchases on Hyperliquid.

Lighter’s update did not explain how the API key was exposed, what the contract upgrades would change or whether the affected trader would be reimbursed.

Cointelegraph contacted Lighter for comment but had not received a response by publication.

😱 Crypto Hits Extreme Fear as Bitcoin Plunges.

According to recent reports, the Crypto Fear and Greed Index printed 10 on Sunday. A month ago it read 63, which is Greed. A week ago it was 28. It has been sliding every day since, and 10 is about as low as that gauge goes.

It has been revealed that this weekend’s price action certainly was extremely fearful. Bitcoin touched roughly $62,000 before stabilizing in the mid-60s, down about a quarter from its early-October high and down something like 9% in three days. ETH fell under $1,850. Solana, XRP and dogecoin are all down more than 25% on the month. Bitcoin is now trading below its 200-week moving average, a level that has historically acted as the floor beneath every cycle, and it lost its 50-week average a week earlier.

It wasn’t just majors. Zcash fell to $800. Hype fell to $62. VVV went sub-$17. Nothing was spared.

The billion-dollar question of course—why is Bitcoin (and crypto) selling off so hard?

CZ addressed the question directly on Sunday, saying “No one knows for sure. Correlation does not prove causation.” But he did give potential reasons.

No one knows for sure. Correlation does not prove causation. Here are some potential reasons.

Money shifting to the Anthropic IPO: https://t.co/jYwVi4huAY.

ETF outflows: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.9 billion in outflows over seven trading… pic.twitter.com/XL2aB1ZL9W.

— CZ 🔶 BNB (@cz_binance) November 15, 2026.

The reasons he listed: money rotating into the Anthropic IPO, ETF outflows, a run of security incidents including the Binance hack itself plus drained iPhone-linked wallets, a Chrome exploit and a Microsoft outage, hot US inflation raising the odds of another Fed hike and strengthening the dollar, and political uncertainty after midterm results that point toward stricter crypto policy.

Those are all pretty valid. Some of those overhangs remove soon (Anthropic IPO), some will fade over time (political uncertainty), but the cyber attack threat will remain until Bitcoin and broader crypto can present a real solution. And if we are faced with a hiking cycle in 2027 due to inflation, that will certainly be a continued headwind.

So where does this leave us? Nvidia reports Tuesday with an interim CEO while its former one openly campaigns to return. The Fed meets December 9 with inflation running hot enough to put another hike in play. And Bitcoin is sitting under a technical level that has held for three cycles.

In a recent development, extreme fear has marked bottoms before. It has also marked the middle of declines. Now we wait for something other than sentiment to turn.

The Fed’s November report puts gross notional leverage at a Q1 2026 record in data starting in 2013. Losses or tighter funding could spread across markets.

According to recent reports, hedge-fund leverage reached a record in Q1 2026 on the gross notional measure, according to the Federal Reserve’s Nov. 13 Financial Stability Report. For Bitcoin, the risk is that losses or demands for additional collateral force leveraged investors to cut positions, spreading pressure across markets.

Industry observers note that the record covers the series beginning in 2013. The report also describes reduced Treasury basis-trade activity alongside record or near-record leverage across equity, relative-value and macro strategies. That broader assessment is why a smaller basis trade alone cannot establish that exposure to financial stress has eased. The comprehensive leverage observation is months old; the report generally reflects information available by Oct. 28.

Industry observers note that gross notional leverage compares total exposure, including derivatives, with net asset value. Balance-sheet leverage compares gross assets with net asset value. Neither is a measure of net directional exposure after offsetting positions, so a gross leverage record should not be read as an equally large one-way market bet.

The Treasury basis trade pairs bonds bought with repo borrowing, secured against the bonds, and a short Treasury futures position. Shrinking that trade can reduce one source of financing demand, while other leveraged strategies remain exposed to losses or tighter funding.

Dallas Fed researchers argued on Oct. 16 that modest basis-trade retrenchment could reflect changing relative returns and the appeal of alternatives such as swap-spread trades. Those trades combine Treasury and interest-rate-swap positions. That is a possible explanation for strategy substitution, not proof of how every fund repositioned.

It has been revealed that the financing mechanism matters more than the strategy label. The Fed’s stability report warns that material losses or worsening funding can generate spillovers, while higher volatility can constrain dealers’ willingness and ability to intermediate.

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin’s connection is conditional. IMF research published in January 2022 found stronger Bitcoin-equity co-movement and spillovers during 2020-21 than before the pandemic, with spillovers tending to intensify during market volatility. That historical evidence supports a route for cross-market stress; it does not establish today’s correlation or identify hedge funds right now selling Bitcoin.

Ledger Brings Clear Signing to Solana, Ending 'Blind' Signing for Jupiter Swaps

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://decrypt.co/383302/ledger-brings-clear-signing-to-solana-ending-blind-signing-for-jupiter-swaps

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ledger Brings Clear Signing to Solana, Ending 'Blind' Signing for Jupiter Swaps.
  • Ledger has brought clear signing to Solana, allowing people of its hardware wallets to read exactly what they are approving before they sign a transaction.
  • Sources indicate that "Until now, most Solana DeFi on a Ledger meant signing blind," the manufacturer tweeted on Monday.

Ledger Brings Clear Signing to Solana, Ending 'Blind' Signing for Jupiter Swaps.

Ledger has brought clear signing to Solana, allowing people of its hardware wallets to read exactly what they are approving before they sign a transaction.

Sources indicate that "Until now, most Solana DeFi on a Ledger meant signing blind," the manufacturer tweeted on Monday. Users can now verify a swap on decentralized exchange aggregator Jupiter "in plain words, showing what you send and what you get before you approve," it said.

Industry observers note that would you approve a swap you can’t read?Clear Signing is finally live on Solana. Until now, most Solana DeFi on a Ledger meant signing blind. Now you can verify a Jupiter swap, in plain words, showing what you send and what you get before you approve.

Clear Signing now covers… pic.twitter.com/BuW3m7y5GG.

In a recent development, blind signing, in which users approve transactions displayed as unreadable data, has long been a weak point for hardware wallet users, since it leaves them unable to spot a malicious request. Ian Rogers, Ledger's chief human agency officer, likened it to "signing a blank check" in a presentation at Solana's Breakpoint conference.

A Jupiter swap that previously meant scrolling through 13 hard-to-read screens on a Ledger device now takes three, showing what the user is giving, what they're getting and who they're dealing with, Rogers said. "It's a huge step for every Solana user," he added.

Clear signing now covers nine Solana apps and 18 of the 22 most common actions people take on the network, according to Ledger. It was built with the Solana Foundation and Anza, the developer of Solana's Agave validator client, with Jupiter and lending protocol Kamino as the first supported apps.

Rogers also pitched the tech giant's tools for AI agents. Ledger's approach is that an agent "never holds the keys; you do," he said, comparing it to a teenager who has to ask parents for the family car. The agent requests approval when it needs to move funds, and the user signs off on a Ledger device.

Because that means an agent has to stop and wait, Ledger last month rolled out Agent Intents, a single queue where approval requests collect so agents can keep working while owners approve them when convenient. It works with Pay.sh, a service that lets AI agents pay for APIs on Solana, Rogers noted.

Sources indicate that he also indicated off Ledger Atom, the touchscreen device based on Android's open-source code that Ledger unveiled last month. When it's time to sign, the device switches its screen to Ledger's secure chip, so secrets stay hidden from Android, Rogers said. Atom will be the first hardware beyond the Solana Seeker phone to carry the Seeker platform, bringing its more than 1,500 apps to the device, he added.

Ledger has previously teamed up with MoonPay on tools to let customers control AI agents' crypto spending with its hardware wallets.

The launch comes weeks after Ledger investigated a suspected $87 million drain of user funds, which it later noted was tied in all confirmed cases to a reseller, Cryptobilis.

#622. Banks are banning AI agents over security... and competition concerns

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5 min read (1037 words)

Banks are banning AI agents over security... and competition concerns

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read | Sumber: https://cointelegraph.com/magazine/banks-are-banning-ai-agents-over-security-and-competition-concerns?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound

💡 Key Takeaways
  • AI agents are set to automate everyday banking tasks — but banks aren’t ready to give up control of the customer relationship just yet.
  • Banks in the United Kingdom have drawn a line over how much access artificial intelligence should have to their customers’ money.
  • Four banks, including HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest and Nationwide, have all moved to block or restrict third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts, especially where they can make transactions without customer involvement.

AI agents are set to automate everyday banking tasks — but banks aren’t ready to give up control of the customer relationship just yet.

Banks in the United Kingdom have drawn a line over how much access artificial intelligence should have to their customers’ money.

Four banks, including HSBC, Barclays, Lloyds, NatWest and Nationwide, have all moved to block or restrict third-party AI agents from accessing customer accounts, especially where they can make transactions without customer involvement.

There’s no evidence yet of AI agents accessing UK bank accounts just yet, but large lenders are worried about what happens if an automated system mismanages customers’ money — and who would be on the hook.

The banks might have other, unspoken concerns too.

Edgars Nemše, chief executive of GenLayer Foundation, an AI-focused blockchain infrastructure project, indicates routine banking tasks like paying bills, moving money and finding better rates could all be handed to agents.

Unfortunately for banks, this means agents would be able to seamlessly find customers a better deal elsewhere as soon as it’s published on the web.

“For plain accounts, that removes the switching costs and makes the space even more competitive,” Nemše tells Magazine.

That scenario could threaten more than just customer loyalty. In September, Apollo chief economist Torsten Slok warned about a possible “agentic bank run.”.

It has been revealed that if swarms of agents start moving household cash from low-yield checking accounts to alternatives offering higher returns en masse, that would drain banks of the low-cost funding they rely on to make loans. And the speed and scale “would be a problem for the entire financial system.”.

Related: Coinbase CEO touts agentic finance as Base tops 100M AI payments.

Industry observers note that JPMorgan Chase chief executive Jamie Dimon has also warned against allowing external agents unrestricted access to bank accounts. “You don’t want rogue agents,” he mentioned on an October earnings call.

Is an agentic bank run coming? Source: Apollo.

Regardless of short-term moves to hold back the tide, AI agents look more and more likely to revolutionize banking within a few years.

Neeraj Makin, group head of strategy analytics at Emirates NBD, predicts agents will usher in a newly introduced era of around-the-clock banking and near-instant payments as normal by 2036.

“Forget about waiting for a payment for 24 hours or inter-country payments taking three days… all of that will be in seconds, atomic,” he says, with AI agents taking over most financial decisions.

Ferdinand Dabitz, chief executive of Augustus, an AI-native banking and payments company, sees a similar shift in how customers interact with financial institutions.

“Every consumer will have 10s and every business will have 100s of agents talking to their bank,” Dabitz indicates.

A human interface will still remain vital for managing those agents and providing a layer of trust, “especially in commercial banking,” he claims.

Related: Agents can trade 24/7 — but Yat Siu warns you could lose access at any time.

Emirates NBD’s developer experience team argued in July that financial institutions should build their own frameworks for agentic AI, rather than allowing individual teams to develop agents without common controls.

Its Leap framework is designed to govern how agents authenticate with core banking systems, access sensitive data and carry out actions, with audit trails, monitoring and human oversight built in.

Emirates NBD says banks should build their own agentic frameworks. Source: Emirates NBD.

However there are still major concerns around the reliability of agents to make major financial decisions on their own.

A recent Bank of England and FCA survey found that while 80% of responding firms had deployed AI agents, just 2% used agents with broad autonomy, identifying data security, third-party dependencies and risks like hallucinations among their biggest concerns.

The AI takeover likely won’t happen overnight; “it will come in steps,” Nemše states.

Recent findings suggest that “Today I use an agent to review my own and my company’s finances every month and queue the payments, and I approve them. The next step is the natural one: once you trust it, you let it spend small amounts without asking.”.

Routine bills, subscriptions and the agent’s own running costs would be among the first tasks to become autonomous, he says.

Dabitz indicates corporate treasury management could be an area delegated to agents, but says banks will need to be involved in developing these early applications.

While consumers may enjoy the upside of automating their finances, who’s on the hook when an agent makes a mistake?

Industry observers note that nemše states banks need to offer “delegated access as a normal feature” to avoid customers sharing logins with agents. Customers could set permissions and spending limits, and agents could make low-value transactions independently while requiring approval for larger amounts.

It has been revealed that but existing dispute processes may struggle if agents begin making thousands of transactions on behalf of each customer. “Even a small share going wrong is a lot of disputes,” he says. “The processes for handling them were built for people making a few payments a week. That part still has to be built.”.

Recent findings suggest that the US Office of the Comptroller of the Currency issued a supervisory framework for banks’ use of what it calls “super intelligence,” including agentic systems, on Nov. 4.

Sources indicate that OCC’s Super Intelligence: Supervisory Framework. Source: OCC.

Industry observers note that the framework is meant to help bank examiners assess how institutions use the technology, and does not introduce fresh binding requirements for banks. Scrutiny should reflect the potential consequences of an agent’s actions, its level of autonomy and the degree of human oversight.

So an AI system helping a bank employee draft a report would present a different risk from one authorized to move customer funds without approval, and the banks that get that balance right are likely to come out on top.

Sweden’s H100 Taps Coinbase Prime and Deribit for Its 3,506 Bitcoin Treasury as It Courts Family Offices

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Swedish bitcoin treasury tech giant H100 Group noted Monday it will use Coinbase Prime and the Deribit derivatives exchange for custody, trading and financing of its roughly 3,506 BTC, a move it states supports both its bitcoin-per-share goal and a push to serve wealthy investors.
  • According to recent reports, H100, which trades on Stockholm’s NGM Nordic SME under the ticker H100, revealed the partnership in a release Monday morning.
  • It has been revealed that H100 valued its holdings at about SEK 2.3 billion, or $226 million, based on a bitcoin price of $64,600 on Nov.

Swedish bitcoin treasury tech giant H100 Group noted Monday it will use Coinbase Prime and the Deribit derivatives exchange for custody, trading and financing of its roughly 3,506 BTC, a move it states supports both its bitcoin-per-share goal and a push to serve wealthy investors.

According to recent reports, H100, which trades on Stockholm’s NGM Nordic SME under the ticker H100, revealed the partnership in a release Monday morning. The company and its subsidiaries will use Coinbase and Deribit, which Coinbase owns, for custody, trading and financing, it mentioned.

It has been revealed that H100 valued its holdings at about SEK 2.3 billion, or $226 million, based on a bitcoin price of $64,600 on Nov. 15. It also has about SEK 219 million ($22 million) in outstanding convertible loans that carry 0% interest, mature on July 9, 2030, and equal less than 10% of the stated value of its bitcoin.

The release did not disclose fees, collateral terms or borrowing limits. It also didn’t say whether H100 has drawn on any financing, how much of its bitcoin will sit with Coinbase, or whether it is moving coins from another custodian.

H100 described Coinbase’s offering as the crypto version of a bank’s prime brokerage desk, bringing custody, financing and trade execution under one roof.

The trading itself will be run in-house. PDI AS, a wholly owned trading and technology unit, builds the software and trading systems used to manage H100’s bitcoin, and the organization said those tools operate “with protecting H100’s Bitcoin holdings as the first priority.”.

“This partnership gives H100 stronger tools for our own balance sheet, and we use them on our own Bitcoin first,” Executive Chairman Sander Andersen mentioned. “Bitcoin per share remains the measure we run the Manufacturer by, and these tools are there to help us deliver on it, not to add risk.”.

Andersen added that this is “the first of several” partnerships, “and the next is already under way.” He did not name the next partner.

Lauren Abendschein, head of institutional sales at Coinbase, said bitcoin treasury companies “have grown into an established part of our institutional client base,” and that their priorities are custody, “liquidity when the market moves, and financing against the same balance sheet.”.

Sources indicate that the second goal is bigger. H100 said it wants to become what majority shareholder Geir Harald Hansen, in a June 11 letter to shareholders, called “a leading European alternative and digital asset manager.” It will start with family offices and high-net-worth individuals looking for a partner on bitcoin investments and financing, and said it will share details as products launch.

H100 began as a health-tech tech giant before adopting a bitcoin treasury strategy in 2025. It agreed in January to buy Swiss treasury firm Future Holdings and closed that deal in February.

Its holdings tripled in August. After shareholders approved the acquisition of two Norwegian holding companies in June, H100 closed the deal on Aug. 10, adding 2,455.37 BTC and lifting its total to 3,506.4 BTC, according to its second-quarter report.

Recent findings suggest that H100 paid for that deal with 790.5 million latest shares. That took its share count to about 1.13 billion and left Hansen with about 69.2% of the company. Eirik Grøttum, who has worked with Hansen for years, became H100’s CEO the next day.

Grøttum wrote in the same report that simply raising money to buy bitcoin “is unlikely to be sufficient on its own” for treasury companies, adding that “BTC should be the hurdle rate, not the business model.”.

According to recent reports, the announcement comes as bitcoin trades near $64,000 after a weekend slide to its lowest level since July, and treasury companies face pressure to show they can grow their bitcoin per share without issuing too much stock. H100 has not said whether it plans to buy more bitcoin.
