Weak growth gives the Bank of Japan reason to pause, but higher borrowing costs and a stronger yen can still squeeze leveraged Bitcoin positions.

Japan's economy stalled in the third quarter, strengthening the case for caution over further Bank of Japan rate increases. But weaker growth does not automatically make yen funding cheaper for leveraged Bitcoin positions or protect them from a stronger Japanese currency.

Japan's Cabinet Office reported in its first estimate on Nov. 16 that real GDP fell 0.1% at an annualized rate in July–September. The quarterly decline rounded to -0.0%, while private consumption fell 0.3% from the previous quarter. The annualized figure describes the quarterly pace expressed over a year, not a year-over-year fall.

The composition was mixed: domestic demand added 0.6 percentage point to quarterly growth, while net exports subtracted 0.6 point.

Sources indicate that the BOJ maintained its overnight-rate target around 1.25% on Oct. 30. That remains the policy backdrop to today's GDP release.

BOJ board member Toichiro Asada had already argued in a Nov. 12 speech that consumption lacked strong growth momentum and that the pace of further hikes deserved care. His personal caution coexists with the Bank's conditional stance of further rate increases as activity, prices and financial conditions develop, alongside upside inflation risks.

There is pressure in the other direction, too. In a Nov. 16 speech, board member Hajime Takata argued for nimbler tightening and described his October proposal for a 1.5% rate as his personal view. The Board had rejected that proposal.

Weak consumption strengthens the argument for patience, but inflation risk keeps further tightening in the policy debate. The GDP number alone cannot settle that tension.

German Lawmakers Back Customs Powers to Seize Crypto of 'Unclear Origin'

💡 Key Takeaways
  • German Lawmakers Back Customs Powers to Seize Crypto of 'Unclear Origin'.
  • Germany's parliament has approved sweeping new powers for the country's customs agency, allowing it to seize assets, including crypto, whose lawful origin is in doubt, even when no criminal investigation is underway.
  • The Bundestag passed the Customs Financial Justice Act, or Zollfinanzgerechtigkeitsgesetz, on Thursday, November 12, the German government mentioned.

German Lawmakers Back Customs Powers to Seize Crypto of 'Unclear Origin'.

Germany's parliament has approved sweeping new powers for the country's customs agency, allowing it to seize assets, including crypto, whose lawful origin is in doubt, even when no criminal investigation is underway.

The Bundestag passed the Customs Financial Justice Act, or Zollfinanzgerechtigkeitsgesetz, on Thursday, November 12, the German government mentioned. Under the law, customs can more easily seize assets where there are "justified doubts" about their lawful origin, an instrument the government describes as a "suspicious wealth order." Customs will also be able to better monitor digital cross-border payment routes and secure crypto assets.

"With this, we are sending a clear signal to criminals: we are getting tougher," German Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil said, according to the government.

Recent findings suggest that the powers apply to "significant" assets, which typically means those worth more than €100,000, according to the government's bill. Because owners of such assets are usually able to explain where they came from, while the state struggles to prove an illegal origin, the government argued that it is reasonable to ask owners to disclose that information. "Almost every law-abiding citizen will be able to explain where these assets came from," the bill's explanatory notes say, as summarized by the Bundestag's news service.

Klingbeil has noted customs could hold assets for up to 180 days without a conviction, during which owners would have to show they were obtained legally. "The Porsche and the Rolex are then gone for now," he said, according to the Berliner Zeitung. Any permanent confiscation would require a court ruling. Following an amendment by the governing coalition, that decision will be made by a panel of finance court judges rather than a single judge.

Industry observers note that the law also reorganizes Germany's customs administration, strengthens its Financial Intelligence Unit and gives customs a legal basis to use technologies such as artificial intelligence. It forms part of an action proposal against organized crime that the government adopted on February 25, 2026.

Germany has seized large amounts of crypto before, and has been quick to sell it. In 2024, authorities in the state of Saxony began selling the nearly 50,000 BTC they had seized from operators of the movie piracy website Movie2K, moving hundreds of millions of dollars' worth at a time as the sell-off continued. Blockchain analytics firm Arkham later said authorities had failed to seize a further 45,000 BTC linked to the site. The fresh law would give customs a way to seize crypto of unclear origin without first having to tie it to a specific crime.

According to recent reports, german authorities have also gone after laundering infrastructure. Last year, they joined Swiss police in shutting down Cryptomixer, a mixing service that had laundered more than $1.4 billion in Bitcoin since 2016. Separately, the finance ministry has drafted a 25% tax on crypto gains from 2027.

Recent findings suggest that the Bundestag's finance committee backed the bill on Wednesday with votes from the governing CDU/CSU and SPD, as well as the far-right AfD. The Left Party voted against, and the Greens abstained.

It has been revealed that the Greens said Germany's money laundering problem is estimated at €100 billion, and that the government's expectation of only €308 million in additional revenue showed the gap between its ambitions and the law. The Left Party said the confiscation process was "built for the cash courier, not the banker.".

The law still needs to pass the Bundesrat, the upper house of parliament that represents Germany's states.

Strategy bought 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 million and spent $228.1 million repurchasing STRC preferred shares, largely funded by fresh common stock sales.

Michael Saylor’s Strategy bought 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 million last week while spending nearly seven times as much repurchasing STRC preferred shares.

The company purchased the Bitcoin (BTC) at an average price of $68,887 between Monday and Sunday, bringing its holdings to 850,849 BTC, according to a Monday filing with the US Securities and Exchange Commission.

The tech giant repurchased 2.28 million STRC shares during the week. STRC is Strategy’s variable-rate preferred stock, which pays regular dividends to shareholders.

Recent findings suggest that strategy reported a $4.75 billion US dollar reserve after using $18.9 million to pay preferred stock dividends. Its separate cash balance stood at $151.2 million as of Sunday.

The tech giant also maintained STRC’s annual dividend rate at 12% for December, saying it intends to keep the rate steady until the shares demonstrate sustained trading near $100.

Strategy spent $188.3 million repurchasing STRC shares and $81.9 million buying Bitcoin the previous week.

Strategy’s MSTR stock fell 8.45% to $102.2 in Monday’s premarket trading, while STRC declined 0.78% to $99.1, according to Yahoo Finance. The losses followed MSCI’s confirmation last week that it would remove Strategy from its global equity indexes after the Nov. 30 market close.

Industry observers note that “Strive acquired 251 $BTC for $17.5M at an average cost of $69,853 per bitcoin, bringing total holdings to ₿43,404,” Cole wrote. Vitalik Buterin Now ‘a Total Bull’ on leanPCS as Fast Track to Quantum-Safe Ethereum.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has thrown his weight behind a proposal he says could make the network quantum-safe much faster than expected.

"Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull," Buterin tweeted on Monday, in a lengthy explainer on how Ethereum could handle the much larger signatures and proofs that quantum-resistant cryptography requires.

Industry observers note that over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.

At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data….

— vitalik.eth (@VitalikButerin) November 16, 2026.

In short, leanPCS is a proposed way for Ethereum to bundle many large, quantum-safe signatures and proofs into a single compact proof, so that the full data never has to be stored onchain. It is built on polynomial commitment schemes, or PCS, the core mathematical building block of STARK proofs.

In a recent development, quantum computers are expected to eventually break the elliptic curve cryptography that secures Ethereum and Bitcoin accounts today. The quantum-safe replacements are far bulkier: Buterin noted signatures would grow from 65 bytes to between 1 and 6 kilobytes, while zero-knowledge proofs would balloon from a few hundred bytes to around 128 kilobytes. "This is unsustainable to put on chain," he wrote.

Buterin's answer is EIP-8288, a draft proposal he co-authored with developer Thomas Coratger in June, which would aggregate those signatures and proofs before they ever reach a block.

Under the design, owners publish their signatures or proofs, and network nodes repeatedly bundle everything they have seen into a single STARK, a type of zero-knowledge proof, that attests the underlying data is valid. These aggregate proofs are themselves combined until a single "master proof" verifies everything in a block. Only short claims, rather than the full signatures or proofs, would need to be stored onchain.

He laid out three ways to build it, depending on what users submit. The simplest, leanSPHINCS, would support a single type of quantum-safe, hash-based signature, costing users only a small amount of gas per signature, but it couldn't do anything else.

According to recent reports, at the other end, leanSTARK would be fully general, allowing any signature scheme, privacy protocols or hidden multisig logic. But Ethereum would first have to agree on a programming language for owners' programs, which Buterin called "the first big case of 'Ethereum moving beyond the EVM,'" and which is likely to take time.

Industry observers note that buterin's preferred option, leanPCS, offers a third route. It would offer the same generality as leanSTARK but "could potentially be implemented very quickly," he stated, because far fewer design choices are needed, and leanSTARK could then be added later.

"So there is a route to getting 'the cryptographic proof singularity' much faster than any of us expected," Buterin wrote, "and that route runs through 8288 with leanPCS.".

Buterin linked to SPHINCS-, a family of hash-based signature schemes optimized for Ethereum, which was published on the Ethereum Research forum in June with input from Buterin and Ethereum Foundation cryptographers. The post shows that a standards-aligned quantum-safe signature can already be verified on Ethereum for about 150,000 gas, without any protocol change, compared with about 3,000 gas for an ECDSA signature today, according to an earlier Buterin estimate.

Under protocol-level aggregation, a future "leanSPHINCS" verification would cost about 3,000 gas, according to the post.

Quantum resistance has become a top priority for Ethereum. The Ethereum Foundation formed a dedicated post-quantum team in January, and Buterin has since stated the network is betting its future on quantum security and privacy. Developers have also proposed overhauling the staking deposit contract to support post-quantum validator keys, and Buterin has pushed a proposal to cut the cost of quantum-safe privacy.

Three messages impersonated Epoch employees by name and job title, while 27 others claimed to come from engineers or auditors.

An investigation also found more than 200 attempts to access actual evaluation logs, along with efforts to discover administrative credentials and hidden endpoints.

Epoch said the agents failed to obtain private or confidential information, but the incident exposed how autonomous systems could pursue unauthorized actions while attempting to complete assigned objectives.

October experiments described by Epoch AI and Trajectory Labs changed their routing and consent arrangements.

Epoch notes the first live-site test happened without approval or prior notice and included attempted exploits and impersonation.

Trajectory states internet-connected agents bypassed routing to a local copy and reached the live site again.

Live-site access and consent are separate questions. Epoch says no private or confidential information was accessed.

The unauthorized activity continued to expose weaknesses in Trajectory's testing environment after researchers attempted to separate the agents from Epoch's real infrastructure.

After the initial incident, Trajectory set up a local copy of Epoch's website and introduced a DNS redirect intended to prevent agents from accessing the live service.

Sources indicate that trajectory suspended all misalignment testing on Nov. 2 and introduced new requirements for risk assessments, third-party consent, monitoring and emergency shutdown mechanisms.

Sources indicate that digital assets have changed more than the way money moves. They have also changed what consumers expect from digital products. A crypto holder can move between exchanges, wallets, and decentralized applications without treating every activity as a completely separate financial relationship. That expectation is increasingly influencing online gaming.

In a recent development, for many players, the traditional model of maintaining one account for sports betting, another for slots, and a third for live casino games feels unnecessarily fragmented. A unified platform offers a simpler alternative: one account, one balance, and a consistent payment experience across several forms of entertainment.

The appeal is particularly relevant to crypto-aware audiences in Canada. These users are already familiar with digital wallets, network confirmations, and assets that can move across borders and applications. When they enter an online gaming environment, they often expect the same degree of continuity.

Industry observers note that the strongest argument for a unified platform is practical rather than promotional. Separate gaming accounts create separate balances, deposit histories, and withdrawal processes. Players may need to move funds repeatedly, learn different interfaces, and review different sets of account information.

A shared account reduces those steps. Funds deposited for a weekend sporting event may remain available for a slot session or a live-dealer table without requiring another external transfer. The player still decides how and when the balance is used, but the platform does not force a new payment journey for every product category.

It has been revealed that this model can be especially useful when crypto is involved. Blockchain transfers are not the same as moving credits between sections of a website. Every external transaction may involve a network selection, a destination address, a fee, and a confirmation period. Keeping more activity within one verified account can reduce the number of blockchain transactions a player needs to initiate.

A large game or market catalogue has value, but variety alone does not create a coherent experience. A genuinely unified platform also needs consistent navigation, account controls and transaction information.

Players should be able to identify their available balance, review deposits and withdrawals, and reach account settings without relearning the interface each time they move from sportsbook to casino. Mobile behaviour matters as well. A platform that works smoothly on desktop but becomes difficult to navigate on a phone does not deliver a truly unified experience.

The same principle applies to support and identity checks. A single account can allow the platform to maintain one verified customer profile instead of asking the user to repeat the same process for each product. It can also provide one place for limits, security settings and support history.

According to recent reports, the growth of combined platforms does not mean that sports betting, slots and live casino are becoming identical. Each product has a different rhythm.

In a recent development, sports betting is event-driven. Activity often rises around major matches, tournaments and seasonal calendars. Slots and live casino games are generally available continuously. A unified platform allows those patterns to coexist without forcing players to maintain separate accounts.

In a recent development, that flexibility can also make the account more useful between major sporting events. A player who primarily follows football, hockey, or basketball may still prefer access to other entertainment from the same balance. Conversely, a casino-focused user may value the option to follow a major match without opening a latest account elsewhere.

The commercial trend is therefore less about persuading every player to use every product and more about removing barriers when interests overlap.

According to recent reports, crypto payments can support a unified experience, but the presence of a digital asset logo does not guarantee a good payment journey. Players still need clear information about supported assets and networks, minimum amounts, processing steps, and withdrawal requirements.

Sources indicate that network compatibility is particularly vital. The same asset may exist on several blockchains, and sending it through an unsupported network can lead to a failed or difficult recovery process. A well-designed deposit page should make the correct network and address clear before funds are sent.

Transaction visibility also matters. Blockchain explorers can show whether a transfer has been broadcast and confirmed, while the gaming account should show when the deposit has been credited. These are related but distinct stages. Clear status information reduces uncertainty.

Betplay illustrates the unified-platform model by bringing sportsbook, slots, and live casino products under one brand and account experience. Its relevance to a crypto publication comes from that combination: the payment layer is connected to several entertainment categories rather than a single-purpose casino product.

The practical value is continuity. A player can explore different parts of the platform without creating a new account or starting a separate balance for every vertical. The brand therefore fits a broader shift in digital entertainment toward consolidated accounts and fewer payment handoffs.

That does not remove the need for normal due diligence. Players should review the assets and networks at the moment supported, transaction instructions, terms, account limits, and withdrawal requirements before depositing. Product availability can also vary by location.

According to recent reports, any discussion of online gaming in Canada requires a regulatory qualification. Gambling is regulated at the provincial level, and the framework is not identical across the country. Ontario introduced a competitive regulated internet gaming market in April 2022, overseen by the Alcohol and Gaming Commission of Ontario and iGaming Ontario. Other provinces use different models and rules.

As a result, Canadian users should confirm that a platform is available where they live and that its use complies with applicable provincial requirements. They should also meet the legal gambling age in their province.

According to recent reports, unified crypto gaming platforms reflect a wider digital trend. Users increasingly expect one identity, one payment layer and a consistent interface across related services. In online gaming, that can mean moving between sportsbook, slots and live casino without repeating the same financial and account-management steps.

In a recent development, the model is not valuable simply because it places several products on one website. Its real value comes from reducing friction while keeping balances, transaction information and account controls understandable.

For crypto-aware audiences, that combination is likely to remain compelling: choice across products, continuity across sessions and fewer unnecessary transfers between platforms.

Elon Musk Joins 160,000 Backing Petition to Bring Jensen Huang Back to Nvidia.

Elon Musk has thrown his support behind a campaign to reinstate Jensen Huang as Nvidia's CEO, as the ousted chipmaker co-founder reportedly weighs a comeback just days after resigning.

Recent findings suggest that "A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I'm signing it too," the Tesla and SpaceX CEO tweeted on Friday. Musk had previously said it would be "an honor" to hire Huang.

A petition is underway to reinstate Jensen and I’m signing it too.

— Elon Musk (@elonmusk) November 13, 2026.

The "Stand with Jensen" open letter calls on Nvidia's board to bring Huang back while an independent investigation establishes the facts. It has drawn more than 160,000 signatures, including Epic Games CEO Tim Sweeney and Y Combinator CEO Garry Tan, CNBC reported, though the site notes that signatories' affiliations are self-reported and unverified. More than 7,500 signatories identified themselves as Nvidia employees, The Guardian reported, a figure it said was equivalent to 18% of the tech giant's workforce.

The campaign follows internal calls from Nvidia staff for Huang's return.

According to recent reports, huang has discussed the possibility of returning with confidants, the Financial Times reported, citing multiple people familiar with the matter. One ally told the newspaper they were assembling a "war room" of Silicon Valley executives to lobby for his reinstatement and would seek support from the White House, adding that the effort had Huang's backing.

Even supporters acknowledged the obstacles. "Having an affair with a subordinate is a fireable offence," one person involved in the effort told the FT.

Two major Nvidia shareholders, Altimeter Capital's Brad Gerstner and Atreides Management's Gavin Baker, urged the board in an open letter on Friday to leave "all options on the table, including the potential return of Jensen Huang.".

Huang resigned as Nvidia's president, CEO and board member on Thursday, capping a week of reports of affairs with Alice Huang, a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom U.S. officials suspect of spying for China, and with an Nvidia executive who reported to him. Chief financial officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO.

Recent findings suggest that the campaign faces resistance in Washington. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent stated on Sunday that Nvidia should look outside the company for its next CEO. "They need a dramatic shake-up," he told Fox News.

Bessent remarked on Sunday Morning Futures that questions over Nvidia's compliance with U.S. export restrictions were the bigger glitch, and that the organization should be judged on whether it had "intentionally ignored the warning signs" of shell companies in Singapore. He said he wanted answers "in the next 10 days from the board and from the outside counsel." Huang also faces congressional inquiries into Nvidia's chip exports to China, as well as a proposed shareholder class action.

Nvidia's board has approached Arm CEO Rene Haas as a potential successor, the FT has reported. "We are in the process of selecting a search firm for the NVIDIA CEO role. We have not formally engaged any potential candidates," an Nvidia spokesperson told CNBC.

Industry observers note that analysts are divided on Huang's chances. "We see no chance Jensen comes back to Nvidia as CEO," Dan Ives of Yorkville Ives & Co. mentioned in a note cited by CNBC, while Seaport Research Partners' Jay Goldberg said Huang could stage "a second act" if he gets through his legal troubles. Former White House communications director Anthony Scaramucci was blunter: "The FBI doesn't take petitions," he tweeted.

Nvidia reports quarterly earnings on Tuesday, the first under Kress.

HKMA and Swift will explore linking Project Ensemble with Swift’s ledger for cross-border payments using tokenized deposits in multiple currencies.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority (HKMA) and Swift will explore connecting their payment infrastructure to support cross-border transfers using tokenized bank deposits, the authority stated Monday.

According to recent reports, the work will examine links between Swift’s blockchain-based ledger and the settlement infrastructure of Project Ensemble. Participating banks include Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered Bank (Hong Kong) and HSBC, according to the announcement.

Tokenized deposits are bank balances represented on a blockchain. They remain claims on the issuing commercial bank, unlike central bank digital currencies, which are claims on a central bank. The proposed Swift connection would explore how separate payment systems could work together across borders in multiple currencies.

Recent findings suggest that the collaboration follows a Nov. 2 upgrade to EnsembleTX, the pilot phase of Project Ensemble, enabling banks to settle tokenized deposit transactions around the clock using tokenized central bank money. The pilot debuted in November 2025 and initially relied on Hong Kong’s dollar-denominated real-time gross settlement system.

In July, Swift said its blockchain-based ledger was ready for initial use and that it was preparing to pilot tokenized cross-border payments with 17 major banks, including Citi, DBS and HSBC.

#651. Singapore, Germany test cross-border FX settlement with CBDCs

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 1 min read (296 words)

Singapore, Germany test cross-border FX settlement with CBDCs

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 1 min read | Sumber: https://cointelegraph.com/news/singapore-german-central-banks-settlement-cbdcs?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Project Simbolon aims to reduce the cost and time of cross-border settlement and promote common standards for payments and FX.
  • The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Deutsche Bundesbank used wholesale central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to test settlement of euro–Singapore dollar trades across their separate digital asset test environments.
  • In a recent development, as part of Project Simbolon, the two central banks used payment-versus-payment settlement, meaning the final transfers of each currency depended on the final transfer of the other, MAS said in a Monday press release.

Project Simbolon aims to reduce the cost and time of cross-border settlement and promote common standards for payments and FX.

The Monetary Authority of Singapore (MAS) and the Deutsche Bundesbank used wholesale central bank digital currencies (CBDCs) to test settlement of euro–Singapore dollar trades across their separate digital asset test environments.

In a recent development, as part of Project Simbolon, the two central banks used payment-versus-payment settlement, meaning the final transfers of each currency depended on the final transfer of the other, MAS said in a Monday press release. Zero-knowledge proofs allowed each system to verify whether settlement conditions were met without directly integrating the central bank ledgers.

It has been revealed that the project aims to make cross-border transfers between Singapore and Germany faster and cheaper. It also aims to promote common standards for cross-border payments, foreign exchange and securities transactions tied to tokenized assets.

The test was the first milestone under a November 2025 memorandum of understanding between the two central banks on tokenization and cross-border settlement. It also advances broader efforts to make tokenized financial markets more efficient under Project Guardian, a tokenization initiative MAS launched in May 2022.

“Project Simbolon paves the way for eliminating settlement risk in global foreign exchange transactions,” said Sabine Mauderer, first deputy governor of the Bundesbank.

In September, the Eurosystem launched Pontes, a system that lets financial institutions settle wholesale tokenized asset transactions in central bank money.

US authorities say they have obtained court approval to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion in digital assets linked to the major October attack on Binance. The action is part of a wider effort to trace and freeze funds attributed to North Korean hackers, and it comes alongside a separate disruption of infrastructure allegedly used to deceive victims through fake video calls.

The distinction between freezing assets, receiving permission to seize them and actually returning money to victims is crucial. A large enforcement announcement should not be presented as evidence that all the stolen cryptocurrency has already been recovered.

The Block reported on the Department of Justice announcement that court approval had been secured to seize or restrain more than $1.2 billion tied to the October 29 Binance breach. US authorities have attributed the attack to North Korean operators associated with the TraderTraitor group, with the initial theft described as exceeding $6 billion.

Industry observers note that the department mentioned more than $2.7 billion had been frozen through the combined efforts of authorities and private-sector companies. A frozen balance is not the same as funds delivered back to an exchange or its customers. Investigators must still establish ownership, navigate legal processes and prevent assets from being moved through other services or jurisdictions.

Public blockchain records can show a trail of transfers from one address to another. That visibility can be valuable when investigators identify wallets and work with trading platforms or other service providers to block proceeds. But hackers can use bridges, mixers and chains with different transaction models to complicate tracing. Technical identification also has to be connected to a legal basis for seizure.

Sources indicate that another challenge is timing. An asset may be visible on-chain but move before a service can act, or it may already have been exchanged into another token. That is why seizure orders, freezes and completed recoveries need to be reported separately. The value of assets at the time of the theft can also differ from what can be recovered months later.

It has been revealed that the DOJ also described action against a scheme referred to as FaceStealer, which allegedly used manipulated or impersonated video calls to compromise victims. Reporting said the operation had been associated with more than $400 million in theft over an 18-month period. Although both announcements involve North Korean cyber activity, they are distinct investigations and should not be merged into a single total of stolen funds.

The underlying lesson is operational. Attackers are increasingly interested in persuading a person to compromise their own device or sign an unsafe transaction, not merely in exploiting smart-contract code. Wallet permissions, staff identity verification and secure approval procedures can therefore matter as much as blockchain analytics after the fact.

Binance has stated it arranged coverage for affected customer assets, according to the reporting, but that statement should be assessed separately from the government's legal recovery process. Customers should rely on official exchange communications for account-specific details, and be cautious of unsolicited messages offering compensation or recovery services. Such approaches can become a second opportunity for fraud.

Recent findings suggest that the broader industry is paying attention to withdrawal approval controls and custody practices. NewsBTC's coverage of business Bitcoin accounts with withdrawal approvals and institutional interest in DeFi infrastructure highlight parts of that security conversation. The DOJ action is meaningful, but a final recovery figure will only be clear as investigations and legal proceedings progress.

Recent findings suggest that solana has officially removed the "beta" tag from its mainnet's name and introduced the Solana 1.0 standard. The switch was announced on Nov. 16 at the Breakpoint conference in London.

"Solana 1.0 marks the network's graduation from 'mainnet beta' to 'mainnet,' retiring the beta designation it has carried since launch," the Solana Foundation said.

Solana rolled out on March 16, 2020, and the network had been working under the "mainnet-beta" label for six years and eight months. According to the foundation, the label "never evolved to signal its production status.".

Recent findings suggest that the Solana Foundation coordinated the rollout with the Anza and Firedancer teams. Co-founder Anatoly Yakovenko replied to the announcement on X with three exploding-head emojis.

Sources indicate that "For consumers, this is the same network, nothing changes. Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same," the foundation wrote. On Monday, SOL is trading at $71.35.

It has been revealed that according to the foundation, two upgrades made the change possible. In October, Solana activated Alpenglow with the Agave 4.3 release, and the time to final confirmation went down by almost 99%, from 12.8 seconds to around 150 milliseconds.

Firedancer, a validator client developed by Jump Crypto independently from Agave, is also now running on the Solana mainnet. Independent implementations "limit the impact of bugs affecting one client, and strengthen network resilience," the foundation said.

Solana 1.0 also gives the network a shared protocol version, and it does not depend on the version numbers of individual clients such as Agave and Firedancer.

"A shared protocol version lets everyone refer to Solana's evolution without using one client's release number as shorthand for the entire network," the Solana Foundation explained. "Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once.".

Recent findings suggest that earlier this year, Solana raised the compute limit per block from 60 million to 100 million compute units in May, and the slot time went down from 400 to 200 milliseconds in August. The maximum transaction size also went up from 1,232 to 4,096 bytes.

"Documentation, websites, explorers, and other ecosystem surfaces will progressively reflect the updated designation," the foundation added.

Huang is reportedly considering a return to Nvidia. He resigned last week after reports that he had an affair with a chip executive whom US authorities suspect of spying for China. Beijing denied the espionage allegation.

Strategy (MSTR) Adds 485 Bitcoin for $33.4 Million as It Spends $228 Million Buying Back Preferred Stock

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/strategy-mstr-adds-485-bitcoin-holdings

💡 Key Takeaways
  • In a recent development, strategy bought another 485 bitcoin last week.
  • According to recent reports, the coins were funded with net proceeds from MSTR common stock sales.
  • The STRC buyback was larger than that ATM slice.

In a recent development, strategy bought another 485 bitcoin last week. A Monday 8-K filing highlights the Saylor-led firm spent $33.4 million at an average of $68,887 per coin between November 9 and November 15, lifting total holdings to 850,849 BTC bought for $64.20 billion at an average of $75,452.

According to recent reports, the coins were funded with net proceeds from MSTR common stock sales. Strategy sold 2,087,040 shares for $244.7 million, put $33.4 million into bitcoin, used $206.3 million of those proceeds to buy back its STRC preferred and parked $5.0 million in USD Cash. No preferred stock was sold under the ATM during the week.

The STRC buyback was larger than that ATM slice. Strategy retired 2,282,510 STRC shares for $228.1 million, funding the other $21.8 million with interest earned on its cash, cash equivalents and short-term investments. It still has $332.2 million left under its preferred repurchase program and $1.0 billion under its MSTR buyback authorization, with about $18.1 billion of MSTR still available under the ATM.

The $228.1 million preferred repurchase was nearly seven times the $33.4 million bitcoin spend. The 485-coin add was also less than half the 1,036 bitcoin Strategy bought the week before.

BREAKING: Public companies Strategy and Strive bought over $47 million worth of Bitcoin during this dip 💥Strategy: 485 BTCStrive: 251 BTC pic.twitter.com/alNNfxbQY2.

The filing lands as the spot bitcoin price sits well below Strategy’s average cost. At the time of writing it trades near $64,100, about 15% under the $75,452 basis, leaving the stack roughly $9.7 billion underwater on paper. A week earlier, the same treasury was only modestly below cost after bitcoin slipped under $75,000.

Recent findings suggest that the upcoming coins do not close that gap. They were bought at $68,887, above today’s price but well below last week’s $79,012 average, and they shaved the manufacturer’s overall cost basis by only $4, to $75,452 from $75,456.

Strategy now holds more than 4% of bitcoin’s 21 million supply cap. The pace of buying has slowed as the firm has put more ATM cash into preferred buybacks than into bitcoin, a pattern that also marked the prior week’s purchase. Between June 30 and August 10, Strategy sold bitcoin in four consecutive filings to fund preferred dividends and STRC buybacks before flipping back to accumulation.

Recent findings suggest that strategy used $18.9 million of its USD Reserve during the week to pay preferred dividends. As of November 15, the reserve stood at $4.75 billion and USD Cash at $151.2 million.

Sources indicate that on November 15, the company mentioned it will keep the regular dividend rate on STRC at 12.00% for record dates in December. Daily STRC dividends for the month total $1.00 per share. Management said it will recommend keeping that 12% rate until STRC “has demonstrated sustained, healthy trading near $100 per share.”.

The board also declared quarterly cash dividends, payable December 31, of $2.50 a share on STRF and STRD, $2.00 on STRK, and €2.50 on STRE. Strategy noted it expects those December payments, including the daily STRC dividends, to be treated as non-taxable returns of capital to the extent of a shareholder’s tax basis.

The filing covers a week that ended with a sharp weekend slide in the bitcoin price, a move that also weighed on bitcoin-linked stocks. MSTR last closed Friday at $111.62.

The upgrade comes as Strategy faces index-fund selling after MSCI removed the stock from its USA index, with funds required to sell by November 30. The SEC 8-K is the primary disclosure; Strategy also posts the same bitcoin figures on its public dashboard.

It has been revealed that at the time of writing, bitcoin is near $64,100. The test now is whether Strategy keeps buying through a deeper underwater stack or leans even harder on preferred buybacks while the ATM stays open.

#660. 64K Bitcoin Miners Hijacked: Why the Attack Failed to Shake BTC

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4 min read (777 words)
General

64K Bitcoin Miners Hijacked: Why the Attack Failed to Shake BTC

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://dailycoin.com/bitcoin-miners-hijacked-luxor-attack-btc-impact/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » 64K Bitcoin Miners Hijacked: Why the Attack Failed to Shake BTC.
  • An AI-assisted exploit of Luxor’s software briefly diverted 1.4% of Bitcoin’s global computing power.
  • An AI-assisted exploit of Luxor’s fleet-management software briefly diverted 1.4% of Bitcoin’s global computing power, netting the attacker over $10,500 while leaving the blockchain itself untouched.

Home » Bitcoin (BTC) » 64K Bitcoin Miners Hijacked: Why the Attack Failed to Shake BTC.

An AI-assisted exploit of Luxor’s software briefly diverted 1.4% of Bitcoin’s global computing power.

An AI-assisted exploit of Luxor’s fleet-management software briefly diverted 1.4% of Bitcoin’s global computing power, netting the attacker over $10,500 while leaving the blockchain itself untouched.

A coordinated weekend cyberattack hijacked approximately 64,000 Bitcoin mining machines, temporarily redirecting up to 13 exahashes per second (EH/s) of computing power to an unauthorized address on the OCEAN mining pool.

While the incident exposed a major vulnerability in third-party mining management tools, the Bitcoin protocol itself was never compromised, and the diverted hashrate fell far short of the threshold needed to disrupt the blockchain.

Bitcoin mining hosting provider CoreX Hosting was the first to flag the suspicious activity on November 14, warning on X that thousands of machines were suddenly connecting to the OCEAN mining pool under a single external payout address.

In a recent development, just a heads up, there is a major miner hack going on as we speak. Miners are being pointed at @ocean_mining with BTC address bc1qphukp9rjfc4rcej7erpm9ae20xmtspw8pcddrr .

It has been revealed that less than an hour later, approximately 13 EH/s of computing power, equivalent to about 1.4% of the entire Bitcoin network’s global hashrate, was pointing toward the attacker’s wallet. CoreX stated it was working to restore the affected machines’ original mining configurations.

By 1:40 a.m. ET on November 15, CoreX confirmed the attack had been contained. The hashrate tied to the rogue address plunged from 13 EH/s down to roughly 100 petahashes per second (PH/s), signaling that nearly all compromised rigs had been recovered or disconnected.

Initially, blockchain trackers noted that the attacker had failed to mine a single block during the brief hijack window, suggesting the heist had yielded zero profit. However, because of how OCEAN’s payout model works, the attacker still managed to walk away with a modest payday.

Under OCEAN’s reward distribution rules, valid mining shares submitted during an active window remain eligible for payouts when the pool subsequently finds blocks.

On-chain tracking later confirmed that the attacker’s address received payouts totaling between 0.162 BTC (roughly $10,500) and 0.243 BTC across two to three block rewards before the eligible work window expired.

While the attacker’s haul was relatively small compared to the massive computing power hijacked, affected mining operators lost real-time revenue during the outage while continuing to pay electricity costs.

The incident took another turn on November 15, when mining services company Luxor confirmed that its Commander mining equipment management software had been exploited to redirect hashrate.

In a recent development, in a post on X, Luxor remarked its internal monitoring detected unauthorized pool reassignments affecting “just over a dozen” client accounts. Engineers patched the vulnerability within two hours and began reverting customer rigs to their original pools. Luxor emphasized that no user data was leaked and that its core mining pool and LuxOS firmware remained unaffected.

Last night our internal monitoring alerted us to an unauthorized redirect of hashrate through Commander. Our on-call engineering team jumped on it right away.Impact: just over a dozen client accounts. Affected machines were pointed to a different pool for a limited window. No….

In a follow-up statement, Luxor CEO Nick Hansen apologized to affected clients and noted the attack involved a “sophisticated AI-enabled vector.”.

He warned that AI-powered cyberattacks are becoming an increasing threat to crypto infrastructure, with automated systems probing for vulnerabilities around the clock.

Luxor promised to fully reimburse affected clients for lost mining revenue, paying them as if their machines had continued mining normally.

The incident exposes a vulnerability in Bitcoin’s mining infrastructure that exists outside the blockchain itself. Still, it never posed a systemic threat to Bitcoin: controlling the network requires over 50% of global computing power.

At its peak, the hijacked hashrate accounted for just ~1.4% of the network and lasted only a few hours—nowhere near enough to alter transactions or double-spend coins.

Because no user wallets were drained and Bitcoin’s consensus rules operated normally, the breach had no direct impact on Bitcoin’s market price, which hovered near the $64,500–$65,000 range amid broader macro-driven market volatility.

Industry observers note that canadian gamblers have spent the past two years quietly rerouting their deposits from Interac transfers and prepaid vouchers to Bitcoin wallets. The shift is practical, driven primarily by settlement speed. A bank e-transfer can sit in processing over a long weekend, while a BTC confirmation clears in roughly ten minutes regardless of province or statutory holiday. Searches for btc casinos and btc casino online have climbed accordingly, though the operators behind those results vary wildly in licensing, game fairness, and how seriously they treat withdrawal limits.

Roobet has built its reputation as the category’s reference point. Its BTC casino model skips fiat rails entirely, crediting deposits as soon as a transaction confirms on-chain rather than waiting for a payment processor to batch it overnight. That design choice is a big reason it keeps surfacing at the top of Canadian comparison lists, even against operators with longer track records.

Deposits move at network speed, which also means there is no chargeback mechanism once a transaction confirms. Players carry the volatility themselves between deposit and cashout, and a platform that converts to stablecoins at deposit removes that exposure in a way a straight BTC balance does not. The sector’s shift toward stablecoin settlement largely reflects players being burned by holding BTC through a losing session during a price drop. Withdrawal limits tell a similar story: a casino that caps daily cashouts low enough to slow a winning streak is usually managing its own liquidity risk. So users should be looking at the fine print on payout ceilings, which deserve more attention than the headline bonus.

Ranked side by side, the gap is less about game count and more about withdrawal friction and Canadian access.

Provably fair systems let a player verify, after the fact, that a game’s outcome wasn’t altered after they placed their bet, using a published seed and hash. It is a meaningful trust layer, but it only confirms a round wasn’t tampered with, not that the house edge is favorable. Canadian players comparing operators against real-money alternatives still need to check return-to-player rates game by game, since a verifiable algorithm and a generous payout rate are separate questions that marketing copy tends to blur.

Sources indicate that most offshore crypto casinos serving Canadians are licensed through the Kahnawake Gaming Commission, based in Mohawk Territory in Quebec, which has issued gambling licenses since 1999. Ontario is the exception: since April 2022 it has run its own regulated online market through iGaming Ontario, meaning operators without an Ontario registration are technically off-limits to residents there, even if the rest of the country can reach them freely. That patchwork is why “player protection” means something different depending on which province a deposit originates in.

None of that structure fixes the harder problem: crypto deposits remove the natural friction that used to slow a losing streak. A platform worth using still publishes deposit limits and self-exclusion tools on the same page as its game lobby, not buried three clicks deep. That detail tells a player more about the platform’s integrity than any welcome offer does.

The November 14 adjustment reversed most of October’s difficulty increases. Expected coin earnings improve, but profits still depend on price, fees and costs.

Industry observers note that bitcoin’s mining difficulty fell 9.1% on November 14, reversing most of the extra computational burden added by October’s two increases. The completed reset increases the chance that a given amount of computing work earns a block reward, providing immediate computational relief for operating miners.

According to recent reports, the adjustment took effect at block 975,744, timestamped 05:02:50 UTC. Difficulty dropped from 148.36 trillion to 134.82 trillion, according to Mempool’s adjustment history.

Bitcoin recalculates difficulty every 2,016 blocks to target an average interval of roughly ten minutes.

Sources indicate that october’s increases had lifted difficulty by a combined 11.8% from its October 3 level of 132.72 trillion. The first increase, on October 16, was about 5.9%; the second, on October 29, added about 5.5%.

In a recent development, the November cut removed 86.5% of the increase accumulated across those two adjustments. Difficulty now sits just 1.6% above the October 3 baseline. The reset therefore unwinds most of that added burden without taking difficulty all the way back to its earlier level.

The completed November 14 reset leaves difficulty 1.59% above October 3. Levels are in trillions (T), rounded to three decimals in labels. Four discrete 2026 retargets; bars begin at zero.

Source: Mempool difficulty-adjustment history.

At unchanged block subsidy and average transaction fees per block, the old-to-new difficulty ratio implies 10% higher expected BTC earnings per unit of computing power.

According to recent reports, the gain is larger than the 9.13% difficulty decline because earnings per hash move inversely with difficulty. Dividing the previous difficulty by the new level gives about 1.1004, meaning the same work has a higher expected reward under those fixed assumptions. It is a calculation of gross expected earnings, rather than a measured increase in a miner’s receipts or profit.

Yi He, the co-founder of the world’s largest cryptocurrency exchange, Binance, has sparked discussions across the crypto market after urging retail traders to stay calm even as major crypto assets continue to post massive daily losses.

Yi He’s consoling statement has come as crypto traders grow increasingly weary and the prolonged market volatility begins to cause even bigger losses, with Bitcoin retesting $63,000.

In her post, Yi urged investors holding major crypto assets that have been substantially affected by the severe market volatility to remain calm amid the latest market downturn.

She described the ongoing crypto market pullback as ‘temporary’ while assuring spot traders that they have little reason to worry.

Alongside the post, Yi He shared a link to the Binance app showcasing a 30-day asset change of approximately -$101.31 million in her account.

The figure indicates the amount of losses the pro-crypto investor has suffered on her holdings over a period of about a month, from October 17 to November 16, 2026.

Although the showcased portfolio reveals a decline in the founder’s holdings, it does not establish whether the decline represents realized trading losses, unrealized losses, withdrawals, or other changes in Yi He’s account.

It appears that some investors may have found comfort in Yi He's message as they expressed support, noting that turbulent conditions like these don’t necessarily last long.

However, other commentators have questioned whether wealthy industry figures like Yi He can fully understand the financial pressure facing retail traders at a time like this.

Some of the arguments questioned how meaningful such reassurance could be for retail investors, arguing that losing 100 million yuan might not significantly affect someone with substantial wealth like her.

Meanwhile, a loss of 20,000 or 30,000 yuan could wipe out an ordinary investor's savings.

Cardano DReps have rejected a proposal by Toto Finance to spend 22 million ADA from the Cardano treasury on a "Strategic Copper Reserve.".

The vote closed on Nov. 15, and DReps holding 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, according to Cardano governance data. DReps with 20.02 million ADA voted in favor of it.

DRep John MacPherson was among those who voted "No," and he explained his decision in a post on X.

MacPherson wrote that he is not against real-world assets on Cardano. Still, he said the proposal asks the treasury "to take on both the copper price and the ada price," and Toto Finance would collect "up to about 3.4M ada in fees.".

At the same time, MacPherson said that the proposal is “more honest about its risks than most.”.

Toto Finance, a company led by Monty Metzger, submitted the proposal on Oct. 15. ADA is trading at $0.152 on Monday, and the requested 22 million ADA is now worth around $3.3 million.

The plan was to buy copper with 14.72 million ADA and store it in a warehouse near Fresh Orleans. Toto Finance wanted to issue one CuTT token for each pound of copper. The metal would be sold in 18 to 24 months.

The Cardano Foundation, which votes as a DRep, revealed its "No" vote in October.

"We recognize the opportunity in real-world asset tokenization; however, this proposal places 22,000,000 ada under the recipient's sole control to fund a fee-heavy concentrated commodity position whose safeguards are not yet in place," the foundation wrote.

Three members of the Constitutional Committee voted "No," and the other four members did not vote.

Crypto commentator Ingeniero Cripto agreed with MacPherson in the replies under his post. He called the "double exposure" to the prices of copper and ADA the key problem of the proposal, as the Cardano treasury already holds ADA.

According to him, RWAs on Cardano make sense, but “funding the asset itself is a different question than funding the rails.”.

It has been revealed that thailand's Securities and Exchange Commission is seeking feedback on restrictions that could significantly change how customers move stablecoins through regulated digital-asset operators. The proposed rules would generally limit eligible transfers into and out of a customer's account to 5 million baht per day in each direction, while requiring wallets at both ends to belong to that customer.

Recent findings suggest that this is a consultation, not a rule that has already taken effect. The details, exemptions and eventual text matter more than the headline dollar equivalent, especially for businesses using stablecoins for legitimate cross-border payments.

In its November 12 announcement, the Thai SEC stated the draft aims to reduce the risk that regulated crypto businesses facilitate money laundering, cybercrime or circumvention of cross-border transfer rules. The proposal would generally require stablecoins entering or leaving a customer's account at a digital-asset operator to come from, or go to, an account or wallet verified as belonging to that same person.

The draft also calls for controls aligned with the Travel Rule, screening for risky wallets and transaction monitoring. Those measures aim to improve traceability where a licensed intermediary is involved. They do not mean all movements of stablecoins across every blockchain would suddenly be visible to, or controlled by, one Thai exchange.

Under the proposal, inbound and outbound transfers would each be limited separately to 5 million baht per customer, per day, with each operator. The SEC's announcement also describes exemptions, including qualifying transfers between the customer's own accounts at regulated operators, certain regulated businesses and approved liquidity-provision activities. The exact scope depends on the final regulation and whether participants satisfy the relevant requirements.

According to recent reports, that nuance is easy to lose in a short headline. It would be inaccurate to say Thailand is proposing a universal daily blockchain transfer limit, or that every business must stop moving more than that amount under all circumstances. The consultation is specifically focused on activity conducted through supervised digital-asset operators.

According to recent reports, stablecoins have become useful tools for businesses moving money across borders, particularly where traditional transfers are expensive or slow. NewsBTC's report on Bitso Business's stablecoin payments shows the commercial use case behind this growth. For such companies, wallet verification and transfer limits create compliance work that must fit alongside existing customer checks.

In a recent development, the risk is that rules designed to catch illicit activity could also make ordinary, lawful operations cumbersome if identity matching is difficult or exceptions are unclear. The regulator, meanwhile, has a legitimate interest in ensuring supervised firms know who is using their systems. That tension is precisely what a public consultation is supposed to examine.

The SEC has invited feedback through November 26, 2026. Businesses should review the official draft rather than rely on simplified social-media summaries, particularly when deciding whether their specific transaction flows would be covered. The same distinction between technology and regulated access appears in NewsBTC's coverage of USDC on Solana through Samsung Wallet.

Sources indicate that thailand's proposal reflects a growing regulatory emphasis on the point where blockchain assets interact with licensed businesses. Whether the final rules strike the intended balance will depend on clear exemptions, workable verification and evidence that the controls reduce risk without unnecessarily obstructing legitimate payments.

Microsoft VP Jason Ronald details how the next-gen console merges Xbox libraries with PC gaming.

Industry observers note that microsoft has officially clarified its vision for the upcoming Project Helix Xbox console, confirming in the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine that the next-generation system is built to run both traditional Xbox libraries and PC games. A hybrid shift could also open new doors for Web3 gaming.

It has been revealed that as Microsoft celebrates Xbox’s 25th anniversary, the manufacturer has shared fresh architectural details about the Project Helix Xbox console, its upcoming next-generation console. When Microsoft first introduced the project earlier this year, it confirmed that the new system would bring Xbox and PC gaming closer together. This led many to assume that Helix would essentially be a Windows gaming PC packaged in a console design.

In a four-page Q&A inside the Xbox 25th Anniversary Magazine, Vice President of Next Generation Jason Ronald pushed back directly against that framing.

“Project Helix is designed to be a console capable of playing games from your PC,” Ronald stated. “It is not a PC that can also play console games.”.

For Microsoft, the distinction comes down to removing the friction traditionally associated with PC gaming, such as driver management, multiple launchers, and complex configuration menus, while keeping deeper controls accessible for enthusiasts.

According to recent reports, “The goal is making it easy, intuitive, and instant to access my games,” Ronald explained. “But if you’re a hardcore gamer or a power user who wants to have that deeper level of customizability across settings and performance options, you can absolutely go do it.”.

According to Ronald and the anniversary feature, Project Helix is being built around several core pillars:.

Project Helix, which Xbox CEO Asha Sharma has previously described as a broader “family of devices” rather than a single box, is taking shape during a turbulent stretch for Microsoft’s gaming division.

After taking the helm earlier in 2026, Sharma oversaw major restructuring, studio closures, and layoffs, candidly remarking in July that the Xbox brand was “not healthy.” Simultaneously, ongoing global memory and storage component shortages have pushed up manufacturing costs across the hardware industry, prompting some players to urge both Microsoft and Sony to delay next-gen launches until prices stabilize.

Ronald acknowledged those supply-chain headwinds, calling the current hardware environment “brutal,” though he argued that the constraints are forcing Xbox engineers to innovate rather than simply throw costlier components at the machine.

Microsoft has not confirmed a price or consumer launch window for Project Helix, though alpha developer hardware is slated to begin shipping in 2027, with retail speculation pointing toward late 2027 or 2028.

For the Web3 gaming sector, Microsoft’s hybrid console-PC strategy could solve a long-standing distribution bottleneck.

Historically, console manufacturers have enforced strict platform policies against blockchain integrations, external crypto wallets, and NFTs, forcing Web3 studios to build almost exclusively for PC, web browsers, and mobile devices.

Still, Ronald noted that the ROG Xbox Ally served as a testing ground for unifying game libraries across multiple stores.

If Project Helix eventually supports third-party PC storefronts such as Steam and the Epic Games Store, it could create upcoming opportunities for blockchain-enabled games to reach console audiences.

Recent findings suggest that however, vital questions remain unanswered. Microsoft has not confirmed third-party storefront support on Project Helix, nor has it announced native support for external crypto wallets, NFT functionality, or blockchain transactions.

It has been revealed that nevertheless, the direction is worth watching. If Project Helix successfully bridges the console and PC gaming ecosystems, it could create fresh distribution opportunities for Web3 games and help bring blockchain-powered gaming experiences closer to mainstream players.

The technology maps rainfall worldwide at 15-minute intervals, offering new tools for studying disasters in poorly monitored regions.

Google DeepMind has opened access to an artificial intelligence system that tracks rainfall worldwide, potentially helping researchers monitor floods and droughts in regions with limited weather infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that the organization revealed on Nov. 13 that researchers and developers can now access historical records and continuously updated data from PARDIG, its AI-powered global precipitation monitoring system.

The technology combines satellite observations and atmospheric data to estimate rainfall every 15 minutes across a global grid with roughly 10-kilometer resolution.

Its release could expand access to rainfall intelligence in developing countries and remote regions where limited weather radar coverage makes it difficult to track storms, flooding and prolonged dry spells.

Google stated PARDIG learns from precipitation measurements collected by NASA's Global Precipitation Measurement satellite and uses additional satellite imagery and atmospheric information to estimate rainfall across the planet.

Unlike conventional monitoring systems that depend heavily on ground-based weather stations, PARDIG can generate estimates over oceans and regions with sparse observation networks.

The dataset also supports Google's WeatherNext 3 forecasting model, which uses PARDIG-generated rainfall information during training.

Researchers can access historical rainfall records dating back to 1999, alongside a separate dataset covering 2016 to the present.

Google has released both under a Creative Commons license that permits commercial reuse with attribution, potentially allowing companies to incorporate the information into agricultural monitoring, water management and disaster-risk applications.

DeepMind mentioned PARDIG achieved more than 30% higher hourly precipitation detection skill than NASA's IMERG-Final dataset when measuring light-to-moderate rainfall.

The organization evaluated the system against radar networks in the United States, Europe and Japan, alongside observations from more than 36,000 weather stations worldwide.

Its research paper also reported improved identification of intense rainfall events, which existing global precipitation datasets can struggle to capture accurately.

These capabilities could help researchers develop more detailed models of extreme weather events, including flash floods, landslides and drought conditions.

Google highlighted the July 2025 Texas Hill Country floods as one example, comparing PARDIG's estimates with ground-based radar measurements and NASA's existing rainfall dataset.

However, the technology has limitations that could constrain its use during rapidly developing emergencies.

Although PARDIG estimates rainfall at 15-minute intervals, Google publishes its near-real-time data in six-hour batches, creating an average delay of about five hours between observation and availability.

XRP Ledger Foundation Director of Community Hussein Zangana (Vet) shared a tidbit of XRPL's early history in a recent X post.

Vet noted that the XRP Ledger (XRPL) still carries traces of Satoshi Nakamoto’s original Bitcoin design, highlighting two features.

According to recent reports, in 2011, three engineers—David Schwartz, Jed McCaleb, and Arthur Britto—began developing the XRP Ledger (XRPL). Fascinated by Bitcoin, they set out to create a better version that improved upon its limitations—with the goal of creating a digital asset that was more sustainable and built specifically for payments.

As reported, the first line of code for the core of what would become the XRP Ledger (XRPL) was written by David Schwartz, who is Ripple CTO emeritus, about 15 years ago, on November 11, 2011.

Vet delves into the earliest part of XRP Ledger history, noting that 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, wrote. Vet added that Jed McCaleb also copied Satoshi’s timekeeping code into the XRPL, even including one of the Bitcoin creator’s comments shared as a screenshot.

Did you know all of us on the XRP Ledger use design choices by Satoshi daily? 15 years ago, the XRP Ledger started out using some Bitcoin code, including helper functions from the Bitcoin client that Satoshi wrote. Jed copied Satoshi's timekeeping code into the XRPL, including one of Satoshi's comments. By the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone. In December 2014, Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment. Two design choices of Satoshi still remain on the XRPL and all of us use at least one of it. Signature curve secp256k1 (we also support Ed25519 thus not everyone uses this) and how XRPL addresses are generated from the public key with SHA-256 followed by RIPEMD-160, that's what all of us use.

The quote "Never go to sea with two chronometers; take one or three" is a classic maritime adage famously included by Satoshi Nakamoto (the pseudonymous creator of Bitcoin) within the Bitcoin source code.

According to recent reports, vet explained that by the end of 2014, the original Satoshi code was gone from the XRP Ledger. In December 2014, former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis removed the last of the timekeeping code, along with Satoshi's comment.

Sources indicate that however, two of Satoshi's design choices still remain on the XRP Ledger: the first is the secp256k1 signature curve, which Bitcoin uses and which the XRP Ledger continues to support. However, the ledger also supports Ed25519, meaning not every XRPL user relies on secp256k1.

"I remember David saying they used secp256k1 so no one would doubt the security because it's the same as Bitcoin's, etc.," Vet stated, citing the insight of the Ripple CTO emeritus on secp256k1, adding, "Lots of interesting things to dig into from the early days.".

The second is the method used to generate XRP Ledger addresses from public keys. The process applies SHA-256 hashing followed by RIPEMD-160, a design inherited from Bitcoin that remains common to all XRPL addresses.

Asked why the timekeeping code and Satoshi's comment were removed, Vet explained that this became leftover code as new code was introduced, so it was cleaned up.

It has been revealed that twenty One Capital has reported net income of about $1.09 billion for the third quarter, a figure that might look extraordinary for a Bitcoin-focused company. But nearly all of that profit came from changes in the fair value of its Bitcoin holdings rather than cash generated by selling services. That makes the result a useful lesson in how digital-asset treasury accounting can obscure the difference between holding an appreciated asset and operating a profitable business.

Neither figure should be ignored. Bitcoin holdings can create real economic value, but marked-to-market gains can reverse quickly when prices change.

According to The Block's account of Twenty One Capital's filing, the company reported $1.087 billion in quarterly net income, driven largely by around $1.093 billion in fair-value increases on Bitcoin. At the same time, it recorded an operating loss of approximately $4.8 million and interest expense near $1.34 million.

In a recent development, that contrast is the heart of the story. An asset can become more valuable on the balance sheet without generating money to pay salaries or service borrowing costs. Accounting rules may require those changes to appear in reported earnings, but investors still need to separate recurring business performance from market revaluation when assessing sustainability.

Twenty One Capital reported holding 43,514 BTC at September 30, with its holdings valued using a Bitcoin price around $83,700 at the reporting date. The company also disclosed approximately $102.8 million in cash and $486.5 million of convertible-note principal collateralised by a portion of its Bitcoin. Those liabilities and collateral arrangements are important because holding a volatile asset alongside debt creates distinct liquidity and financing considerations.

Recent findings suggest that A higher Bitcoin price can make the balance sheet appear stronger. A lower price can compress asset values while obligations remain, potentially forcing management to reconsider capital allocation. That is why the composition of the treasury, maturity profile and collateral terms can be just as relevant as the headline quantity of BTC.

Industry observers note that chief executive Rapha Zagury has made clear that asset appreciation and profits earned through operations are different. The manufacturer has discussed possible opportunities in mining, lending, treasury-related services and share repurchases. Those ideas could broaden its sources of income, but they should be treated as areas under consideration until the business publishes concrete agreements, operating milestones and results.

Industry observers note that the same filing showed a net loss for the first nine months of 2026, underscoring how results can swing with changing Bitcoin prices. Investors evaluating a treasury business should consider asset value per share, the effect of any new share or debt issuance, cash needs and whether proposed business lines eventually contribute positive operating cash flow.

It has been revealed that there is a market-wide backdrop too. Recent Bitcoin ETF redemptions covered by NewsBTC show that demand for BTC exposure can weaken abruptly. Twenty One Capital's quarterly statement is not evidence that the Bitcoin treasury model has either won or failed. It is evidence that accounting earnings can be dominated by the underlying asset — and that understanding the difference is essential.

Harvard’s gold ETF share count rose nearly 20-fold in Q3, while Dartmouth kept its positions in Solana and Ether staking ETFs unchanged.

Harvard University and Dartmouth College reported unchanged share counts in BlackRock’s spot Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF) at the end of the third quarter as a Bitcoin rally lifted the value of both stakes.

Harvard held 3.04 million shares of the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (IBIT), worth about $144.1 million at the end of September, while Dartmouth reported 201,531 shares valued at $9.5 million, according to Form 13F filings with the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

In a recent development, IBIT gained about 42% in Q3 as Bitcoin (BTC) rallied nearly 43%. Both posted their strongest quarterly gains of 2026 through September.

Harvard has reported the same IBIT share count since the end of March, after cutting its holdings by 43% in Q1 and 21% in Q4 2025. Dartmouth has reported the same 201,531 shares since first disclosing its Bitcoin ETF position in Q4 2025.

Harvard increased its share count in the State Street’s SPDR Gold Shares ETF (GLD) nearly 20-fold in Q3, to 1.16 million from 58,862. The position was worth $442.2 million at the end of September.

Industry observers note that dartmouth again reported 304,803 shares of the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF and 178,148 shares of the Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF. The positions were worth $4.9 million and $4.5 million, respectively, at quarter-end.

According to recent reports, the steady university holdings contrasted with moves by major financial companies. Jane Street reduced its IBIT shares by 19% in Q3, while JPMorgan Chase increased the number of shares it held by 9.6%, according to their latest quarterly filings.

Recent findings suggest that kraken parent Payward has reported a sequential improvement in quarterly profitability even as its business remains smaller on several measures than it was a year earlier. The organization posted $60 million in adjusted EBITDA for the third quarter of 2026, up from $23 million in the previous quarter, alongside an expansion of its platform beyond conventional cryptocurrency trading.

Sources indicate that those results point to a business trying to diversify while navigating a difficult trading environment. They also require attention to the company's chosen metrics: adjusted EBITDA and its newly emphasised Total Platform Margin are not the same thing as statutory net profit or ordinary gross revenue.

In its November 13 financial update, Payward reported Total Platform Margin, or TPM, of $487 million, compared with $436 million in the second quarter. That represented 12% sequential growth, although TPM was also down 12% from a year earlier. Adjusted EBITDA increased to $60 million from $23 million in Q2, while remaining substantially below the year-earlier result.

Recent findings suggest that payward has changed how it presents the business, replacing a previously highlighted adjusted-revenue measure with TPM. The company claims this approach deducts costs passed on to customers, including certain staking rewards, to provide a better view of what the platform retains. Investors should compare periods on consistent definitions rather than treating a renamed headline metric as automatically equivalent to prior revenue figures.

Total platform transaction volume reached about $353 billion, up 22% quarter on quarter, though down 30% from Q3 2025. Funded accounts increased to around 7.1 million, reflecting an expanding account base even as overall trading conditions remained challenging. The combination suggests growth in the number of customers does not necessarily translate into a proportional increase in transaction activity every quarter.

Sources indicate that the organization also highlighted transaction-based, asset-based and access-based sources of platform margin. Together, asset and access activity represented slightly more than half of TPM, indicating an effort to rely less exclusively on trading fees. Whether those businesses remain resilient through another difficult market cycle will be more telling than one period of sequential recovery.

It has been revealed that payward's broader ambitions include banking, asset management, services for other businesses and AI-driven financial tools. Its statement describes plans to introduce an agent-oriented layer intended to let customers authorise software to perform actions within programmed risk limits. Such a system raises practical questions about consent, error handling and how a customer reverses an unwanted automated action.

According to recent reports, newsBTC previously covered Payward's proposed move into European banking through Saldo, which illustrates how the company is seeking a wider relationship with customers than a trading account alone. These plans should not be confused with proof that every revealed product is already commercially available or licensed in every market.

Expanding into adjacent activities can smooth the effects of volatile crypto trading, but it can also introduce fresh costs and regulatory obligations. Payward's investment in Aave covered by NewsBTC is another example of the tech giant's interest in market infrastructure beyond centralised exchange transactions.

The next quarterly update should show whether TPM growth continues without depending on a short-lived jump in volumes, and how much of the improvement reaches the bottom line. For now, the Q3 release offers a mixed but informative picture: recovery from Q2, weaker comparisons with last year and a company making a deliberate bet on diversification.

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has replied to XRP holders who criticized him for selling most of his XRP with a Saturday Night Live GIF of Natalie Portman saying, "I never said I was a role model.".

According to Schwartz, his XRP holdings are down 88%, from a peak of roughly 26 million tokens to 3 million. His Bitcoin went from about 1,500 coins to one, and his Ether went from about 40,000 to six.

According to recent reports, schwartz wrote that he "really doesn't like risk." According to Schwartz, he and his wife agreed years ago to sell some of their coins every time crypto reached a new all-time high. In 2025, Schwartz sold around 2.5 million XRP and paid about $1.7 million in capital gains tax on the sale. He had received these tokens in 2020 and 2023.
