Schwartz noted that all of his sales were made under written trading looks, and a lawyer approved each blueprint at least 30 days before each sale. According to Schwartz, his largest risk asset is still his stake in Ripple.

Schwartz also mentioned that he was a skeptic from the start and did not believe in the early price records of crypto. "When XRP hit 10 cents, that seemed ridiculous. When ETH hit $1, that seemed ridiculous," he wrote.

In a recent development, in his view, the price of XRP today depends on overall sentiment in the crypto market, and fees on the network barely move it. Schwartz allows that the token could capture some of the value of a successful ecosystem in the future, but there are no guarantees. On Monday, the price of XRP stands at $0.956.

On Nov. 16, Schwartz also posted a review of the XRPL codebase by the Qwen AI model. "I asked Qwen to rate my work on the XRPL software. It was mostly good. But this was harsh and it's not wrong," he wrote.

It has been revealed that according to the review, the overall architecture of XRPL is good. Still, Qwen stated that some components of the code are too tightly coupled, and the migration to a fresh testing framework stopped halfway. The AI model also called the code generation in XRPL opaque.

Several XRPL developers replied to the post and noted that they are already rewriting some of these parts of the code. Other users asked for formal verification of the XRPL core before the new features planned for 2027 go live.

BTC enthusiast GalaxyMind estimated that the attack affected approximately 64,000 Bitcoin mining machines, redirecting 13 exahashes per second (EH/s) of computing power since around 8 p.m. Central Time on Nov. 14.

Blockchain security firm CoinSpect added that the redirected computing power represented approximately 1.5% of Bitcoin's global hashrate.

The incident threatened miners' earnings because the unauthorized changes directed rewards away from their intended recipients while their equipment continued consuming electricity and processing transactions.

CoreX subsequently reported that it was restoring affected miners to their original configurations and believed it had isolated the program responsible for the unauthorized changes.

The tech giant later declared the incident over after the computing power associated with the suspicious address reportedly fell to approximately 100 petahashes per second (PH/s), down from the previously reported 13 EH/s.

Still, blockchain records show that the Bitcoin address identified in CoreX's original warning had received mining rewards. Data from OCEAN shows three payments totaling 0.24308905 BTC between Nov. 15 and Nov. 16.

“Last night our internal monitoring alerted us to an unauthorized redirect of hashrate through Commander…over a dozen client accounts. Affected machines were pointed to a different pool for a limited window. No data was leaked or exfiltrated from our systems.”.

The firm's engineering team patched Commander within two hours and began restoring affected machines to their original mining pools. It also promised full compensation for the redirected computing power.

Luxor CEO Nick Hansen attributed the compromise to a “sophisticated AI-enabled vector,” saying the attack began around 6 p.m. Pacific time on Nov. 14.

Luxor has not disclosed the precise method used to compromise Commander or confirmed GalaxyMind's estimates of 64,000 affected machines and 13 EH/s.

Hyperliquid's derivatives business has grown large enough to challenge some familiar centralised exchange names on a key measure: open interest. A third-quarter research report put positions open on the platform at approximately $16.8 billion at the end of September, a major increase over the previous quarter. For a decentralised trading venue, the scale is striking. But comparing it with conventional exchanges requires more than ranking a single number.

Open interest is the value of contracts that remain outstanding, not the amount of cash a venue has collected in fees or the value of trades settled that day. It reveals participation and leverage, while leaving vital questions about market depth and resilience unanswered.

Recent findings suggest that the Block's report on Hyperliquid's Q3 figures described open interest reaching roughly $16.8 billion, nearly 80% above the level recorded at the end of June. The report compared that snapshot with data for exchanges including Bybit, Kraken and OKX, though rankings depend on which products, venues and measurement conventions are included.

The headline number suggests that traders are comfortable maintaining substantial derivative exposure on Hyperliquid. It does not prove that all of that exposure is unhedged directional speculation. Some participants may be market makers or arbitrageurs carrying positions that offset risk elsewhere, while other traders could be using leverage to express very concentrated views.

In a recent development, the same Q3 analysis estimated approximately $191 million in protocol revenue, an increase of about 21.7% from the second quarter but a decrease of roughly 36.5% compared with the year-earlier period. That contrast is a useful warning against assuming that more open contracts automatically translate into stronger year-on-year economics. Revenue depends on trading activity, fees and the mix of products used.

Stock-linked perpetual products were another standout, with reported quarterly trading volume of about $153.8 billion, up approximately 161% sequentially. Yet volume can be affected by incentives, volatility and the churn of high-frequency participants. Healthy trading infrastructure also needs reliable pricing, liquid order books and a credible process for handling extreme market moves.

Industry observers note that perpetual futures let traders maintain leveraged exposure without a fixed expiry date. That flexibility comes with funding payments, margin requirements and liquidation risk. During a sharp market decline, forced closing of positions can magnify volatility. A platform's decentralised components do not eliminate the economic risk of carrying leverage or the operational need for robust safeguards.

It has been revealed that this is particularly relevant after the week's crypto sell-off. Market watchers should compare open interest with trading volume, funding costs and liquidation activity rather than treating rising positions as inherently bullish. A platform can be technologically impressive and still host dangerous levels of speculative risk.

In a recent development, the rise of on-chain perpetuals adds to the broader discussion about where exchange activity should take place. NewsBTC's coverage of institutional interest in DeFi through Aave highlights that traditional crypto firms are exploring decentralised infrastructure. Meanwhile, Aave's reserve-factor debate illustrates the governance decisions that shape the economics of on-chain services.

Recent findings suggest that hyperliquid's Q3 performance is evidence that decentralised derivatives can operate at considerable scale. The harder test comes during severe volatility, when users will judge it on execution quality, orderly liquidations and transparent risk management. Those outcomes will say more about the durability of its position than any single exchange league table.

It has been revealed that major U.S. wealth management company EP Wealth Advisors has revealed that it holds an investment in an XRP exchange-traded fund (ETF). This was disclosed in the company's latest 13F filing with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC).

Industry observers note that EP Wealth Advisors, a California-based investment advisory firm with about $24.4 billion in securities holdings, has revealed that it held 18,400 shares in the Volatility Shares XRP ETF (XRPI) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

This was disclosed in the official SEC filing that the tech giant submitted to the commission on Nov. 13. The filing indicated that the investment was valued at $147,936 at the end of the third quarter.

According to recent reports, furthermore, the filing indicated that the total portfolio value reported by EP Wealth Advisors stood at $24,380,879,896. This value comprises 1,603 items in the tech giant's 13F information table.

It's worth noting, however, that this isn't the manufacturer's total assets under management. It's the value of its reportable securities holdings. There are also assets that are not included in Form 13F.

It has been revealed that interestingly, this isn't the first time EP Wealth Advisors has held an investment in XRPI. Data from its historical 13F filings reveals that in the second quarter of 2026, the wealth management firm held 13,425 shares in XRPI.

It has been revealed that the recent filing indicates that the firm has now increased the number of shares it holds in the XRP ETF by 4,975 shares. This represents about a 37% increase in the company's XRPI holdings during the third quarter.

Nevertheless, this amount is very small relative to the company's multibillion-dollar securities portfolio. It represents less than 0.01% of the total value of its reported securities holdings.

It's also worth reiterating that Form 13F is simply a filing that shows institutional holdings at the end of a quarter. It doesn't necessarily represent the investment manager's current holdings.

Industry observers note that the Volatility Shares XRP ETF was rolled out in May 2025. Its ticker symbol is XRPI, and it is right now trading on Nasdaq.

According to recent reports, XRPI isn't a spot XRP ETF. This means it doesn't directly hold the cryptocurrency XRP. Rather, it primarily derives its exposure to XRP's price movements through XRP futures contracts.

This ETF essentially provides investors with a way to invest in XRP without actually having to hold or custody the cryptocurrency. The ETF aims to deliver investment returns that correlate with the performance of XRP.

As of Nov. 13, the most recent available data from the fund issuer reveals that XRPI's net assets stood at about $77.9 million.

Bitcoin may be approaching one of the most interesting technical windows of its current market cycle. A newly shared historical chart suggests that BTC has repeatedly broken major descending resistance lines around 1,000 days after a halving, raising questions about whether another recovery could be approaching.

The analysis comes as Bitcoin trades near $64,282.54, according to the latest price provided at the time of writing, following a significant correction from its 2025 highs.

While traders continue debating whether the four-year cycle remains relevant, Bitcoinist recently examined how Bitcoin’s technical structure could avoid upcoming lows, highlighting the importance of reclaiming long-term moving averages.

Now, another historical pattern is attracting attention.

On November 16, Rand Group shared a chart credited to analyst Jesse Olson, highlighting an unusual similarity between previous Bitcoin halving cycles.

The analysis suggests that Bitcoin’s 2016 and 2020 cycles broke their post-peak descending trendlines around day 1,000 after their respective halvings.

The chart overlays several cycles, using the number of days after each halving to compare their price structures.

According to Rand Group, the current cycle is approaching the same historical window.

Using the April 20, 2024 halving date, November 16, 2026 represents approximately day 940, leaving around 60 days before the 1,000-day milestone.

The historical comparison is particularly interesting because both previous breakouts occurred after extended periods of declining prices.

However, the pattern does not establish that Bitcoin must repeat its earlier performance.

The Bitcoin halving history confirms the dates used to compare the cycles, but the descending trendlines and their breakout timing remain the analyst’s interpretation.

The central question is whether Bitcoin’s current price structure supports the possibility of another trend reversal.

At approximately $64,282, Bitcoin remains below the immediate $65,000 resistance area.

A sustained recovery above that threshold could provide the first indication of improving short-term momentum.

However, stronger confirmation would require BTC to reclaim higher resistance around $68,000 and $70,000.

From a technical perspective, a descending trendline connects a series of lower highs.

Breaking above that line suggests selling pressure may be weakening, but traders generally look for additional confirmation through stronger volume and successful retests.

The Relative Strength Index is another key indicator.

A sustained move above 50 could suggest improving bullish momentum, particularly if Bitcoin simultaneously establishes higher lows.

Conversely, continued rejection below resistance would indicate that the broader downtrend remains intact.

The $62,000 region represents an notable downside reference, followed by the psychological $60,000 level.

Historical cycle analysis has become increasingly popular as investors search for signs of a market bottom.

Bitcoinist previously covered an analyst’s Bitcoin cycle timing model, which similarly examined recurring intervals between major market turning points.

Nevertheless, exact timing models can be misleading when they rely on a small number of historical observations.

Bitcoin’s current market structure is also different from earlier cycles.

Institutional participation, exchange-traded funds, and changing global liquidity conditions could influence how future recoveries develop.

Another Bitcoinist analysis explored the possibility of a historical Bitcoin fakeout, demonstrating why investors should consider alternative scenarios before treating recurring chart formations as guaranteed outcomes.

The strongest bullish signal would not simply be reaching day 1,000.

Instead, it would be a confirmed breakout above descending resistance, supported by improving volume, momentum, and market structure.

Bitcoin’s approaching 1,000-day milestone offers an intriguing historical comparison.

If the pattern highlighted by Rand Group repeats, the coming weeks could become an vital period for traders watching the end of the current downtrend.

We believe the technical evidence deserves attention, particularly if Bitcoin begins reclaiming resistance levels and establishing a sequence of higher lows.

However, historical similarities alone cannot confirm a market bottom.

For now, $65,000 remains the first resistance area to monitor, followed by $68,000 and $70,000.

A convincing breakout through these levels could strengthen the case for a broader recovery.

Until then, the 1,000-day halving pattern remains a potentially bullish setup awaiting confirmation.

Sources indicate that A confrontation between Louisiana officials and the US Commodity Futures Trading Commission is sharpening the dispute over who gets to regulate prediction markets. The state has pursued restrictions on certain event-contract offerings, while the federal agency has gone to court asserting its authority. The dispute could affect platforms offering sports and other outcome-based contracts, but the legal arguments have not yet produced a final nationwide answer.

Sources indicate that it is a case where the exact stage of litigation matters. Temporary orders, complaints and jurisdictional claims are not final findings about which side is right.

Industry observers note that the Block reported that a Louisiana state court issued a temporary restraining order on November 12 involving a group of prediction-market and related businesses. The state's approach seeks to require geographic restrictions for certain offerings that it indicates should not be available without appropriate state authorisation. Firms named in the proceedings reportedly include Kalshi, Polymarket, Coinbase and Robinhood among a wider set.

An order of this kind is designed to address immediate concerns while further litigation continues. Its existence does not establish that every product mentioned is unlawful under all circumstances. Different platforms may offer different types of contracts, and the precise language of the order and subsequent court rulings determines what each respondent must do.

The CFTC filed a federal complaint on November 13 as the dispute escalated. Federal commodities law gives the agency crucial powers over derivatives markets, but state authorities have their own responsibilities for gambling and consumer protection. The central legal question is where one set of powers ends and the other begins when an event contract resembles both a derivative and a bet on an outcome.

In a recent development, the disagreement is not merely political theatre. Companies need clear boundaries to decide which products may be offered, how customers must be screened and what licences or approvals are necessary. Conflicting instructions from different levels of government can be expensive to implement and difficult for customers to understand.

For an operator, an adverse ruling might mean geofencing customers, suspending products or changing contract design. For people, it might affect whether an existing market remains accessible in their location and what protections apply if a dispute arises. These potential consequences make the litigation commercially significant even before the courts resolve the larger federalism question.

NewsBTC's earlier account of CFTC-related litigation involving Coinbase and Kalshi offers useful background on the expanding legal debate around event and derivative markets. A single case, however, should not be treated as decisive precedent for every possible contract category.

Reporting identifies November 30 as a date to watch in the Louisiana proceedings. Whether temporary restrictions remain in force, are modified or expire can depend on procedural developments before then. Readers should also monitor the federal case independently, as it may follow a different timetable and raise distinct legal questions.

In a recent development, other jurisdictions are wrestling with how to supervise fresh financial infrastructure, including tokenisation standards in Europe. Louisiana's dispute is a particularly sharp example of the same underlying problem: innovation does not arrive organised according to existing regulator boundaries. Until courts and lawmakers clarify those boundaries, platforms will continue to operate amid uncertainty rather than a settled national rulebook.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has published a lengthy post on EIP-8037, a change planned for the Glamsterdam upgrade. In his latest post, Buterin wrote that something like EIP-8037 is, unfortunately, the only way for Ethereum to scale safely.

With the upgrade, Ethereum will collect an additional gas fee for the creation of newly introduced accounts. Creating a new account would cost more than five times as much gas as it does now, with new storage slots and contracts getting more expensive too.

According to Buterin, execution is easy to scale, but Ethereum's state already grows by around 110 GiB per year, and every node has to keep it.

In a recent development, unfortunately, it will bring more pressure on existing contracts, for example, the OP Stack bridge. The bridge has a hardcoded gas limit of 40,000, and even a small increase in state gas costs would push its operation above it. Mainnet has at least 13 contracts like that, according to the security firm ChainSecurity.

It's a double-edged sword: from one standpoint, it limits the ability of spammers and scammers to fill the network with junk accounts used by illicit actors; from the other, it creates additional financial pressure.

Glamsterdam being postponed is another pain factor here: considering the poor state of the market and Ethereum's struggle, it's clear that any delays in major updates negatively affect the network outlook. The new date is yet to be confirmed.

Vitalik Buterin has been hinting at the change in gas consumption for ages now. Back in 2024, he called multidimensional gas the hardest problem in his own post on the topic.

In a recent development, setting strict limits was never a farsighted option, and developers have been told that for years. However, it's yet another question: who's actually to blame? Buterin himself admitted that this rule hasn't been written down or repeated since 2021, so newer developers simply didn't know about it.

He now suggests writing down a list of features that are likely to change, from gas mechanics to slot time.

Meta is reportedly experimenting with a prediction game for employees in which participants forecast outcomes using points rather than real money. That may sound like a small internal product test, but it offers an interesting window into how large technology companies are thinking about forecasting, social engagement and the mechanics behind prediction markets.

The essential distinction is that a points-based game is not automatically a cash-settled financial market. No public launch or real-money service has been confirmed in the reporting on the experiment, so it would be misleading to describe Meta as having entered the regulated betting or event-contract business.

Sources indicate that the Block, citing The Wall Street Journal, reported that Meta was testing an employee application known as Takes, previously called Arena. Participants can make forecasts and earn or lose an internal points balance referred to as cred. The structure resembles a prediction market in some respects, but without the same money flows or legal arrangements as a traded contract.

It has been revealed that an internal trial can help answer useful product questions. Do people enjoy making forecasts? How should results be scored? Does a ranking system reward genuine insight or simply encourage attention-grabbing guesses? Those questions matter whether the eventual outcome is a staff game, a public social feature or nothing at all. The existence of a test does not establish which direction Meta will choose.

It has been revealed that real-money prediction markets can involve financial risk, market manipulation concerns, customer eligibility, settlement disputes and questions about gambling or derivatives law. A points-based contest may avoid some of those features, depending on its design. But a game can still have integrity problems if employees feel encouraged to trade on private information or if forecasts become workplace performance signals.

There is also a difference between a prediction with a numerical score and a security or derivative. Those categories are shaped by contract terms and applicable law, not simply by whether the interface looks like a market. Readers should be cautious when comparing an internal staff experiment directly with companies offering event contracts to paying customers.

Recent findings suggest that regulated prediction markets are attracting scrutiny from federal and state authorities, particularly around sports-related contracts. NewsBTC previously examined a CFTC-related lawsuit involving Coinbase and Kalshi, an example of how disputes over jurisdiction can arise as firms offer products that do not fit neatly into traditional categories.

It has been revealed that that uncertainty makes Meta's use of non-cash points noteworthy. A platform can learn about user participation and forecasting behaviour without immediately building the custody, settlement and compliance systems required for real-money products. Whether that is the strategic reason for the design has not been established; it is simply a material distinction between the two models.

Massive companies routinely trial features that never reach the public. Employee feedback can reveal problems early, and an internal rename does not by itself mean a product is ready for commercial deployment. Similarly, parallels with AI-agent payment experiments covered by NewsBTC show how companies use small tests to explore unfamiliar transaction designs before the market is settled.

Industry observers note that the next meaningful development would be an official description of the experiment's objectives, product scope or possible external release. Until then, Takes is best understood as a reported internal forecasting test — an interesting sign of curiosity, but not evidence that Meta has introduced a new exchange.

Tech Report: Bitcoin’s Biggest Options Bet Just Flipped — Is a Major Price Reversal Coming?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/bitcoins-biggest-options-bet-just-flipped-is-a-major-price-reversal-coming/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that bitcoin traders are facing an unusual situation.
  • In a recent development, the development comes after Bitcoin’s latest correction pushed the cryptocurrency toward its lowest levels in months.
  • Now, with traders increasingly focused on downside protection, an vital question is emerging: Could the market’s defensive positioning eventually create the conditions for an unexpected Bitcoin recovery?

Recent findings suggest that bitcoin traders are facing an unusual situation. A massive $900 million options position has emerged as the largest on Deribit, but the real surprise is where that position sits: $60,000.

In a recent development, the development comes after Bitcoin’s latest correction pushed the cryptocurrency toward its lowest levels in months. As we recently reported, Bitcoin briefly fell below $63,000, before recovering above $64,000.

Now, with traders increasingly focused on downside protection, an vital question is emerging: Could the market’s defensive positioning eventually create the conditions for an unexpected Bitcoin recovery?

Bitcoin’s $60,000 put options have overtaken the previously dominant $100,000 calls on Deribit, reaching approximately $900 million in notional open interest.

The $100,000 calls, meanwhile, have fallen to roughly $867 million.

This reversal is particularly interesting because the two contracts represent very different market expectations.

Call options provide exposure to potential price increases, while put options can be used to profit from declines or protect existing Bitcoin holdings.

However, the change does not necessarily mean investors suddenly placed $900 million in fresh bearish bets.

Open interest measures outstanding contracts accumulated over time. The decline in $100,000 call positions also reflects traders reducing earlier bullish exposure.

Investors can monitor the latest positioning through Deribit’s official options statistics.

The shift highlights how the options market has become increasingly defensive, even as Bitcoin continues attracting long-term institutional interest.

From a technical perspective, the $60,000 region deserves close attention.

Bitcoin recently declined toward $62,000 before staging a partial recovery, suggesting buyers remain active around the lower end of the current trading range.

However, a temporary bounce is not the same as a confirmed bullish reversal.

The first important area to monitor is the recent $62,000 low. Holding above this region would suggest that buyers are attempting to establish a short-term base.

A move above $65,000 could provide an initial sign of improving momentum, while a sustained recovery toward $68,000–$70,000 would offer a more meaningful test of overhead resistance.

The 50-period and 200-period exponential moving averages are also important.

If Bitcoin reclaims both indicators while the RSI moves above 50, the technical outlook could begin improving.

Conversely, a sustained breakdown below $62,000 would increase the risk of another test of the psychologically important $60,000 level.

These are potential scenarios, not confirmed breakout signals.

The most interesting possibility is that defensive market positioning could eventually help amplify a recovery.

When sentiment becomes heavily bearish, an unexpected rise in Bitcoin’s price can force leveraged short sellers to close their positions.

This process, known as a short squeeze, can accelerate upward momentum.

Bitcoinist recently examined how an analyst is buying Bitcoin during the correction, highlighting the possibility that improving liquidity and market structure could support a recovery.

However, put-option open interest should not be confused with short futures positions. Large put holdings alone do not demonstrate that a short squeeze is imminent.

Another notable factor is the recent wave of liquidations.

As previously covered, Bitcoin’s market sell-off triggered over $1.6 billion in liquidations, removing substantial leveraged exposure from the cryptocurrency market.

Such events can intensify short-term volatility, but they can also reduce excessive leverage.

The options market is sending an important signal: traders are increasingly concerned about protecting their positions.

Nevertheless, the $900 million concentration around $60,000 does not guarantee another major decline.

For now, we believe Bitcoin’s ability to hold above its recent lows will be critical.

A recovery through $65,000, followed by stronger volume and improving momentum indicators, could begin challenging the current bearish narrative.

If buyers eventually reclaim $68,000–$70,000, attention could shift toward whether the latest correction has established a sustainable bottom.

The $60,000 options position may be dominating headlines, but Bitcoin’s next decisive move will ultimately depend on spot demand, liquidity, and whether buyers can regain control of the trend.

#705. Tech Report: Brazil Takes Aim at Stablecoins With Shocking Money Laundering Claim

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 2 min read (495 words)

Tech Report: Brazil Takes Aim at Stablecoins With Shocking Money Laundering Claim

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read | Sumber: https://u.today/brazil-takes-aim-at-stablecoins-with-shocking-money-laundering-claim

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.
  • The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.
  • According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

The head of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil has claimed that legitimately obtained money could be considered laundered if it’s used to purchase stablecoins.

The senior Brazilian official claimed that converting money into stablecoins could link it to money laundering, even when it was initially obtained legally.

According to a recent report, Gerson Romantini, who is the director of the foreign exchange department at the Central Bank of Brazil, allegedly made the controversial statements at a private event attended by representatives of financial companies.

Romantini claimed that funds acquired legally could be transformed once they enter the stablecoin ecosystem.

In his view, even legally obtained money could effectively be "dirtied" if used in certain stablecoin schemes, and thus be considered part of a money laundering operation.

It’s crucial to note that the comments attributed to Romantini do not represent an official statement that all conversions into stablecoins could be considered money laundering.

This statement comes as Brazil has already moved to tighten restrictions on how cryptocurrencies are used for international payments.

Industry observers note that on April 30, the Central Bank of Brazil published Resolution No. 561, which took effect on Oct. 1.

The resolution limits the use of virtual assets for the settlement of international payment and transfer services, also known as eFX.

In practice, this means that payments between an eFX provider and its foreign partner must be settled through traditional foreign exchange operations or a Brazilian real account opened by nonresidents.

Crypto payments for these particular settlements are off-limits.

A practice called the "stablecoin sandwich" is particularly concerning.

The way it works is that a Brazilian fintech accepts a certain amount of reais from a customer, then uses this money to purchase stablecoins like USDT or USDC and sends the funds in crypto to an offshore tech giant.

This firm, in turn, can convert these stablecoins into fiat currency to make payments or send money to families.

This allows people to make international money transfers for a lower fee and circumvent some of the infrastructure banks use.

The controversial statements have already received a response from Brazil’s crypto industry.

In a statement on Nov. 14, the Brazilian Association of Tokenization and Digital Assets (ABToken) questioned the alleged classification of stablecoin transactions as money laundering.

ABToken maintains that the use of stablecoins is not necessarily illegal.

Furthermore, the association also cautioned that sweeping bans may create legal confusion and hinder legitimate business activities that use stablecoins for international payments.

With influential Silicon Valley figures reportedly supporting his comeback, investors are watching whether the leadership uncertainty could influence Nvidia’s stock and broader risk appetite, including Bitcoin.

The discussions reportedly follow efforts by supporters in Silicon Valley to persuade the manufacturer’s board to reconsider his departure.

One supporter reportedly described plans to assemble a group of technology executives to advocate for Huang’s reinstatement and seek support from the White House.

The developments represent an unexpected turn for Nvidia, which announced Huang’s resignation on November 12 and appointed Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress as interim CEO.

Huang’s departure followed reports concerning his personal relationships and questions about the tech giant’s China-related business dealings. Nvidia’s board had previously unveiled an independent investigation into concerns involving a possible foreign intelligence effort.

Ethereum price is approaching another notable technical turning point as co-founder Vitalik Buterin expresses renewed optimism about a proposal that could accelerate the network’s transition toward quantum-resistant cryptography.

The development has attracted attention across the cryptocurrency community, raising questions about whether Ethereum’s improving long-term technological outlook could eventually support stronger demand for ETH.

The announcement comes as Ethereum continues navigating a challenging market environment. As we recently reported, Ethereum whales are buying the dip, with large holders accumulating ETH around important support levels. This activity could become particularly significant if buyers regain control of short-term momentum.

On November 16, Buterin shared a detailed explanation of leanPCS, a cryptographic approach associated with Ethereum Improvement Proposal 8288.

His comments marked a significant change in his assessment of the technology.

Over the past few weeks I’ve gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull.

Buterin explained that Ethereum faces an important technical challenge as it prepares to adopt quantum-resistant cryptography.

Industry observers note that traditional Ethereum transaction signatures are relatively small. However, quantum-resistant signatures and advanced cryptographic proofs can require significantly more data, potentially increasing network costs.

According to the official Ethereum EIP-8288 proposal, the proposed architecture would aggregate cryptographic signatures and proofs into a single recursive STARK, potentially reducing the data requirements associated with quantum-resistant transactions.

The approach could eventually support more efficient transactions, stronger cryptographic security, and greater flexibility for developers.

However, EIP-8288 remains a draft proposal. Its potential benefits have not yet been deployed across Ethereum’s mainnet.

While Buterin’s comments provide a potentially encouraging long-term development, Ethereum’s immediate price outlook depends on whether buyers can regain control of the market.

The $2,000 region represents an notable psychological threshold, particularly after the cryptocurrency’s recent weakness.

Recent analysis of Ethereum’s accumulation trend highlights another crucial development: the share of ETH held in staking has reached record levels, suggesting continued commitment among long-term holders.

A sustained recovery above $2,000 would be an encouraging initial signal, but traders should also examine the four-hour chart for confirmation.

The 50-period exponential moving average can help identify changes in short-term momentum, while the 200-period EMA provides a broader view of the prevailing trend.

If ETH moves above both indicators and successfully retests them as support, the recovery scenario would become more convincing.

However, if the price remains below these moving averages, upward movements could represent temporary relief rallies rather than a confirmed trend reversal.

The Relative Strength Index (RSI) provides another notable signal.

A sustained move above 50 would suggest improving momentum, particularly if accompanied by stronger trading volume. Conversely, an RSI reading below 50 would indicate that sellers still retain an advantage.

For now, traders should prioritize confirmation rather than assuming that positive technological developments will immediately translate into higher prices.

Nevertheless, the cryptocurrency’s next major move will depend on whether buyers can establish stronger technical momentum.

We believe the combination of Ethereum’s continuing development and improving price structure could create a more favorable environment for ETH over time.

Industry observers note that lighter has suspended crypto withdrawals after a suspected security breach drained $15.5 million from two market-maker accounts. Its LIT token fell more than 15% as traders assessed the damage.

In a recent development, the decentralized perpetual futures exchange halted withdrawals and fresh liquidity pool creation on November 16. The incident reportedly involved compromised API keys belonging to two market makers, rather than a vulnerability in Lighter’s core smart contracts.

It has been revealed that upgrade: Our investigation indicates that today’s incident was caused by a leaked API key for a specific trader's account. The Lighter protocol and smart contracts are unaffected.As a precaution, we have enabled Guardian mode on our smart contract. Our main priority is to… https://t.co/LUuFiY5cK0.

On-chain investigators identified a $10.39 million USDC withdrawal from Lighter’s Ethereum settlement contract. Another $5.09 million loss was reported from a second account, although investigators had not independently verified that amount leaving the platform.

The incident has raised fresh questions about security across decentralized derivatives platforms, particularly how exchanges protect large trading accounts and their liquidity infrastructure.

The suspected attacker reportedly gained access to API keys associated with two market-maker accounts. These credentials allegedly provided enough permissions to manipulate their trading positions and liquidity pool activity.

It has been revealed that the reported losses were split between two accounts, with $10.39 million and $5.09 million in USDC taken from their respective balances. The alleged attack involved closing existing positions before creating a zero-fee liquidity pool under a compromised account. Attacker purchased nearly all its shares, transferred the victim’s funds into the pool, and redeemed those shares.

Sources indicate that bitquery independently tracked the first major withdrawal through Ethereum. The attacker converted $10.36 million in USDC into ETH within four minutes.

LIVE: tracking the Lighter hack walletAs of 11:36 UTC, 16 Nov:• 10.39M USDC out of @Lighter_xyz → 5,764 ETH• 10 payments of 160 ETH → Hyperliquid → 5,583 XMR1• 4,165 ETH still in the walletWe update as it moves:https://t.co/NZvBlmMEeP https://t.co/JcD3AOQ8Bs.

The wallet received 5,764 ETH, subsequently distributing 960 ETH across six fresh wallets. Those wallets moved funds through Hyperliquid and purchased XMR1, while approximately 4,805 ETH remained in the original wallet during Bitquery’s investigation.

Lighter initially described this crypto incident as involving a compromised external party. It suspended withdrawals and new liquidity pool creation while investigating the breach.

The team subsequently clarified that its protocol and smart contracts were not compromised. Instead, the incident reportedly originated from a leaked API key belonging to a specific trader.

As of now, Lighter activated Guardian mode on its smart contracts and revealed aims to upgrade its contracts through its Security Committee. The exchange also identified recovering funds associated with additional withdrawal attempts as a priority. Its stated target was completing the upgrade and restoring withdrawals by the end of November 16.

LIT traders now face another question: whether the exchange can restore withdrawals quickly enough to prevent a prolonged confidence crisis.

Lighter builds its derivatives ecosystem around Ethereum, while ASTER taps into BNB Chain and Hyperliquid operates its own blockchain. Bitcoin, meanwhile, still has considerable room to develop its decentralized derivatives infrastructure.

It has been revealed that the idea is to bring more sophisticated DeFi applications to Bitcoin, potentially including decentralized perpetual futures trading. According to recent reports, the project also has a live testnet featuring a bridge, faucet, explorer, and wallet infrastructure. Its roadmap targets further development of its Bitcoin bridge and DeFi ecosystem.

November 26 is the presale closing date, putting the token’s next major launch milestone just days away. So, for those watching the next generation of decentralized derivatives, Bitcoin’s potential role in that market remains an interesting opportunity.

Bitcoin Hyper is betting that combining Bitcoin’s liquidity with Solana-style execution can help establish that missing infrastructure.

Recent findings suggest that lighter’s immediate challenge is restoring withdrawals and demonstrating that its security upgrades address the vulnerabilities exposed by the incident. The coming sessions could prove decisive as traders monitor withdrawal availability, recovery efforts, and further disclosures from the exchange.

Two of the industry’s most influential figures are pushing back against very different concerns. Binance co-founder Changpeng Zhao, known as CZ, has rejected accusations that the exchange sold crypto during the latest market crash. Meanwhile, Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin is backing a faster approach to protecting the network against future quantum computing threats.

Their comments arrive as crypto suffers a sharp correction, leveraged traders absorb billions in liquidations, and Ethereum developers reconsider how swiftly the network should prepare for a post-quantum future.

Changpeng Zhao has directly rejected speculation that Binance contributed to the latest cryptocurrency sell-off by selling digital assets.

“No, Binance did not sell crypto,” CZ wrote in a post on X.

Instead, the former Binance CEO stated he had personally been buying crypto after receiving stablecoins over the past few days.

His response came as Bitcoin plunged toward $62,000, marking its lowest level since July. The wider market experienced approximately $2.02 billion in liquidations over a 24-hour period, with long positions accounting for $1.68 billion.

CZ also offered several possible explanations for the market weakness, including institutional ETF outflows, expectations of another Federal Reserve rate hike, security concerns, and investors potentially moving capital toward Anthropic’s anticipated IPO.

Why are crypto prices down?No one knows for sure. Correlation does not prove causation. Here are some potential reasons.Money shifting to the Anthropic IPO: https://t.co/jYwVi4huAYETF outflows: U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs saw about $1.9 billion in outflows over seven trading… pic.twitter.com/XL2aB1ZL9W.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs recorded $1.91 billion in net outflows across seven consecutive trading sessions through November 13. Spot Ether ETFs also suffered $398.9 million in weekly withdrawals.

The Binance selling allegations carry particular weight following the exchange’s October 29 security breach, but CZ public denial provides a clear counterargument to speculation that exchange selling accelerated the market decline.

His personal buying comments also show that he sees the current weakness differently from traders rushing to exit their positions. Defending the exchange’s reputation during a period of market stress is becoming just as notable as explaining the direction of crypto prices.

While CZ is addressing immediate market concerns, Vitalik Buterin is looking much further ahead.

The Ethereum co-founder has dramatically changed his assessment of leanPCS, a proposed cryptographic technique designed to make Ethereum more resistant to quantum computing attacks.

“Over the past few weeks I’ve gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull,” Buterin wrote on X.

Over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data….

The statement indicates growing confidence in an approach that could help Ethereum introduce quantum-resistant cryptography without dramatically increasing transaction costs and blockchain storage requirements.

It has been revealed that the proposal, outlined in EIP-8288, focuses on combining individual digital signatures and cryptographic proofs into a shared mathematical proof. This is good for Ethereum because quantum-resistant signatures can be considerably larger than the cryptographic signatures Ethereum presently uses.

Industry observers note that A standard Ethereum signature occupies approximately 65 bytes. Some proposed quantum-resistant alternatives could require between 1,000 and 6,000 bytes. Storing those larger signatures individually could consume substantial block space, potentially increasing network costs.

LeanPCS attempts to solve that problem by allowing computers to aggregate multiple signatures and verification checks before submitting a compact proof to Ethereum. Rather than permanently storing every bulky signature individually, the network could verify a shared proof covering multiple transactions.

Buterin favors this approach because it could provide a practical route toward quantum resistance without requiring Ethereum to commit immediately to a much larger architectural redesign.

Ethereum’s quantum preparation is already underway, with the Ethereum Foundation targeting 2029 for core post-quantum infrastructure milestones. The potential threat remains years away, but Ethereum developers increasingly recognize that replacing cryptographic foundations requires considerable preparation.

Sources indicate that CZ and Buterin are confronting different problems, but both developments highlight the pressures facing the crypto industry. Binance needs to maintain market confidence while investors question exchange activity, security, and institutional capital flows.

Ethereum needs to strengthen its cryptographic foundations before quantum computing potentially threatens the security assumptions underlying today’s blockchain infrastructure.

CZ’s comments offer reassurance during an immediate market downturn, while Buterin’s endorsement could accelerate an important technical discussion within Ethereum.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Researchers say attackers compromised scripts delivered through Optimizely, exposing visitors to malware designed to replace crypto wallet addresses and steal payment card details.
  • Major global brands including Ledger, Salesforce and BBC served cryptocurrency and credit card-stealing malware to website visitors on Monday, in a major attack exploiting website optimization platform Optimizely, according to security researchers.
  • Dubbed “Optimjack” by researcher Amirul Iman, the campaign delivered malicious code through scripts hosted by Optimizely.

Researchers say attackers compromised scripts delivered through Optimizely, exposing visitors to malware designed to replace crypto wallet addresses and steal payment card details.

Major global brands including Ledger, Salesforce and BBC served cryptocurrency and credit card-stealing malware to website visitors on Monday, in a major attack exploiting website optimization platform Optimizely, according to security researchers.

Dubbed “Optimjack” by researcher Amirul Iman, the campaign delivered malicious code through scripts hosted by Optimizely. The malware can replace legitimate cryptocurrency wallet addresses with attacker-controlled alternatives when visitors copy addresses. It also captured credit card details entered into website forms, according to a separate analysis by cybersecurity firm StepSecurity.

The campaign affected website scripts belonging to 178 organizations, including hardware wallet Ledger, OANDA / Coinpass and trading platforms IG, Interactive Investor and TMS Brokers, according to Report URI’s investigation. Other affected brands included IKEA, Salesforce, Zoom, the BBC and CNN, websites that collectively attract millions of visitors a day.

BBC was among the first websites observed to serve the Optimizely injection at around 4:21 am UTC on Monday. By 9:52 pm UTC, most of the malicious code had been removed, with Ledger’s snippet cleaned at about 8:41 pm UTC.

Cointelegraph reached out to Ledger, Coinpass, and a number of other major businesses reported to be impacted by the malicious injection.

This is a developing story, more information will be added as it becomes available.

Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It.
  • Alibaba released Qwen 4 Max on Monday, its most powerful AI model yet and the first flagship built on its new Qwen 4 architecture.
  • It is also the highest-ranked Chinese model on Arena's agent leaderboard, putting the organization ahead of Tencent, Moonshot AI and DeepSeek in that particular test.

Alibaba's Qwen 4 Max Leads China's AI Agent Race—But You Can't Download It.

Alibaba released Qwen 4 Max on Monday, its most powerful AI model yet and the first flagship built on its new Qwen 4 architecture.

It is also the highest-ranked Chinese model on Arena's agent leaderboard, putting the organization ahead of Tencent, Moonshot AI and DeepSeek in that particular test.

Sources indicate that the upcoming model has 2.4 trillion parameters, can process text, images and video, and accepts up to one million tokens of context. Parameters are all the different dials a model can handle and tweak when processing information. Tokens are basically the smallest unit of information a model can handle. Its current configuration is enough room for lengthy codebases or stacks of documents.

Industry observers note that alibaba uses a mixture-of-experts design, which keeps most of those parameters idle for any given word it processes. Qwen 4 Max activates 71 billion at a time, compared with 95 billion for Qwen 3.8 Max, allowing a very large model to use less computing power per token.

On Agent Arena, Qwen 4 Max placed 14th among individual models and made Alibaba the fifth-ranked laboratory overall.

Industry observers note that the leaderboard evaluates real agent sessions using task completion, user satisfaction and how well models respond to corrections, then scores each model by its net percentage improvement over an average competitor. Qwen 4 Max posted a preliminary 7.46% score across 14,727 sessions, the highest among Chinese entries.

Its visual work may be the more interesting part for regular owners. The Code Arena web-development ranking compares websites built by AI models using head-to-head user votes and a points-based rating system. Qwen 4 Max debuted sixth globally at 1,750 points, up 74 from its predecessor, and placed eighth in categories for branding and reference-based design.

That puts it in the same neighborhood as the best American models at turning a request, a screenshot or a rough idea into a working interface that actually looks good.

Alibaba's demos go further, showing the model building game environments and translating factory layouts into 3D models, although those are company-selected examples rather than independent tests.

Recent findings suggest that the visual capability is for understanding images and video and producing code or other text-based outputs. It is not the same as releasing a fresh image generator.

Recent findings suggest that qwen 4 Max costs $1.50 per million input tokens and $4.50 per million generated tokens through QwenCloud, a 25% reduction from the previous flagship's $2 and $6 rates. Reused input served from an automatic cache costs $0.075 per million tokens, which can make repetitive workflows substantially cheaper.

Sources indicate that alibaba notes its internal testing across hundreds of professional specialties found that the model used 35% fewer tokens and reduced average task costs by roughly 60% compared with Qwen 3.8 Max. In other words, it should be cheaper to execute tasks on this model even against competitors with a similar price..

The bigger limitation for the community is that Qwen 4 Max is closed-weight. Developers can use it through an API or Alibaba's apps, but they cannot download its internal parameters, modify it or run it privately on their own hardware.

According to recent reports, qwen has become a foundation for the open-model ecosystem. An August report from Hugging Face counted 151,448 Qwen-based derivative models on its platform, about 4.7 times the number built specifically on Meta's Llama family. Those include community fine-tunes and optimized versions that power local assistants and specialized tools.

Industry observers note that alibaba opened the weights of Qwen 3.8 Max earlier this year, despite having kept some previous Max models proprietary. It also previewed elements of the Qwen 4 architecture with smaller models months before Monday's release.

The launch lands in a crowded Chinese race. Moonshot's Kimi K3 pushed enormous open-weight models toward Western performance, while DeepSeek has been competing hard on API prices.

Industry observers note that qwen 4 Max leads some Chinese rankings, but American labs still hold the top spots in Arena's overall agent and web-development tables. They are also considerably more expensive.

Alibaba says smaller Qwen 4 models will be released with open weights, giving developers a chance to build on this generation rather than simply rent its biggest model. It has not confirmed their sizes or release dates.

Custodia Bank loses Supreme Court bid for direct Fed payment access

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://cointelegraph.com/news/custodia-bank-loses-supreme-court-bid-for-direct-fed-payment-access?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Supreme Court refused to hear Custodia Bank’s appeal, meaning a lower court ruling allowing the Fed to reject account applications will stand.
  • The United States Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear an appeal from crypto-focused bank Custodia, effectively ending the bank’s latest legal effort to gain direct access to the Federal Reserve’s payment system.
  • Custodia is a Wyoming-chartered bank founded by Caitlin Long.

The Supreme Court refused to hear Custodia Bank’s appeal, meaning a lower court ruling allowing the Fed to reject account applications will stand.

The United States Supreme Court on Monday declined to hear an appeal from crypto-focused bank Custodia, effectively ending the bank’s latest legal effort to gain direct access to the Federal Reserve’s payment system.

Custodia is a Wyoming-chartered bank founded by Caitlin Long. The bank has been trying for a Fed master account since 2020, which would allow it to process payments directly without relying on third-party financial institutions.

Now, the Supreme Court’s Monday decision means an earlier ruling allowing the Fed to reject applications from eligible banks will remain in effect.

According to recent reports, the case highlights some of the challenges crypto-facing banks face in gaining direct access to the US payment system. Still, even if state-chartered banks qualify for master accounts, the Fed does not have to approve every application.

In a dissent issued in March, US Circuit Judge Timothy Tymkovich criticized the appeals court’s decision to give Federal Reserve banks discretion over master accounts.

“Without a master account, a bank cannot operate in the modern banking system,” Tymkovich wrote, arguing that the ruling effectively gives the Fed the power to override state banking decisions.

Custodia first sued the Federal Reserve in 2022 after waiting around two years for a decision on its master account application. The Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City ended up rejecting the request in January 2023, citing concerns about risks linked to the bank’s crypto-focused business model.

In October 2025, a federal appeals court ruled against Custodia, finding that Federal Reserve banks did not have to grant master accounts to every eligible institution.

Related: Crypto among sectors ‘debanked’ by 9 major banks: US regulator.

Cointelegraph previously reported that the court declined to reconsider its decision in March. This led Custodia to take its case to the Supreme Court.

The bank’s appeal also received support from the Blockchain Association, which argued that the Fed’s ability to reject applications could weaken the authority of state banking regulators.

Senator Cynthia Lummis and former Senator Patrick Toomey also filed a brief with the Supreme Court in August, supporting Custodia’s appeal.

Industry observers note that today’s decision comes as other crypto-focused banks seek access to the Fed’s payment system. In March, Kraken Financial received approval for a restricted account from the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City — the same regional bank that rejected Custodia’s application.

Notably, Kraken’s account was approved for an initial one-year period and allows it to send and receive payments through the Fed’s Fedwire system. However, the account has restrictions and does not offer all the services of a full master account.

Looking ahead, Custodia may still be able to apply for another master account or seek limited access to the Fed’s payment system under a separate proposal.

#740. German lawmakers back crypto freezes outside criminal cases

German lawmakers back crypto freezes outside criminal cases

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://cointelegraph.com/news/german-lawmakers-back-crypto-freezes-outside-criminal-cases?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Customs authorities could hold “suspicious” assets for 30 days under the bill, with court oversight for extensions and disputed confiscation.
  • Germany’s lower house of parliament has passed a bill that would let customs authorities temporarily freeze cryptocurrency and other high-value assets suspected of having unlawful origins without first opening a criminal investigation.
  • The Bundestag passed the customs reform bill on Friday as part of a wider effort to combat money laundering and organized crime.

Customs authorities could hold “suspicious” assets for 30 days under the bill, with court oversight for extensions and disputed confiscation.

Germany’s lower house of parliament has passed a bill that would let customs authorities temporarily freeze cryptocurrency and other high-value assets suspected of having unlawful origins without first opening a criminal investigation.

The Bundestag passed the customs reform bill on Friday as part of a wider effort to combat money laundering and organized crime. The proposed procedure would target assets worth more than 100,000 euros and explicitly mentions cryptocurrencies.

In a recent development, under the bill’s text approved by lawmakers, authorities would be able to hold assets for up to 30 days where there are factual indications of unlawful origins, according to a translated version. However, filing an application for confiscation could suspend those deadlines pending a court decision, and in contested cases, a court would have to be satisfied that the assets were of unlawful origin before ordering confiscation, effectively putting the burden of proof on the crypto holder.

German Social Democratic Party lawmaker Ingo Vogel remarked that the powers would allow authorities to pursue suspicious assets even when there are not yet grounds to open a criminal case, according to the Bundestag’s summary of the debate on the bill.

The bill still requires consent from the Bundesrat, Germany’s upper house of parliament, and is intended to take effect on Jan. 1, 2027.

Germany’s Federal Bar Association, known as BRAK, previously opposed the government’s draft in an Oct. 28 statement, warning that the meaning of unlawful origin is too vague and risks treating missing records as evidence of illicit wealth.

The association pointed to assets inherited through generations as one example where owners may lack a paper trail. It also questioned what the administrative process would add to Germany’s existing criminal confiscation rules.

Industry observers note that german blockchain industry association Bundesblock also raised concerns about the treatment of digital assets in a March 31 submission on an earlier draft. It warned at the time that blockchain analysis should not automatically be treated as proof of ownership or control, and that incorrect wallet attribution could even infringe fundamental rights.

Related: Crypto adoption blooming in Germany, while UK is falling ‘behind,’ says CoinShares researcher.

Germany has already carried out large crypto seizures under existing law. As Cointelegraph reported, Saxony authorities sold 49,858 Bitcoin (BTC) linked to the Movie2k piracy investigation in 2024, raising about 2.6 billion euros, or $2.8 billion. At the time, prosecutors mentioned the proceeds remained secured pending a court ruling on confiscation.

In a recent development, local outlet MDR reported on Friday that a Leipzig judge proposed ending proceedings against the main defendant in exchange for 40,000 BTC and a payment of 38 million euros for the potential victims. The proposal remains under consideration.

Industry News: Bitcoin Wallet Maker Trezor Notes Customer Data Was Exposed Again

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://decrypt.co/383397/bitcoin-wallet-trezor-third-party-breach-customer-data

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin Wallet Maker Trezor Says Customer Data Was Exposed Again.
  • The “days since last third-party breach” counter at Trezor has reset to zero once again.
  • This time, hackers accessed shipping partner Skladon's systems and likely exported information tied to approximately 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, according to a company disclosure published Monday.

Bitcoin Wallet Maker Trezor Says Customer Data Was Exposed Again.

The “days since last third-party breach” counter at Trezor has reset to zero once again.

This time, hackers accessed shipping partner Skladon's systems and likely exported information tied to approximately 27,000 hardware-wallet orders, according to a company disclosure published Monday.

The intrusion occurred November 7, but Skladon did not notify Trezor until November 15. The exposed records cover orders placed between August 9 and November 7, including customers' full names, phone numbers, delivery and email addresses, plus the products they bought and their prices.

In a recent development, trezor mentioned its own systems were not compromised, and no wallet backups, PINs or passphrases were involved. The breach does not, by itself, let an attacker move a buyer's coins, but it gives them a potentially dangerous combination: a home address and evidence that someone bought a device designed to store crypto.

The latest incident follows an August shipping partner hack and a September email provider breach, making three separate third-party security incidents in a little over three months.

According to recent reports, trezor said some customers have already reported fraudulent phone calls. Criminals could cite the exact model and price of a wallet to make an unsolicited call, text or letter seem legitimate, or use a home address to identify someone who may hold cryptocurrency.

In August, logistics provider ShipMonk suffered a breach that initially appeared to affect fewer than 14,000 Trezor customers. An updated investigation uncovered records for another 67,000 U.S. buyers from 2019 to 2021 that ShipMonk had retained despite assurances they had been deleted, bringing the total to 80,689 people.

Sources indicate that september brought another incident, this time at marketing email provider Brevo. Hackers used Trezor's legitimate email channel to distribute a fake security warning urging recipients to install an app that requested their wallet backups. Trezor later said 347,149 email addresses had been exported.

Recent findings suggest that these weren't Trezor's first brushes with the problem. A Mailchimp insider attack targeted Trezor users in 2022, and a 2024 breach of its external support portal put the contact details of up to 66,000 people at risk.

It has been revealed that the fallout can go beyond inbox spam. In February, fake letters were sent to hardware-wallet owners, complete with Trezor branding, holograms and QR codes leading to phishing sites.

Recent findings suggest that asked why an order from Trezor's official store involved an outside tech giant, Trezor responded that it’s basically a logistics question, not a tech glitch. “Companies of our size and global reach can’t run efficiently without third-party service providers,” the company replied to a comment on X.

It has been revealed that hi, companies of our size and global reach can’t run efficiently without third-party service providers. Handling as much as possible internally is the goal, but doing every part of the business ourselves isn’t realistic. Skladon is one of the partners that delivers Trezor orders,….

It remarked Skladon held only the information needed to deliver parcels, and handling every stage of global distribution in-house was not realistic.

Trezor states Skladon does not ship to the United States, so American buyers were not affected by this incident. Affected customers have been notified where possible, though some people who ordered between August 9 and 14 may not receive an email because Trezor had already anonymized their records.

The company has introduced anonymous pickup at parcel lockers or collection points in 18 European countries, allowing buyers to avoid supplying a home address. It is also working to shorten retention of order data from 90 to 45 days and says shipping partners will have to follow the same policy.

Trezor advises customers to ignore unexpected calls and messages about their orders, check any concerns through its official support site and never share a wallet backup. It has notified a data protection authority, but has not yet disclosed how attackers got into Skladon's systems.

Binance hack may push institutions to outside custody, FalconX exec claims

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://cointelegraph.com/news/binance-hack-institutional-crypto-custody-falconx?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound

💡 Key Takeaways
  • FalconX’s Joshua Lim claims the Binance hack could push institutions to keep crypto off exchanges and change how large investors trade in 2027.
  • A major shift in institutional crypto trading could be on the horizon following the recent Binance hack, as security concerns may lead to more large investors keeping their assets outside exchanges, according to a FalconX executive.
  • Recent findings suggest that in an exclusive interview with Cointelegraph at the Digital Asset Forum in New York City on Nov.

FalconX’s Joshua Lim claims the Binance hack could push institutions to keep crypto off exchanges and change how large investors trade in 2027.

A major shift in institutional crypto trading could be on the horizon following the recent Binance hack, as security concerns may lead to more large investors keeping their assets outside exchanges, according to a FalconX executive.

Recent findings suggest that in an exclusive interview with Cointelegraph at the Digital Asset Forum in New York City on Nov. 13, Joshua Lim, global head of markets at FalconX, a digital asset brokerage for institutional investors, said the Oct. 29 hack could make institutions more cautious about trading crypto and change how they store their assets.

“It’s actually quite bearish for more institutional participation in crypto,” Lim told Cointelegraph. He said traders initially played down the hack but later began to recognize its potential long-term impact.

As a result, Lim expects more institutions to turn to outside custody providers and trading firms that allow them to trade without keeping their crypto on exchanges, a shift he believes could become one of the biggest trends in 2027.

North Korean-linked hackers stole about $6.4 billion in cryptocurrency from Binance, making it the largest crypto theft on record, according to blockchain analytics firm Chainalysis.

The shift toward keeping crypto outside exchanges already appeared to be underway even before the hack. In an October proposal, the US Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) said industry practices were developing that reduced the need to move investment advisers’ client assets and regulated funds’ crypto holdings out of permitted custody for trading.

Lim pointed to Copper, a crypto custody provider, as one organization that could benefit. Its ClearLoop service lets investors trade on supported exchanges while keeping their crypto with a separate company.

Copper said collateral protected by its ClearLoop service supported more than $240 billion in perpetual futures trading volume during the first quarter of 2026, more than double the amount a year earlier.

It has been revealed that lim explained that investors can keep their assets outside an exchange while receiving credited balances that allow them to trade on it. Under the brokerage model Lim described, a hedge fund can place trades through FalconX, which executes them using its own exchange accounts and relationships. Still, investors face risks tied to the firms holding their assets and settling their trades.

“For many players, facing a regulated entity like ours is more palatable,” Lim added.

Related: Crypto hack losses equal 57 cents per $1 earned onchain: Ark’s Valente.

Binance recorded large Bitcoin outflows in mid-November, although it is not clear whether they were linked to the hack.

According to CryptoQuant data, Binance recorded net withdrawals of about 2,771 Bitcoin (BTC) on Friday, followed by 2,708 BTC on Saturday and 5,636 BTC on Sunday — totaling about 11,115 BTC leaving the exchange than entered over those three days.

The withdrawals came as the broader crypto market was falling, with Bitcoin trading around $65,000 at 9:41 pm UTC Monday, down about 20% over the past month, according to CoinGecko.

Sources indicate that however, the data does not show who moved the Bitcoin or why. Investors could have transferred their funds to personal wallets, companies that store crypto on their behalf, or to other exchanges.

Beyond concerns about exchange security, Lim expects other changes in how large investors trade in 2027. He said institutions want more ways to trade assets such as oil, gold and stock market indexes through crypto platforms, including outside regular market hours.

“You can respond rapidly to news events when they happen,” Lim noted, citing one of the benefits of 24/7 trading.

Sources indicate that that type of trading is already taking place on Hyperliquid, a decentralized trading platform that offers contracts tied to traditional assets. As of Monday, Hyperliquid’s markets for traditional assets and other contracts had about $4.3 billion in open interest and recorded $3.9 billion in trading volume over 24 hours, according to data from Perpys.

But while crypto platforms are giving investors more ways to trade, Lim said the financial services needed to support those trades have not kept up, particularly when it comes to borrowing money and managing risk.

For example, investors can now trade oil through traditional futures markets, investment funds and crypto platforms. But lenders may treat trades on each platform separately, even when those trades balance each other out.

“There’s not enough players that can give you leverage or margin financing against all of these things collectively,” Lim mentioned. “The risk netting is not quite there yet.”.

Bitcoin Lightning developers patch bug that could make completed payments disappear

💡 Key Takeaways
  • A software flaw could cause nodes to lose track of settled payment updates after restarting, threatening the integrity of Lightning channel records.
  • Bitcoin Lightning developers patched a software vulnerability that could cause nodes to lose track of settled payments after a restart, potentially disrupting the accounting records that secure payment channels.
  • The flaw affected LND, a widely used implementation of Bitcoin's Lightning Network, which enables owners to send Bitcoin through payment channels without recording every transaction directly on the blockchain.

A software flaw could cause nodes to lose track of settled payment updates after restarting, threatening the integrity of Lightning channel records.

Bitcoin Lightning developers patched a software vulnerability that could cause nodes to lose track of settled payments after a restart, potentially disrupting the accounting records that secure payment channels.

The flaw affected LND, a widely used implementation of Bitcoin's Lightning Network, which enables owners to send Bitcoin through payment channels without recording every transaction directly on the blockchain.

Sources indicate that developers released v0.21.8-beta and v0.20.8-beta on Nov. 11 to address the issue, which stemmed from an error in how the software saved and restored channel updates.

The vulnerability could cause a node to reconstruct incomplete payment records after restarting, even when the original information remained stored on its disk.

That failure threatened the consistency of Lightning channels, where participants rely on accurate records to determine which payments have settled and what each party is owed.

According to LND maintainer Olaoluwa Osuntokun, known as Roasbeef, the problem involved a counter that tracked acknowledged updates from a connected Lightning peer.

The software stored the number of entries using a 16-bit unsigned integer, which can represent values only up to 65,535.

Once the list reached 65,536 entries, the counter reset to zero, even though LND continued writing the updates to storage.

Upon restarting, the node could interpret that zero as an empty list and omit a previously settled hashed timelock contract (HTLC), a conditional payment mechanism that helps secure transactions across Lightning channels.

At 65,536 log entries, LND's old stored count could wrap to zero. The released patch adds write guards and checks older records on load.

Oversized lists are rejected before commitment progress or revocation, and before serialization writes record bytes.

The updated reader validates entries and count. It can recover qualifying complete lists; malformed trailing data is rejected.

The fix prevents new oversized logs and conditionally recovers complete older records.

Applies to this unsigned acknowledged enhancement log and its overflow condition. Complete legacy data must pass entry/count checks; malformed data is rejected. No observed exploitation or financial loss is established by the reviewed sources.

It has been revealed that schematic of the maintainer-described count/content mismatch and the released write and legacy-load checks. Geometry highlights control flow, not measured traffic or payment values. Selected states distinguish newly rejected oversized logs from conditional recovery of older records.

Industry observers note that applies to this unsigned acknowledged upgrade log and its overflow condition. Complete legacy data must pass entry/count checks; malformed data is rejected. No observed exploitation or financial loss is established by the reviewed sources.

The vulnerability became more concerning after developers identified a potential way for connected peers to push the affected patch list toward its limit.

In the GitHub discussion, LND collaborator ziggie1984 explained that a peer could repeatedly send transaction fee updates and commitment signatures while withholding a required revocation message.

That behavior allowed the list of pending acknowledgments to grow without being cleared.

The developer reproduced the behavior in a unit test, generating 201 stored updates after 200 rounds of messages.

Crucially, the accumulated entries survived reconnects, suggesting that repeatedly disconnecting and reconnecting would not necessarily prevent the list from eventually reaching the overflow threshold.

Recent findings suggest that the potential weakness matters because Lightning depends on both parties maintaining consistent payment-channel states. Losing track of a settled revision could undermine the records used to reconcile channel obligations.

However, the project's disclosures do not identify any confirmed exploitation or financial losses associated with the flaw.

To address the problem, developers introduced checks that prevent oversized enhancement lists from advancing the channel state or being written to storage.

They also modified how LND reads existing records, allowing nodes to recover complete enhancement lists saved by older versions when the underlying data passes validation.

Sources indicate that the fix was merged into LND's main development branch on Nov. 5 before being included in both November releases.
