💡 Key Takeaways
  • Johnson was joined by Lord Ross Kempsell who called for regulators to work with industry participants to bring the UK to the forefront.
  • Former United Kingdom Prime Minister Boris Johnson has backed blockchain technology and tokenization as opportunities for the UK’s financial sector, despite persistent doubts about cryptocurrencies.
  • Speaking at Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London on Monday, Johnson maintained his position that Bitcoin (BTC) resembles a Ponzi scheme, following an opinion piece published in the Daily Mail in March.

Johnson was joined by Lord Ross Kempsell who called for regulators to work with industry participants to bring the UK to the forefront.

Former United Kingdom Prime Minister Boris Johnson has backed blockchain technology and tokenization as opportunities for the UK’s financial sector, despite persistent doubts about cryptocurrencies.

Speaking at Solana’s Breakpoint conference in London on Monday, Johnson maintained his position that Bitcoin (BTC) resembles a Ponzi scheme, following an opinion piece published in the Daily Mail in March. He questioned who investors could hold accountable if funds were stolen.

However, Johnson distinguished his criticism of digital assets from his view of the underlying technology, saying the UK should be at the forefront of tokenization.

Lord Ross Kempsell, who joined Johnson on stage, said although he shared his reservations on cryptocurrencies, “on the parts of the industry that can be brought into a regulated perimeter, which the regulators are working on, there’s a lot of scope here for a high growth industry.”.

Kempsell, whom Johnson nominated for a peerage in 2022, told the panel that more than 8% of UK adults hold crypto, in line with Financial Conduct Authority-commissioned research published in December 2025. Speaking to Cointelegraph after his stage appearance, he said, “I’m a very big believer in making London and keeping London as the onchain capital for innovation.”.

Related: UK financial watchdog opens consultations for DeFi guidance, crypto laws.

Sources indicate that he argued that consumer protection and financial innovation should not be treated as competing priorities, pointing to the UK’s established fintech industry as an example of how regulation can coexist with innovation in the country. He remarked the UK should avoid introducing a single, all-encompassing piece of crypto legislation, opting instead for “a more ad-hoc approach” to regulation.

He called for collaboration between the regulators and market participants to understand both the risks and opportunities. While he saw consumer protection as “paramount,” he felt it was unfair to single out the crypto industry as the only sector where consumer protection was at risk.

It has been revealed that “Really what I care about is the economic growth potential that there is in this industry, the job creation potential, and also its wider links to tech, AI and traditional financial innovation. London’s always been at the center of those historically,” Kempsell told Cointelegraph.

When asked about the approach of the current administration in the UK, he highlighted that “they need to make sure that they get the fundamental market conditions right.” In his eyes, that meant making the UK a competitive player in regard to tax and facilitating business innovation.

Related: UK names 6 banks to lead first digitally native government bond.

Tim Meggs, co-founder of London-based digital asset trading firm Lo:Tech, noted Johnson “made a fair point about people getting burned,” but said most of the losses experienced by the industry stemmed from thin liquidity and a lack of visibility over how prices were made.

In a recent development, “If the FCA gets its perimeter right, the UK has a chance to make that kind of transparency the norm,” Meggs noted. “But until the clearing and prime broking infrastructure catches up, good rules won’t be enough on their own to make London the place where serious digital asset trading gets done.”.

Recent findings suggest that robin Nordnes, founder and CEO of Solana infrastructure firm Raiku, argued that Johnson’s question about who is in charge makes the case for blockchain, since a public ledger needs no guarantor. “Every transaction on Solana is public and can be checked by anyone, which is more than you can say for most of what happens in the City,” he said.

Nordnes warned that “if Westminster keeps treating this as retail speculation, the trading systems behind the next generation of markets will be built in Fresh York and Singapore, and London will end up renting them.”.

Bitcoin's $2 Billion Liquidation Weekend Leaves Traders Watching $60,000

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin's $2 Billion Liquidation Weekend Leaves Traders Watching $60,000.
  • Sources indicate that bitcoin fell to around $62,100 on Sunday as roughly $2 billion in crypto derivatives positions were forcibly closed, mostly bets that prices would rise.
  • Bitcoin had recovered to around $64,300 early Monday.

Bitcoin's $2 Billion Liquidation Weekend Leaves Traders Watching $60,000.

Sources indicate that bitcoin fell to around $62,100 on Sunday as roughly $2 billion in crypto derivatives positions were forcibly closed, mostly bets that prices would rise. The weekend slide sent the cryptocurrency to its lowest level since July 14, adding another ugly chapter to six consecutive weeks of losses.

Bitcoin had recovered to around $64,300 early Monday. But the options market is showing why traders aren't necessarily treating that bounce as an all-clear.

Liquidations happen when an exchange closes a trader's position because the money posted to support a borrowed bet is no longer enough to cover its losses. CoinGlass figures from Saturday indicated $1.9 billion liquidated in one 24-hour period, about $1.8 billion of it bullish positions across cryptocurrencies, not just Bitcoin.

U.S. spot Bitcoin ETFs had already been losing investors before the weekend. Data from Decrypt’s ETF tracker show $185.4 million in net outflows on Friday, extending their losing streak to seven trading sessions and bringing withdrawals since November 5 to approximately $1.91 billion.

Sources indicate that blackRock's IBIT accounted for $143.5 million of Friday's withdrawals, while Fidelity's FBTC lost $41.9 million. The funds' earlier weakness had helped explain the broader exodus, although ETF flow totals measure fund creations and redemptions rather than every trade between investors.

Those numbers also come with a timing distinction: U.S. ETFs do not trade over the weekend, while Bitcoin trades around the clock. Friday's outflows show weakened demand before the crash, not that ETF shareholders were redeeming shares during Sunday's plunge.

Bitcoin's technical indicators suggest the selling may be overstretched, but that doesn't necessarily mean the worst is over.

According to recent reports, the daily Relative Strength Index sat near 24 in oversold territory on the daily charts. Meanwhile, the Average Directional Index stood above 33, indicating a strong prevailing trend, with bearish directional pressure still dominating. The weekly RSI, near 38, pointed to a weak longer-term picture, although it had not reached oversold territory.

Recent findings suggest that the cryptocurrency bounced after approaching support around $62,000. A recovery would face potential resistance near $66,500 to $67,200, followed by another obstacle around $69,300, based on the chart's Fibonacci levels that measure support and resistance marks.

A decisive break below $62,000, meanwhile, would put the psychologically important $60,000 level back in focus—precisely where options traders have accumulated significant downside exposure.

Bitcoin's next test will be whether fresh U.S. ETF flow data show more withdrawals for Monday and whether traders keep paying for downside protection. The heavily watched November 27 options expiration is still ahead, with $50,000 puts among the contracts drawing the most recent trading activity.

Tech Report: Ripple's Schwartz Reveals Why XRP Ledger Used Satoshi's Code

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read | Sumber: https://u.today/ripples-schwartz-reveals-why-xrp-ledger-used-satoshis-code

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.
  • Recent findings suggest that in his Nov.
  • The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.

Ripple CTO emeritus David Schwartz has shared the reason the XRP Ledger (XRPL) used code and cryptography from Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto, in its early stages.

Recent findings suggest that in his Nov. 16 post on X, Schwartz remarked they primarily chose to do so for security reasons and to prevent backlash from the Bitcoin community when the XRP Ledger was still in its early development.

The conversation started when prominent XRPL validator Vet (@Vet_X0) pointed out how some of Satoshi Nakamoto's initial design decisions are still present in the XRP Ledger's structure.

Vet stated that the XRP Ledger initially used helper functions from the original Bitcoin software, including timekeeping functions coded by Satoshi Nakamoto himself.

Some of those helper functions were reportedly copied by Jed McCaleb, one of the early developers of the XRP Ledger. The original Bitcoin code even included a comment left by the mysterious creator of Bitcoin.

Afterward, Schwartz shared the reason why XRP Ledger developers opted to use the cryptographic options from Bitcoin instead of creating latest ones.

"We did things that way in the very early days because we didn't want to be potentially facing criticism that our choices for those core crypto functions were less secure than Bitcoin's," said Schwartz.

In other words, XRP Ledger developers opted to use Bitcoin's cryptographic options to avoid possible controversial security-related decisions when creating a new cryptocurrency network.

Later on, Vet asked Schwartz if their decision helped gain acceptance among Bitcoin supporters who looked at their protocol in its early stages.

Schwartz said it was hard to say whether it helped or not.

"It's hard to say. Obviously we never got those criticisms. But it's hard to know if we would have," Schwartz stated.

Additionally, the Ripple executive pointed out that it was uncertain whether the developers could have come up with better options if they had chosen to make their own cryptographic decisions.

"I'm not sure we would have come up with better ones had we made our own decisions anyway," Schwartz wrote.

It is worth noting that the original Bitcoin code copied in the early stages of the XRP Ledger is no longer present in the network's codebase.

According to Vet, the remaining parts of Satoshi Nakamoto's timekeeping code were deleted in December 2014 by former Ripple engineering lead Nik Bougalis.

There are two crucial cryptographic design decisions from Bitcoin that are still used on the XRP Ledger.

More than half of its $2.7 billion repurchase spending came at average prices above $99, leaving just $332 million as Bitcoin purchases slow.

Strategy has spent more repurchasing STRC near $100 than at deeper discounts, testing its stated strategy of slowing purchases as the preferred stock approaches face value.

Sources indicate that A CryptoSlate analysis of the Michael Saylor-founded organization's regulatory filings highlights that it spent approximately $1.4 billion buying back STRC between Sept. 28 and Nov. 15, when weekly average purchase prices ranged from $99.06 to $99.93.

In a recent development, that represents 52% of the nearly $2.7 billion Strategy has spent under its preferred-stock repurchase program since July. By comparison, the organization spent approximately $1.28 billion during the preceding 10 weeks, when its average purchase prices were below $99.

Averages are shown to two decimals by STRC.live, derived from issuer-reported share counts and buyback spending rounded to $0.1 million, so cents are approximate. The Nov. 9–15 average is calculated from Strategy’s $228.1 million and 2,282,510 shares. The $100 series is the security’s stated amount.

Source: STRC.live buyback tracker, July 20 to Nov. 8, 2026 · Strategy Form 8-K, Nov. 16, 2026 (latest week).

The spending has coincided with STRC's recovery toward its $100 stated value. The preferred stock briefly touched $100 on Nov. 4 for the first time since May before retreating below that threshold.

However, the continued buying contrasts with the approach Strategy CEO Phong Le outlined in July.

Le remarked the company intended to scale purchases according to price and liquidity, buying “more at deeper discounts and less as the STRC trading price approaches $100 per share.”.

The company's weekly disclosures show that its STRC spending generally increased as the discount narrowed.

Strategy initially spent $25 million repurchasing 288,930 shares at an average price of $86.52 between July 20 and July 26.

Recent findings suggest that by Sept. 28-Oct. 4, weekly spending had climbed to $176.3 million at an average price of $99.39, even though the discount to stated value had narrowed from nearly 13.5% to approximately 0.6%.

Sources indicate that buyback spending is reported to the nearest $0.1 million. Each bar is assigned to its reporting period end date, not necessarily a calendar week. The Sep. 8–13 reporting interval contains six days. Companion chart indicates average price per share.

Source: STRC.live buyback tracker, July 20 to Nov. 8, 2026 · Strategy Form 8-K, Nov. 16, 2026 (latest week).

In a recent development, purchases remained substantial in subsequent weeks, reaching a record $228.1 million between Nov. 9 and Nov. 15 at an implied average price of $99.93.

The sustained spending has also made Strategy a significant participant in STRC trading.

Pro-MSTR analyst Zaid estimated that the manufacturer's latest repurchases equaled 25.2% of STRC's total weekly trading volume, describing its presence as being toward the higher end of historical buyback activity.

Meanwhile, Crypto Banter founder Ran Neuner highlighted the scale of the intervention, observing that Strategy had repurchased nearly 30% of the STRC it had issued.

The tech giant nevertheless has an economic incentive to continue retiring shares near face value.

STRC presently carries a 12% annualized dividend, meaning repurchases reduce future dividend obligations at the prevailing rate.

However, Strategy's ability to maintain its current buying pace under the existing program is diminishing.

Its latest SEC filing showed just $332.2 million remaining under its $3 billion authorization, with nearly 89% already exhausted.

At the latest weekly pace, another $228.1 million in repurchases would leave approximately $104 million available.

Zaid suggested another expansion could arrive soon, given the spending pace. Strategy previously raised the authorization from $1 billion to $2 billion in September and to $3 billion in October.

Strategy has continued accumulating Bitcoin alongside its preferred-stock repurchases, although purchases have slowed considerably.

Recent findings suggest that between Sept. 28 and Nov. 15, the company acquired 3,183 BTC for approximately $253.1 million, compared with the $1.39 billion spent on STRC during the same period.

The gap was particularly pronounced last week, when Strategy spent $228.1 million to repurchase STRC, compared with just $33.4 million to acquire 485 BTC.

According to recent reports, those transactions increased its Bitcoin holdings to 850,849 BTC, acquired for approximately $64.2 billion at an average price of $75,452 per coin. The firm presently has unrealized losses of more than $10 billion.

Strategy funded $206.3 million of its latest STRC repurchases through MSTR common-stock sales, highlighting the trade-off between reducing preferred-dividend obligations and expanding its Bitcoin treasury.

That capital-allocation decision comes as the company faces another challenge.

Index provider MSCI has confirmed Strategy's removal from its global equity indexes, effective Dec. 1, under rules excluding companies classified as non-operating businesses.

The exclusion could create additional selling pressure from index-tracking funds, potentially weakening MSTR's share price and making equity-funded Bitcoin purchases less attractive.

With its STRC repurchase authorization nearly exhausted, Strategy must decide whether to expand the program again or reduce purchases near $100.

That decision will also help determine whether the company can return to the larger Bitcoin acquisitions seen earlier this year while its common stock adjusts to the loss of MSCI index membership.

Elite university Harvard maintains significant Bitcoin exposure as it holds over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin ETF, a recent regulatory filing has revealed.

Harvard University remains highly exposed to Bitcoin (BTC) as the elite institution continues to hold over 3 million shares of a Bitcoin exchange-traded fund (ETF).

Industry observers note that as per Bitcoin Magazine’s Nov. 16 report, Harvard Management Manufacturer, which manages Harvard University’s endowment, held 3,044,612 shares of BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust (IBIT) as of Sept. 30, 2026.

Sources indicate that the Form 13F filing by Harvard University with the U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (SEC) highlighted that its investment in the Bitcoin ETF was worth roughly $144.1 million at the end of the third quarter.

Notably, Harvard did not change its Bitcoin ETF share count during the third quarter. The university held the same number of shares as reported at the end of June.

Harvard first disclosed its investment in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF during the second quarter of 2025.

In a recent development, as per Harvard's Form 13F filing submitted on Aug. 8, 2025, it held 1,906,000 IBIT shares at the end of the second quarter. The investment was worth roughly $116.7 million as of June 30.

The university subsequently increased its Bitcoin exposure significantly.

For instance, at the end of September 2025, Harvard held 6,813,612 IBIT shares, worth roughly $442.9 million. The Bitcoin ETF was the biggest investment that Harvard publicly reported at the time.

Later, however, the university started trimming its Bitcoin exposure. For example, during the fourth quarter of 2025, Harvard reduced its IBIT holdings by about 21.4%. Its total share holdings fell to 5.35 million.

During the first quarter of 2026, Harvard again reduced its Bitcoin exposure by 43.1%. This brought down the number of IBIT shares to roughly 3.04 million.

In a recent development, since then, the university has maintained this number of shares. Harvard's quarter-end share count has remained unchanged in recent quarters.

Hackers Redirected Bitcoin Miner Rewards via AI Attack, Luxor CEO Notes.

Hackers briefly hijacked computing power from Bitcoin miners using Luxor’s fleet management software, in what the company’s CEO called an AI-enabled attack.

Luxor Technology said Sunday that its internal monitoring flagged an unauthorized redirect of hashrate through Commander, its tool for managing mining machines.

Hashrate is the computing power miners devote to securing Bitcoin and earning rewards. Just over a dozen client accounts were affected, with their machines pointed to a different mining pool for a limited window, effectively sending the value of their work elsewhere.

Recent findings suggest that luxor said it patched Commander within two hours and began restoring affected machines to their original settings. No data was leaked or taken from its systems, and the problem was isolated to Commander, according to the firm.

Luxor Pool and its LuxOS software weren’t affected, the tech giant remarked, adding that every affected client will be paid in full for the redirected hashrate, as if their machines had mined normally.

Luxor CEO Nick Hansen said the compromise began around 6 p.m. Pacific time Saturday through “a sophisticated AI-enabled vector.” He didn’t detail how the attack worked. “You trust us with your fleet, and we need to be better,” he wrote on X.

Around 6:00p PDT yesterday, a subset of Commander customers were compromised, through a sophisticated AI-enabled vector. We were able to identify and patch quickly so that it didn't continue, then the hard work of reverting started.….

In a follow-up post, Hansen stated crypto businesses are now “inundated with AI-enabled attacks,” with abliterated models, or AI models stripped of their safety guardrails, probing systems around the clock for weaknesses.

Luxor has responded by buying its own bare-metal GPUs to run such models defensively. It has also put most fresh feature work on hold to harden its infrastructure by rotating keys, updating kernels and pinning dependencies. Hansen urged other companies running similar services to do the same.

Sources indicate that bitcoin developers are grappling with the same threat. Bitcoin Core updated its security policy to address AI-driven threats, and an AI “red team” effort has turned up critical vulnerabilities throughout the year.

Recent findings suggest that the incident also follows other attacks on Bitcoin infrastructure. Blockstream’s Liquid Network restored full Bitcoin backing earlier this month, two months after a $320 million exploit.

Luxor said it would soon publish a full post-mortem of the hack.

Harvard and Dartmouth reported the same numbers of shares in BlackRock’s Bitcoin ETF at the end of September as they had at the end of June. The positions became more valuable as the fund rose.

The distinction is useful: a larger dollar figure can describe a change in market prices without showing an increase in the number of shares held. These filings, submitted on November 13, also reveal other portfolio choices that put the Bitcoin positions into perspective.

Harvard Management Tech giant’s September filing lists 3,044,612 shares of the iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF, valued at $144.1 million. Dartmouth’s disclosure lists 201,531 shares worth approximately $9.5 million.

Industry observers note that the corresponding June disclosures show identical share counts, valued at about $101.4 million and $6.7 million. That works out to an increase of roughly 42% in the reported value of each position. The calculation compares the two filing snapshots; it is not a measure of fresh cash invested during the quarter.

Matching endpoints do not establish that no transactions happened between them. A manager could trade during a quarter and finish with the same holding. The documents establish the reported balances on the two dates.

In a recent development, the difference is easier to see in Harvard’s SPDR Gold Shares position. Its latest filing reports 1,161,000 GLD shares, compared with 58,862 in the June information table. That is nearly twenty times the earlier share count. The September position was worth about $442.2 million.

Sources indicate that those figures support a statement that Harvard’s reported exposure through that gold fund expanded substantially. They do not, by themselves, explain why. Inflation protection, portfolio construction and other motives require evidence beyond a list of securities.

Nor does the gold increase prove that Bitcoin financed it. Establishing such a rotation would require information about cash movements and the wider portfolio. Here, the Bitcoin share count stayed level while the GLD count rose.

Dartmouth also reported 304,803 shares in the Bitwise Solana Staking ETF and 178,148 shares in the Grayscale Ethereum Staking ETF. Those share counts likewise match its June table. Their September values were approximately $4.9 million and $4.5 million respectively.

Recent findings suggest that the fund names describe distinct underlying exposures. Combining their dollar values can show the size of the reported crypto-linked positions, but it does not turn them into one interchangeable investment. Bitcoin, Ether and Solana can respond differently to network developments, and a staking product introduces mechanics that a straightforward Bitcoin trust does not have.

NewsBTC’s recent report on JPMorgan’s crypto-linked securities holdings reveals another reason to inspect the actual instrument before interpreting an institutional total.

Industry observers note that the SEC’s Form 13F guidance explains the delayed quarterly reporting framework. These disclosures are a record of reportable securities holdings, not a complete picture of each university’s assets or a live trading feed.

That timing matters after November’s sustained Bitcoin ETF withdrawals. A September position can coexist with subsequent market selling, and the latest filings cannot show whether either university changed its exposure after quarter-end.

The evidence is specific but useful: both reported stable Bitcoin ETF share counts through September, while Harvard’s gold holding expanded sharply. The next comparable filing will show whether that pattern survived the market’s later reversal.

Tom Lee Blames Nvidia and Anthropic IPO for Ethereum Plunge as Bitmine Buys the Dip.

Bitmine Immersion Technologies kept buying Ethereum through a punishing selloff, adding 7,653 ETH worth roughly $14 million, as chairman Tom Lee argued the token’s steep decline runs counter to improving fundamentals and echoes a dip that preceded a major tech IPO earlier this year.

The NYSE-listed organization said Monday its holdings reached 6,077,745 ETH, worth about $11.1 billion at a reference price of $1,823 per coin, far below where the firm’s stack was valued just weeks ago.

That marks a stark drop in paper value: Bitmine’s total crypto, cash and “moonshot” holdings now stand at $11.8 billion, down from $14.3 billion a week earlier, almost entirely because of ETH’s price slide rather than any selling.

The position still represents 4.97% of Ethereum’s 122.2 million token supply, leaving Bitmine 99% of the way to its goal of owning 5% of the network, the target it calls the “Alchemy of 5%.”.

Lee did not sugarcoat the move. “ETH tumbled 28% in the past two weeks,” he said, calling the “waterfall decline” inconsistent with what he views as positive fundamentals, including banks and financial institutions announcing tokenization projects built on Ethereum. (Disclosure: Tom Lee is an investor in Dastan, Decrypt’s parent manufacturer.).

He pointed to external pressures weighing on the price, including the fallout from Nvidia’s turmoil triggering margin selling in Asia and investors raising cash ahead of Anthropic’s initial public offering, whose pricing is reported for Nov. 18.

Lee also drew a historical parallel, arguing the drop mirrors the sell-off ahead of SpaceX’s $75 billion June IPO, when ETH fell 39% over eight weeks and bottomed three trading days before pricing. Lee suggested the current slump, down a similar amount ahead of the Anthropic listing, could follow the same pattern.

Bitmine remains the world’s largest Ethereum treasury and the second-largest crypto treasury overall, behind Michael Saylor’s Strategy, which now holds 849,327 BTC. Strategy also kept buying through the downturn, with Saylor nudging the market to rally with the quip “this dip could use a little orange.”.

Bitmine has 5,227,037 ETH, about 86% of its holdings, staked through its MAVAN platform, with projected annualized revenue of roughly $245 million at current levels.

It also holds 216 Bitcoin, $448 million in cash and marketable securities, a $180 million stake in Beast Industries and a $67 million position in Eightco Holdings.

Tech Report: Coinbase and Broadridge propose standard for tokenized stock disclosures

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read | Sumber: https://cointelegraph.com/news/coinbase-broadridge-tokenized-stock-shareholder-notices?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The proposed standard aims to connect tokenized stockholders with corporate disclosures and voting materials across digital wallets, but would not create shareholder rights.
  • Coinbase and Broadridge proposed a technical standard Monday that would let digital wallets find and display shareholder notices linked to tokenized stocks.
  • Sources indicate that the jointly developed Onchain Rights Standard would give issuers, custodians and wallet providers a shared format for communications about dividends, shareholder meetings and other corporate actions.

The proposed standard aims to connect tokenized stockholders with corporate disclosures and voting materials across digital wallets, but would not create shareholder rights.

Coinbase and Broadridge proposed a technical standard Monday that would let digital wallets find and display shareholder notices linked to tokenized stocks.

Sources indicate that the jointly developed Onchain Rights Standard would give issuers, custodians and wallet providers a shared format for communications about dividends, shareholder meetings and other corporate actions. Broadridge separately unveiled a supporting data service, known as an oracle, intended to help participating firms document the distribution of those notices.

The proposal’s technical documentation describes an onchain announcement that links a token to a standardized corporate document. A dividend notice, for example, could specify the date, payment terms and any choices available to holders. Compatible wallets could then display notices from different issuers using the same format, reducing the need for multiple other integrations.

“The proposed standard is a communications framework; it does not itself create shareholder rights,” Mark Nichols, Broadridge’s co-president of digital assets, told Cointelegraph.

Nichols remarked implementation would depend on the underlying structure of each tokenized stock, including whether holders have direct shareholder rights.

The companies said they submitted the proposal for review as an Ethereum Improvement Proposal. They did not name additional adopters of the standard or give an implementation timetable.

Broadridge introduced its onchain shareholder governance platform in April, naming Galaxy as an intended user for its May shareholder meeting. The platform integrates Broadridge’s ProxyVote system with digital wallets, allowing investors to receive shareholder materials, confirm holdings and submit votes, with voting records maintained on an Avalanche-based blockchain.

Industry observers note that hong Kong’s Financial Secretary Paul Chan has reaffirmed looks to introduce a bill before the end of 2026 expanding the city’s digital-asset licensing framework. Speaking on November 16, he linked that regulatory work with a market moving toward regular use of tokenized investment products. The message was that more activity on blockchains still needs identifiable institutions responsible for the services around it.

Recent findings suggest that chan’s Bloomberg Global Regulatory Forum speech names dealing, advice, management and custody as activities to be brought within the perimeter. He also highlighted the two licensed stablecoin issuers and the emergence of around-the-clock trading in tokenized money-market funds.

The timetable is a reiteration, not a newly enacted rule. In a November 4 Legislative Council reply, the government said it planned to amend the Anti-Money Laundering and Counter-Terrorist Financing Ordinance and extend the existing trading-platform regime. That earlier explanation helps locate the proposal: the focus is the businesses handling digital assets and the functions they perform.

For a customer, the same investment can involve several such functions. One company might recommend it, another execute the purchase and another safeguard the resulting holding. A useful regulatory structure has to make responsibility visible at each handoff.

The November 4 government reply reported 17 authorised retail investment products with tokenized classes at the end of September, representing about HK$10.3 billion in those classes. These included money-market funds and gold-related products. The figure concerns a defined set of investment products; it should not be presented as the size of Hong Kong’s entire digital-asset market.

The Securities and Futures Commission’s October 26 approval allowed secondary trading of ChinaAMC’s Hong Kong-dollar and US-dollar digital money-market funds on a licensed virtual-asset platform. Secondary trading lets investors exchange existing interests rather than relying solely on subscriptions and redemptions with a fund.

Industry observers note that that creates a different set of questions from simply recording ownership on a blockchain. Investors need meaningful prices, sufficient counterparties and a clear understanding of how traded units relate to their rights in the underlying product.

If a platform offers trading through a weekend, its customer support, security and controls have to account for that window. Yet the assets held by a fund may trade on a different schedule. A round-the-clock token does not ensure that its underlying market has become equally liquid at every hour.

The cash side is another dependency. Hong Kong’s EnsembleTX settlement work addresses how tokenized money and investment transactions can fit together. The trading venue, fund, custodian and payment service each need a consistent view of what has completed and what remains outstanding.

Stablecoin distribution raises similar questions about access and redemption. Anchorpoint’s planned native HKDAP expansion shows why a network integration and the conditions under which customers can use a product are separate milestones. A new route for transferring an asset does not by itself explain every holder’s rights.

It has been revealed that chan’s speech does not itself set final licence conditions or establish a commencement date for the expanded regime. Those details matter to firms deciding whether to add a service, change a custody arrangement or work through another authorised provider.

The most useful next evidence will be the legislative text and its treatment of different business models. Clear definitions can help firms determine where their obligations begin, while practical transition arrangements affect how existing customers are served.

Industry observers note that hong Kong’s challenge is now partly one of coordination: allowing more products and trading hours while keeping responsibility legible. A tokenized market will be easier to evaluate when investors can identify who owes them what, who controls a transaction and which regulator oversees each service.

The XRP Ledger’s proposed AMM V2 overhaul would let creators of automated trading pools choose how those pools price trades, potentially giving traders more usable liquidity for the same deposit. For XRP holders, the potential benefits are better execution and new ways to provide liquidity; additional demand to hold the token would depend on which assets and routes attract capital.

According to recent reports, the distinction is visible in today’s pools. XRPSCAN responses retrieved at 13:15 UTC on Nov. 15 showed roughly 25,065 of Ripple’s dollar stablecoin RLUSD and 25,068 of Circle’s USDC in the RLUSD/USDC pool, about $50,133 if both stablecoins are valued at $1. CryptoSlate’s XRP page displayed $0.97 when retrieved at 13:15 UTC on Nov. 15, with market data marked as updated eight minutes earlier.

An automated market maker, or AMM, lets people trade against a pool whose prices follow a formula. XRPL’s current design uses a constant-product-style curve. Liquidity supports trading across a broad price range, even when the assets usually trade close to one another.

Sources indicate that the AMM Swappable Curves draft proposes alternatives. StableSwap would concentrate effective depth near the expected relationship between correlated assets, such as two dollar stablecoins. Concentrated liquidity would let providers allocate capital within chosen price ranges. Binned liquidity would place assets at discrete fixed prices, with execution moving to another price when a funded bin is exhausted.

Industry observers note that the economic aim is more executable depth per unit of capital. A stablecoin pool could serve trades near parity with less money spread across distant prices. A provider choosing a narrower range could make the same deposit more useful while that range remains active.

The size of any trading improvement would depend on funding, price ranges, fees, trade size and whether correlated assets remain close in value.

Industry observers note that routing matters as much as the curve. XRPL already combines AMMs and order books. The draft would compare curve offers at each routing step using their actual output after fees at the offer’s size, rather than choosing solely by the displayed marginal price. Any execution comparison must therefore include order-book liquidity and alternative routes, not just these two pools.

According to recent reports, A more efficient direct RLUSD/USDC pool could improve stablecoin execution without holding XRP as either trading asset. Customers still face XRP transaction costs and applicable account or trust-line reserve requirements. Those requirements are separate from funding XRP inventory in a trading pair; current AMM ledger entries themselves have reserve exemptions, which do not automatically extend to latest position entries proposed for AMM V2.

Industry observers note that an XRP pair creates a different opportunity because its inventory includes XRP. Even there, capital efficiency cuts both ways. Less XRP could support a given amount of executable depth, while a larger, more active market could attract enough providers to raise aggregate deposits.

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Hong Kong’s SWIFT Push Puts XRP Back In Focus.

Programmable blockchain payments are coming: Swift is plugging its ledger into Hong Kong’s Project Ensemble.

The Hong Kong Monetary Authority announced on 16 November, 2026 a strengthened partnership with Swift to explore how tokenised deposits can improve the speed and end-to-end experience of cross-border transactions.

The work builds on collaboration that began in 2023 through the Project Ensemble Sandbox, where the two organisations tested interoperability between central bank digital currency systems.

The latest phase brings in major Hong Kong banks, including Bank of China (Hong Kong), Standard Chartered, and HSBC, to examine how the Swift ledger can connect with Project Ensemble’s settlement layer.

The goal is to develop mechanisms that use multi-currency tokenised deposits for cross-border payments, using Swift’s global network to link international and local systems more tightly.

HKMA Deputy Chief Executive Howard Lee described it as another step toward supporting real-time, always-on, and programmable cross-border transactions.

Industry observers note that swift is plugging its ledger into Hong Kong's Project Ensemble.The HKMA, Swift, HSBC, Standard Chartered and Bank of China (Hong Kong) will explore moving tokenized deposits across borders in multiple currencies. The goal is real-time, 24/7, programmable payments.It's still….

Swift’s Chief Business Officer Thierry Chilosi noted that as domestic systems evolve to handle new forms of digital value, the organisation is exploring how its ledger can connect these platforms across borders so institutions can settle more efficiently.

Recent findings suggest that this is not Hong Kong’s first experiment with tokenised assets and digital money infrastructure. In 2023, Ripple and Fubon Bank participated in the HKMA’s inaugural e-HKD Pilot Programme.

Their use case combined a hypothetical e-HKD with tokenised real estate (property liens) and lending protocols to enable faster access to home equity.

The solution ran on a private ledger built with the same technology as the XRP Ledger, with Ripple’s CBDC platform handling the digital currency layer.

Industry observers note that that earlier pilot focused on domestic retail and asset-tokenisation scenarios. The upcoming HKMA x Swift x XRP work shifts the emphasis toward wholesale interbank settlement and multi-currency cross-border flows using tokenised deposits.

Both efforts share the same underlying requirement: different systems, whether CBDC platforms, tokenized deposit ledgers, or traditional messaging networks, must be able to interoperate without forcing every participant on one rail.

Public blockchains such as the XRP Ledger have long been positioned by their proponents as neutral settlement layers that can sit between otherwise incompatible systems.

Industry observers note that HKMA + SWIFT + tokenized deposits is a peak "TradFi meets onchain" moment 🤝 honest q fam: would you hold tokenized bank deposits, or stick with stablecoins? 🤔.

XRP itself is frequently discussed as a potential bridge asset for currency conversions in corridors where no single national digital currency is suitable as an intermediary.

Ripple’s earlier work with the HKMA already demonstrated that XRPL-derived technology could support tokenized asset and CBDC-related use cases inside a regulated pilot.

Sources indicate that the current Project Ensemble-Swift collaboration does not name any public blockchain or bridge asset. The programme focuses on connecting existing institutional infrastructure with emerging tokenised-deposit systems.

Authorities in the United States and Canada have revealed a major cross-border crackdown on cryptocurrency fraud, bringing together law enforcement agencies, financial regulators and private companies to target online scam networks.

Industry observers note that the Ontario Securities Commission (OSC) announced on Nov. 16 the launch of Operation Niagara, a coordinated initiative aimed at disrupting organized cryptocurrency fraud schemes and protecting potential victims.

According to the Canadian securities regulator, the operation involves investigators, securities specialists and financial crime experts from both countries.

The initiative will use advanced technology and enhanced investigative capabilities to identify fraudulent activity and potential victims in near real time.

Recent findings suggest that importantly, the operation will not focus solely on investigating criminals after fraud has occurred. Authorities also intend to identify individuals who are being targeted by scammers and intervene before they suffer further financial losses.

"Fraud knows no border, and it targets everyday people," said Bonnie Lysyk, Executive Vice-President of Enforcement at the OSC.

The initiative brings together several major law enforcement and regulatory agencies, including the U.S. Secret Service, Ontario Provincial Police (OPP) and Royal Canadian Mounted Police (RCMP).

Canadian securities regulators, including the Alberta Securities Commission, British Columbia Securities Commission and Autorité des marchés financiers, are also participating.

Private-sector companies will contribute technical expertise and intelligence to help authorities identify and disrupt fraudulent networks.

It’s worth noting that the OSC didn’t provide details on how many fraud networks it is targeting, how many potential victims have been identified or how much cryptocurrency is involved in Operation Niagara.

Recent findings suggest that backpack has secured a US derivatives-clearing registration, adding a regulated institution for handling the obligations behind trades. The Commodity Futures Trading Commission registered TLD Clearing, doing business as Backpack Clearing, on November 13. The approval is a meaningful part of the group’s market-infrastructure plans, while a separate application to operate an exchange remains pending.

The CFTC’s public register permits Backpack Clearing to clear margined futures, along with fully collateralized futures, options on futures and swaps. This identifies the clearinghouse’s authorised scope; it does not show that every potential contract has launched.

It has been revealed that A clearinghouse becomes the central counterparty to accepted trades and manages the resulting obligations. Its job differs from matching buyers and sellers on an exchange. A trading screen can display an executed order rapidly, but the market also needs arrangements for collecting collateral, settling gains and losses and dealing with a participant that cannot pay.

Sources indicate that the distinction is relevant to the broader industry push toward integrated derivatives operations. Coinbase’s earlier clearing registration demonstrated another crypto group building this part of its infrastructure, under its own approved scope.

Backpack’s clearing-activities submission describes an intended central-counterparty model for contracts listed on registered markets. It includes initial and variation margin, risk-based requirements and default-management procedures. The filing also describes legally separate exchange, clearing and brokerage entities working within a coordinated framework.

That separation matters when a group offers several services under one familiar brand. A customer needs to know which entity holds its account, which one accepts a trade for clearing and which rules apply if something goes wrong. Shared ownership does not make those roles interchangeable.

The application contemplated a phased product rollout. Its list of possible future products should therefore be read as a strategy subject to the relevant approvals and operating capacity, rather than a current trading menu. Clearing registration alone does not establish availability, customer eligibility or the amount of market liquidity.

Industry observers note that the registration order records commitments to enforce clearing-member standards and maintain member funds separately from the clearinghouse’s own funds. It also states changes to material facts or circumstances may require a upcoming or amended order.

Recent findings suggest that these are operating obligations that continue after the approval date. For a clearing business, reliable performance depends on how it handles changing exposures and exceptional events, not only on passing an initial regulatory assessment.

Imagine a sharp market move that leaves one member owing more collateral. The clearinghouse needs timely prices, dependable calls for funds and a credible process if that member fails. The practical strength of the model would become visible through those controls and its ability to complete settlements under stress.

The CFTC’s record for TLD Markets lists its designated-contract-market application as pending, dated April 22, 2026. That is the status shown in the public record reviewed for this report. The clearing decision should not be described as approval of that separate exchange application.

Nor should the US registration be blended with other Backpack-branded activity, such as tokenized-equity collateral used in Kamino’s Solana lending market. Different products can sit within different legal entities and regulatory arrangements even when their branding overlaps.

For Backpack, the immediate achievement is a registered clearing operation with an identified scope. The next commercial milestones are the remaining relevant permissions and clearly documented products, participants and launch arrangements. Those details will determine what traders can actually access through the US structure.

Clarity Act Defeat ‘Failure of American Leadership’: Trump’s Former Crypto Chief.

The Senate's failure to pass the Clarity Act was "a failure of American leadership," according to Patrick Witt, President Donald Trump's former top crypto adviser.

Industry observers note that "It was extremely disappointing," Witt mentioned in an on-stage interview at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London. "I was knee deep in Clarity. I lived it for a year plus negotiating that bill," he noted, adding that the bill, "would have been incredibly impactful.".

Witt served as executive director of the President's Council of Advisers for Digital Assets until last month and led the White House push for the bill, which would have set out a framework for regulating crypto markets. It failed a key procedural vote in the Senate in September.

In a recent development, "We ultimately lost against the clock," he stated, adding that, "The policy was good. We resolved pretty much all of the policy differences." But with the midterm elections approaching, "the political problem of ethics really consumed everything else," he said.

Industry observers note that democrats had raised concerns over the Trump family's crypto ventures. Witt acknowledged that Trump's involvement in crypto was "arguably the issue," but mentioned the president had agreed to two ethics provisions. The second would have barred federal officials, including the president, from issuing or sponsoring digital assets, forced the president to divest certain digital assets or put them in a blind trust, and let state attorneys general enforce violations. "There's no precedent for those kinds of things in American law," he said.

According to recent reports, the GENIUS stablecoin bill also lost an initial procedural vote in 2025 but recovered because it came early in Trump's term, Witt noted. With Clarity, "we knew that we were going to get one shot at it, and unfortunately we just came up short," he noted.

It has been revealed that looking ahead, Witt mentioned the odds of passing a comprehensive replacement are low. "I would expect that market structure in the United States is going to be less written on Capitol Hill and more written in the Federal Register, which is where the agencies do their rulemakings and issue their guidance," Witt said.

Parts of the Clarity Act could still pass in larger legislative packages, and lawmakers could grant targeted powers, such as giving the Commodity Futures Trading Commission authority over spot crypto markets, he said.

Recent findings suggest that witt said regulators already have "ample authority," and that the administration had to "hold them back a little bit" while the bill played out. The SEC and CFTC have since moved ahead with their own crypto rules, though House Financial Services Committee Chairman French Hill (R-AR) has said those efforts fall short of what the legislation would have achieved.

Sources indicate that SEC Chair Paul Atkins and CFTC Chair Michael Selig "are committed to moving markets on chain," Witt said, framing the concern as one of American competitiveness. "Capital is going to go where it's treated best," he said.

Sources indicate that despite Democrats winning control of both chambers of Congress in this month's midterms, Witt mentioned he is "not bearish on the industry overall," since the regulators and the president remain in place. Democrats are reportedly planning to push their own, broader market structure bill.

He said opposition to crypto is increasingly generational rather than purely partisan. While some Democrats, such as Sen. Elizabeth Warren (D-MA), are "going to be 100% opposed to anything that seemingly is favorable to crypto," younger lawmakers on both sides see it as "part of the fabric of financial infrastructure," he said, pointing to Sens. Angela Alsobrooks (D-MD) and Ruben Gallego (D-AZ).

Witt left the administration in October, The Hill reported. He mentioned he has held talks with crypto firms, venture capital firms and defense companies, and hopes to announce his next move in the coming weeks.

Unocoin has revised its account of a security incident that disrupted the Indian exchange, putting estimated cryptocurrency losses at about $200,000. The more significant technical finding is how transactions could proceed after the exchange asked its wallet providers to freeze activity.

Industry observers note that unocoin’s November 14 enhancement identifies compromised backup keys as part of the explanation. The incident illustrates a distinction that can be easy to miss: suspending access to a service and removing the ability to authorize a blockchain transaction are separate things.

According to recent reports, unocoin said three operational hot wallets were compromised and promised to fund the identified loss from its own resources. Its earlier assessment had not identified missing cryptocurrency. The company also disclosed possible exposure of customer information, while saying it had found no evidence that KYC documents were accessed.

Those findings remain subject to investigation. An initial loss estimate is useful for assessing scale, but it is not the same as a final reconciliation of every asset and transaction. Potential information exposure also needs to be assessed separately from the amount of cryptocurrency taken.

That distinction matters for customers. Replacing coins can restore an account balance; it cannot make exposed contact or account information private again. A financial remedy and a data-security response address different consequences.

BitGo’s November 13 account notes the affected Ethereum wallet used a two-of-three multisignature arrangement. Unocoin controlled the user and backup keys, while BitGo controlled the third. BitGo says the reviewed transfers used the two Unocoin keys and were broadcast outside its platform.

It has been revealed that the design permits an owner to recover assets without depending on the service provider. That is valuable when a provider is unavailable, but the same independence means that the provider’s refusal to sign cannot prevent two other valid keys from acting together.

It has been revealed that bitGo’s wallet documentation distinguishes self-custody arrangements from its custody products, including differences in who controls keys. A provider’s name therefore does not, by itself, tell a reader who had final authority over a particular wallet.

The broader control question is whether emergency credentials are separated effectively from everyday systems. A recovery mechanism has to remain available to its legitimate owner while being difficult for an intruder to assemble with other signing material.

NewsBTC’s coverage of business Bitcoin accounts with team approvals examined another part of that problem: permission to request or approve a transfer is not necessarily identical to possession of the cryptographic keys.

Combining several safeguards can help, but their independence matters. Two approvals provide less protection if one compromised system can obtain both. This is an architectural lesson from the reported signing arrangement, not a determination of the still-unknown route into Unocoin’s backup storage.

Industry observers note that unocoin states it is rebuilding infrastructure and investigating how the backup material was compromised. A convincing follow-up would connect that forensic explanation with a complete accounting of losses, restored services and the handling of potentially exposed information.

Sources indicate that bitGo’s wider commercial growth, covered in NewsBTC’s report on its quarterly results, shows how large the custody and infrastructure business has become. Scale makes clear descriptions of individual service arrangements more valuable, particularly when several companies participate in one transaction process.

It has been revealed that the available disclosures narrow the explanation considerably. They identify which keys authorized the reviewed Ethereum transfers. They do not yet provide a complete account of how those keys were obtained or establish that every part of the incident has been resolved.

WhiteBIT has relaunched its over-the-counter (OTC) platform and enhanced its institutional offering with a large-volume trading section for digital assets and fiat currencies. It is tailored for institutional and corporate clients, investment funds, family offices, and other participants in the market that seek a special approach when having high-value deals.

In a recent development, unlike normal exchange trading, where big orders may impact market prices and execution expenses, OTC trades are transactions carried out outside the public order book, straight between a client and the trading desk. This can reduce the impact on the market, give more flexibility in terms of the execution period, and give more customization for institutional trading.

“The institutional engagement with cryptocurrencies is growing at the level of more than just access to cryptocurrencies. Equipped with a reliable compliance framework, a dedicated team of support, and processes that are predictable in their operations, funds, corporate treasuries, and professional investors require execution models that allow them to operate in the same way they do in traditional financial markets. By relaunching our OTC desk, we’re strengthening the infrastructure that enables these participants to execute large transactions more efficiently and with greater flexibility,” mentioned Volodymyr Nosov, Founder and President of W Group, of which WhiteBIT is a part.

The relaunched desk supports crypto-to-fiat and fiat-to-crypto transactions in major fiat currencies, including the US dollar (USD), euro (EUR), British pound (GBP), and Swiss franc (CHF), as well as the stablecoins USDT and USDC. Also, the top 10 crypto assets by market capitalization are now available for trading on the OTC desk against USDT and USDC. Other crypto assets outside the top 10 and additional fiat currencies are available upon individual request.

It has been revealed that whiteBIT does not impose a fixed upper limit on OTC transaction sizes. Instead, the maximum amount is determined by the source of funds and the results of the required compliance checks, so capacity is set around each client’s actual activity.

Industry observers note that each client is assigned to a dedicated OTC manager, who provides them with support in negotiating the transaction parameters, agreeing the terms of execution, and support throughout the transaction. The service protects client data and transactional information and follows Know Your Customer (KYC), Know Your Business (KYB), and all applicable compliance regulations.

It has been revealed that whiteBIT is introducing a zero-fee offer for upcoming OTC clients, covering their first transaction of up to $2 million. It is a one-time offer, valid for three months from release, after which it can be extended; transactions with the top 10 crypto assets are not covered by the offer. Deals with a value of more than 2 million are processed as a single tranche with an indicative price derived from the OTC pricing strategy established in advance with the client’s dedicated OTC manager, allowing institutional and corporate clients to proposal bigger deals from the beginning.

The relaunch is a part of WhiteBIT’s institutional and professional market business growth strategy. With the addition of a dedicated OTC execution channel, WhiteBIT will aim to provide crypto liquidity and allow more flexibility in handling large-scale digital asset transactions for businesses and investors.

WhiteBIT is a leading global crypto exchange by user traffic, offering over 1020 trading pairs, 370+ assets, and supporting 8 fiat currencies. With a strong focus on regulatory compliance, WhiteBIT serves 10 million customers across six continents and more than 150 countries. Founded in 2018, the platform is part of W Group, which has more than 40 million customers globally. WhiteBIT collaborates with Visa, FACEIT, FC Barcelona, Juventus FC, and the Ukrainian national football team. The tech giant is dedicated to driving the widespread adoption of blockchain technology worldwide.

Bitcoin‘s recovery above $64,000 risks losing momentum as leveraged traders dominate market activity while institutional investors continue withdrawing capital.

It has been revealed that the cryptocurrency staged a modest rebound after plunging toward $62,000 over the weekend, its lowest level since July. However, the recovery comes against a backdrop of weakening demand, with US spot Bitcoin ETFs recording substantial withdrawals and futures positions shrinking across major exchanges.

The clearest warning came from Wall Street before the weekend crash.

According to Farside Investors, US spot Bitcoin ETFs saw more than $1 billion in net outflows over the five trading sessions ending Nov. 13. BlackRock's iShares Bitcoin Trust accounted for about $908 million of those withdrawals, highlighting a retreat from one of Bitcoin's largest institutional investment channels.

With ETF demand retreating, leveraged traders dominated the weekend's market activity.

A CryptoQuant analysis highlighted that Bitcoin futures generated $64.11 billion in trading volume on Nov. 14, dwarfing the $13.36 billion recorded across tracked spot exchanges.

That meant derivatives accounted for nearly 83% of combined trading activity, with futures turnover almost five times larger than spot volume.

The imbalance was particularly striking on Binance, where $24.46 billion in Bitcoin futures trading exceeded the combined spot volume of every exchange tracked by CryptoQuant by 83%.

Industry observers note that the disparity raises a troubling possibility for Bitcoin's recovery. Prices may stabilize as leveraged traders unwind bearish positions, but that buying can disappear promptly if investors don't return to accumulate the underlying cryptocurrency.

The weekend's derivatives frenzy coincided with a significant retreat in open interest, suggesting traders were reducing exposure as Bitcoin absorbed its latest losses.

It has been revealed that binance data revealed that open interest in its coin-margined Bitcoin futures market dropped 7.3%, from 16.25 million contracts on Nov. 13 to 15.06 million by Monday morning.

The perpetual futures segment contracted even faster, declining approximately 7.8% over the same period.

Home » Ripple (XRP) » Is The $30B XRP Burn Offer Acceptable For Ripple?

A courageous proposal to burn more than half of the remaining XRP supply lands on Ripple’s table.

Lawyer and longtime XRP observer Bill Morgan reacted to a fresh call for Ripple to destroy its entire escrow by stating the obvious: “Imagine asking a company to destroy an asset valued at $30 billion, believe they would ever do it, and expect to be viewed as sane.”.

Recent findings suggest that the demand in question came from an open letter urging Ripple CEO Brad Garlinghouse to burn the full remaining escrow, currently about 31.1 billion XRP, by the first quarter of 2027. At recent prices near $0.95, that amount is worth roughly $30 billion.

Ripple locked 55 billion XRP into on-ledger escrow contracts in December, 2017 specifically to make supply more predictable.

Each month, up to 1 billion XRP becomes available; historically, the tech giant has re-locked the majority into new smart contracts further down the line and retained a smaller net amount for operational use.

It would make more sense for XRPL validators to vote on any major supply change, because the XRP Ledger is decentralized. Ripple runs only a small share of the default Unique Node List (roughly 1 of ~35, or low single-digit percent).Protocol amendments require ~80% of trusted… https://t.co/Ib7cTsQHUx.

The escrow balance has already declined from 55 billion to roughly 31.1 billion as a result of this process.

Destroying the remaining escrow would mean permanently removing an asset that sits on Ripple’s balance sheet and that the manufacturer has repeatedly said is intended for controlled distribution, partnerships, and ecosystem growth.

No public company has ever willingly incinerated tens of billions of dollars in assets simply because a segment of token holders asked for it.

In a recent development, morgan has addressed similar proposals before. He has pointed out that large burns by other projects, including Stellar’s well-known reduction of its XLM supply, did not produce lasting price strength or prevent later declines.

The recurring demand to burn the XRP escrow, in his view, often functions more as a signal that the requester doubts the asset’s underlying value than as a coherent supply-side strategy.

Critics of the XRP escrow schedule frequently treat every monthly unlock as an automatic dump that suppresses price.

In practice, the majority of each release is returned to escrow, and XRP’s price has continued to move largely in line with broader crypto market conditions rather than in lockstep with the XRP escrow schedule.

Recent findings suggest that the supply was never meant to last forever. At the current net release rate of roughly 300 million XRP per month, the locked supply continues to decline gradually.

Imagine asking a company to destroy an asset valued at $30 billion, believe they would ever do it, and expect to be viewed as sane https://t.co/sft8TRMV80.

Morgan the lawyer has also noted in earlier posts that the escrow has already fallen from 55 billion in late 2017 to the low-to-mid 30s of billions today.

That full distribution under the original monthly cap would have emptied it years ago had Ripple not retained the flexibility to re-lock unused amounts.

#805. Latest Update: Zelle picks Solana for ZelleUSD stablecoin and international payments

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4 min read (868 words)

Latest Update: Zelle picks Solana for ZelleUSD stablecoin and international payments

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://cointelegraph.com/news/zelle-solana-zelleusd-stablecoin-international-payments?utm_source=rss_feed&utm_medium=rss&utm_campaign=rss_partner_inbound

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Zelle plans to use Solana for its ZelleUSD stablecoin and international payments, with confidential transfers designed to hide payment amounts.
  • Zelle, the US peer-to-peer payments network operated by Early Warning Services (EWS), a consortium of banks that includes JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, is partnering with Solana to support its expansion into international payments.
  • The move brings one of the largest domestic payments networks in the US into the blockchain-based payments market.

Zelle plans to use Solana for its ZelleUSD stablecoin and international payments, with confidential transfers designed to hide payment amounts.

Zelle, the US peer-to-peer payments network operated by Early Warning Services (EWS), a consortium of banks that includes JPMorgan and Wells Fargo, is partnering with Solana to support its expansion into international payments. The organization announced on stage at Breakpoint 2026 that its proprietary dollar-backed stablecoin, ZelleUSD (ZLUSD), will launch on the Solana blockchain to allow for peer-to-peer payments internationally.

The move brings one of the largest domestic payments networks in the US into the blockchain-based payments market. Zelle processed more than $1.2 trillion in US payments in 2025 and has since taken steps to establish an international business. In June, the company named India as its first international remittance corridor, with plans to allow US consumers to send money to friends and family in the country. In the same announcement, the company unveiled ZelleUSD, intended to underpin future international payment capabilities in additional markets. ZelleUSD’s issuer is Anchorage Digital Bank.

Recent findings suggest that “Sending money around the world is a pain; it’s complex, it’s fragmented and it’s often unfamiliar. Over half of the Remittance services that are offered today don’t deliver money as fast as we’d like them to,” stated Alexandra Lang, vice president of digital asset partnerships at Zelle. “Solana is a partner we chose because we’re here to deliver payments at scale.”.

The collaboration will also include ongoing experimentation into the development of privacy features for the transactions, aimed at preserving the sensitivity of payments on the public blockchain.

For Zelle, the decision to select Solana appears to have been driven in large part by the network’s infrastructure. “Zelle has such a massive scale in the United States, we needed a partner that can also deliver at massive scale internationally as well,” said Denise Leonhard, General Manager at Zelle in a video discussing the partnership.

“The number one priority is the responsibility that we have to make sure that payments are safe, secure, and they get to the right place [...] That piece around trust, security, proven infrastructure is the reason why we chose Solana.”.

Following several years in which network outages raised questions about Solana’s suitability for financial applications, the chain has maintained 100% uptime since February 2024. This is despite a routing failure at infrastructure provider Teraswitch in August 2026, which took 29% of Solana’s network offline. According to blockchain intelligence platform Metrika, transaction finality slowed, but uptime was sustained.

On stage at Breakpoint 2026, the Solana Foundation unveiled the migration of Solana from beta into mainnet, bringing with it an improvement in finality speed from 13 seconds to 150 milliseconds.

Related: HKMA, Swift explore tokenized deposits for cross-border bank payments.

Recent findings suggest that going deeper into what the collaboration will entail, on stage at Breakpoint, Lang introduced the confidential payments features the two companies had developed. She explained that the privacy focus aimed at balancing customer privacy over their payments on the network with the money laundering checks large institutions are required to make.

In the payments wallet, customers will have the option to encrypt their transfer so it is shielded from the public blockchain. Institutions that are part of Zelle’s network will be able to decrypt the transfer to carry out the checks needed to maintain compliance.

“Features like this are paramount to really getting payments to scale,” said Lang.

Related: DBS, JPMorgan’s Kinexys launch 24/7 transfers of tokenized deposits.

Sources indicate that although Solana is gaining ground in stablecoin activity, Ethereum and Tron continue to hold substantially larger pools of dollar-pegged assets. According to Token Terminal data pulled on Nov. 14, Ethereum held $150.5 billion in stablecoins while Tron held $93.2 billion, compared with $13.9 billion on Solana.

According to recent reports, however, Solana’s stablecoin activity is growing faster in transaction frequency than on either of its larger competitors. The network recorded an 82% increase in monthly stablecoin transfers year-over-year in October, compared with 48% growth on Ethereum, while Tron’s transfer count declined by nearly 8%, according to Token Terminal data.

In a recent development, zelle’s choice of Solana over both Tron and Ethereum follows other remittance providers that have expanded on-chain. Also at Breakpoint, MoneyGram outlined an integration with Solflare allowing Solflare wallet users to exchange UDSC to cash. The move expands MoneyGram Ramps on Solana, launched by the manufacturer in August.

“That’s where MoneyGram brings something different to the ecosystem: the ability to bridge digital dollars and physical cash at scale, making stablecoins more useful in everyday life,” noted Luke Tuttle, Chief Product and Technology Officer at MoneyGram in a press release.

While Zelle did not provide a timeline for the launch of international payments on stage, earlier announcements indicated that the India corridor would be live by the end of 2026.

It has been revealed that the X page thought the attack was done by a similar group that compromised Hiveon a couple of days ago. Customers discovered their pool information changed without their knowledge.

Luxor was also compromised in the management software, drawing similarities in the two attacks. Luxor confirmed this activity by writing,.

As a result, the attacked hash rate dropped to 100 PH/s, while that of OCEAN spiked to 48.8 EH/s before falling back to around 40 EH/s.

Recent findings suggest that the attacker failed to mine a BTC block; hence, they did not receive any reward. However, the attacked miners lost the opportunity to earn rewards, as the hashing time cannot be recovered.

Notably, the frightening aspect was that there was nothing wrong with the miners themselves. The management program perched above them was the weak point.

After realizing the compromise, Luxor Technology’s on-call engineering team jumped into the matter immediately.

Recent findings suggest that the vulnerability in the Commander software was patched in two hours. However, some say that was the emergency patch, and the extensive restoration took six hours.

In a recent development, while there was no data leaked from their system, over a dozen clients were affected. The firm promised compensation, saying,.

Every affected client will be paid in full for the redirected hashrate, as if it had mined normally.

The manufacturer has assured users that Commander is operating normally and no action is needed. They also confirmed that Luxor Pool and LuxOS were not impacted.

With operations now restored and a lined-up compensation, Luxor may restore confidence in consumers. Some users said the response was not bad at all.

According to recent reports, meanwhile, the last Bitcoin is expected to be mined around 2140; thereafter, miners won’t earn upcoming BTC, only transaction fees. 💡 Key Takeaways
  • The Senate Agriculture Committee will hear President Donald Trump’s two nominees to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on Tuesday, a confirmation hearing that comes as the derivatives regulator has only one sitting commissioner.
  • It has been revealed that the committee scheduled the session for 3 p.m.
  • Trump nominated the pair last week as part of a bipartisan slate for the CFTC and the Securities and Exchange Commission, a step that would begin to refill two regulators that have been operating short-handed.

The Senate Agriculture Committee will hear President Donald Trump’s two nominees to the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (CFTC) on Tuesday, a confirmation hearing that comes as the derivatives regulator has only one sitting commissioner.

It has been revealed that the committee scheduled the session for 3 p.m. Eastern in Room 106 of the Dirksen Senate Office Building. The White House sent the nominations to the Senate on Nov. 12. The nominees are Nathan Anonick of Virginia and Matthew Rowland of the District of Columbia. The hearing notice notes to check back for live video, and the committee has not posted written testimony.

Trump nominated the pair last week as part of a bipartisan slate for the CFTC and the Securities and Exchange Commission, a step that would begin to refill two regulators that have been operating short-handed.

Anonick serves on the Republican staff of the Senate Agriculture Committee under Chairman John Boozman of Arkansas. He was nominated to the seat once held by former Chairman Rostin Behnam, for a term ending June 19, 2031. A 2023 committee release said Anonick joined the panel in 2022 to manage a portfolio that includes cryptocurrencies, futures markets and derivatives, and that he had previously worked at the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation as a resolution policy specialist.

Recent findings suggest that rowland is a CFTC attorney detailed to the committee’s Democratic staff under Ranking Member Amy Klobuchar of Minnesota. He would fill the remainder of former Commissioner Summer K. Mersinger’s term, which expires April 13, 2028. Both nominees come from the committee that oversees the CFTC.

CFTC Chairman Michael Selig called them “two strong bipartisan picks” and remarked he looks forward to working with them “upon their confirmation by the US Senate.”.

Kristin N. Johnson and Steven Levine, the two SEC nominees from the same White House list, are on the agenda for a Senate Banking Committee nominations hearing at 10 a.m. Thursday in Dirksen 538.

It has been revealed that the CFTC can seat up to five commissioners, with no more than three from the same party. Chairman Michael S. Selig, sworn in Dec. 22, 2025, is at the moment the only sitting commissioner listed on the agency’s website. Even if the Senate confirms both nominees, two of the five seats would remain vacant.

Industry observers note that each nominee still needs a committee vote and then confirmation by the full Senate. The Agriculture Committee has not scheduled that vote.

The hearing lands in a lame-duck Senate, weeks after Democrats swept both chambers of Congress in the Nov. 3 midterms. The new Congress is seated in January. If the Senate does not confirm the nominations before then, they would typically be returned to the president and have to be sent again.

After the election, TD Cowen’s Jaret Seiberg told clients he does not expect Democrats to confirm Trump nominees unless the president fills Democratic seats at agencies such as the FDIC and the SEC, a step he has called unlikely. The White House slate does that at both the SEC and the CFTC.

The nominations also arrive with crypto market structure legislation stalled. The Clarity Act failed a Senate cloture vote 49-50 on Sept. 15 and dies on Jan. 3 unless the lame-duck session revives it. The bill would formally divide oversight of digital assets between the SEC and the CFTC, distinguishing which are securities, commodities or stablecoins.

Without new law, the CFTC has set much of its crypto policy on its own this year. Selig’s agency opened the door to equity perpetual futures, and a federal judge later said the CFTC likely overstepped its authority while letting trading continue.

The open question is whether a Senate heading for Democratic control confirms the CFTC picks before January, or leaves the agency short-handed into 2027.
