Singapore and Germany have tested a way to settle foreign-exchange transactions using digital central-bank money while keeping their underlying systems separate. Project Simbolon, revealed on November 16, uses cryptographic proofs to coordinate the two payment legs. Its interest lies in a practical design choice: institutions may be able to exchange value without first agreeing to run everything on one shared ledger.

In a recent development, the Monetary Authority of Singapore’s release indicates DBS and Deutsche Bank participated, with technology from Partior. The experiment covered euro–Singapore dollar payments in the central banks’ test environments. Zero-knowledge proofs verified settlement conditions without direct technical integration between the ledgers.

The intended payment-versus-payment arrangement makes each final transfer dependent on the other. Imagine a bank paying euros to receive Singapore dollars: it wants assurance that its counterparty’s payment will complete before its own funds become irretrievable. Making both legs conditional addresses that exposure at settlement. It does not make an unfunded account suddenly able to pay.

According to recent reports, the central banks’ November 2025 cooperation agreement set out an ambition to improve cross-border transfers and develop common standards for payments, FX and tokenized securities. Simbolon is a milestone within that work, rather than the launch of a generally available international payment service.

According to recent reports, keeping ledgers independent can make collaboration more manageable. Each operator may retain its own infrastructure, access rules and upgrade process. The connecting arrangement then needs precise answers about which evidence is accepted, how long an instruction remains valid and what happens when one environment stops responding.

Those questions are related to the Meridian FX APAC trial covered by NewsBTC, although the two projects should not be conflated. Both address coordination across settlement systems; Simbolon’s announcement specifically centres on the euro–Singapore dollar test and its use of cryptographic proofs.

A treasury desk usually wants to know when it must commit funds and when it can use the proceeds. An arrangement that reduces uncertainty could allow it to fund a transaction closer to completion. The economic advantage would come from the timing of usable balances, not simply a faster message between computers.

According to recent reports, MAS’ broader Project Guardian framework treats interoperability, custody, legal finality and operational resilience as connected requirements for tokenized markets. It spans several kinds of assets and money. That breadth matters because a securities transaction may involve more than a currency exchange: ownership records and collateral obligations must also remain consistent.

The challenge resembles the one behind delivery-versus-payment tools for tokenized securities. Coordinating asset and cash movements can reduce exposure between them, but the contractual rights associated with both sides still require a clear legal basis.

According to recent reports, the central banks identify performance, legal, regulatory, operational and governance work as areas for further exploration. They also say a fuller technical report will follow. No commercial launch date or measured cost reduction is established by the announcement.

That leaves useful questions for the next stage. A production arrangement would need to explain recovery after an interrupted transfer, the treatment of expired instructions and which institution resolves a disagreement about completion. Testing those situations would show whether the connection is dependable when conditions become awkward.

Simbolon provides evidence that independent digital infrastructures can coordinate an FX settlement in a controlled setting. Turning that result into a financial service will require the institutions to make the same coordination reliable, legally effective and understandable to the people managing real balances.

Fed Is Modeling AI 'Super Intelligence' Scenarios, Including Job Losses and a Stock Market Slump.

In a recent development, federal Reserve Chair Kevin Warsh stated Monday that central bank staff have started modeling how artificial intelligence could reshape the U.S. economy, including scenarios where the technology raises unemployment even as the economy grows.

Speaking at the Fed's Productivity and Jobs conference in San Francisco, Warsh described three possible paths: a productivity boom benefiting workers, a boom that leaves workers behind, and an AI investment bust that drags down stocks and economic growth.

According to recent reports, “These are illustrative scenarios, not forecasts,” Warsh mentioned, explaining that staff are using simplified economic models to test what might happen over the next several years. The Fed is preparing for different outcomes, not predicting which one will materialize.

In a recent development, warsh called the technology “super intelligence,” or SI. That language is now official Fed terminology after an October change following a Donald Trump administration executive order, rather than a scientific determination that today's AI systems have already surpassed human intelligence.

It has been revealed that in the most optimistic scenario, AI helps companies produce more with the same resources, raising the country's economic output above its historical growth rate. Workers share in those gains, and unemployment stays close to the level economists associate with a healthy job market.

In the second scenario, AI still makes the economy grow faster, but businesses automate jobs more quickly than displaced workers can find new ones. Unemployment rises despite the productivity gains.

The third scenario assumes AI investments fail to deliver the returns Wall Street expects. Companies spend heavily on infrastructure, stock prices rise on expectations of huge profits, and those expectations eventually prove too optimistic.

“Equity valuations could fall, leading to an economic slowdown,” Warsh said. In that scenario, unemployment rises more sharply, and the economy eventually recovers without the promised productivity boost.

Those risks are already receiving attention elsewhere at the Fed. Governor Michael Barr warned Monday that the AI construction boom is increasingly financed through complex arrangements, including long-term computing leases, energy contracts and financial guarantees.

Sources indicate that the Fed estimates that the potential maximum value of these off-balance-sheet obligations now exceeds $3 trillion. Those commitments are not the same as debt already owed, but they show why disappointing AI revenues could create problems beyond the technology companies building data centers.

It has been revealed that warsh did not propose an interest-rate change in Monday's remarks. The Fed's next policy meeting is scheduled for December 8 and 9.

  • Cardano holders have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to spend approximately $5 million from its treasury on physical copper, shutting down an unusual attempt to bring a traditional commodity investment onto the blockchain.

Cardano holders have overwhelmingly rejected a proposal to spend approximately $5 million from its treasury on physical copper, shutting down an unusual attempt to bring a traditional commodity investment onto the blockchain.

It has been revealed that the funding request, submitted by Toto Finance, sought 22 million ADA to purchase and tokenize warehouse-stored copper through a project called the Cardano Strategic Copper Reserve. However, the proposal received only limited support when voting closed on November 15, with opposing votes outweighing support by more than 140 to 1. The rejection means Cardano’s treasury will retain the funds that would otherwise have been allocated to the project, while raising questions about how much risk the community is willing to accept when financing real-world asset initiatives.

Toto Finance submitted its request on October 15, asking Cardano’s treasury to release 22 million ADA for the purchase, storage, and tokenization of physical copper.

In a recent development, the proposal required approval from delegated representatives, known as DReps, as well as Cardano’s Constitutional Committee. Treasury withdrawals require support from 67% of the active voting stake. The final result was overwhelmingly negative. DReps representing approximately 2.86 billion ADA voted against the proposal, while only 20.02 million ADA supported it. This meant that less than 1% of the stake voting for or against the request backed the investment.

In a recent development, the Constitutional Committee also withheld approval. Three of its seven members voted against the proposal’s constitutionality, while the remaining four did not vote. With neither governance requirement satisfied, the request expired without any treasury funds being transferred to Toto Finance.

Concerns surrounding financial exposure, management fees, and control over treasury funds contributed to the proposal’s defeat.

In a recent development, one of the main objections involved the investment’s dependence on two separate asset prices: copper and ADA. The treasury would have committed its funds in ADA, while the potential return depended on the future value of physical copper. According to Toto’s calculations, copper would have needed to appreciate approximately 49% for the treasury to recover its original investment if ADA’s dollar value remained unchanged and the full budget was spent.

The proposal also included substantial payments for technology, management, execution, storage, and insurance. Toto could have received up to approximately 3.36 million ADA through these arrangements, representing around 15% of the requested funding. DRep John MacPherson, who opposed the proposal, argued that the treasury would be exposed to both copper and ADA price fluctuations. He also questioned the amount allocated to Toto, although he acknowledged that the proposal was relatively transparent about its risks.

The Cardano Foundation had previously raised concerns about the investment structure, particularly the concentration of funds under the recipient’s control and the safeguards that still needed to be established.

Clearpool’s move from CPOOL to CLEAR is reaching the point where a project timetable becomes an exchange-access problem. Its self-custody migration opens on November 17, while some trading venues have scheduled restrictions before that date.

Recent findings suggest that the distinction matters because holders do not all follow the same process. A token in a personal wallet and a balance on an exchange may represent similar market exposure, but the organizations responsible for converting them are different.

Clearpool’s November 12 migration guide sets a one-for-one conversion and a February 17, 2027 deadline. It identifies CLEAR as an ERC-20 token on Ethereum. The guide separates holders using their own wallets from those whose exchanges will handle the migration.

Recent findings suggest that that separation is more useful than treating the announcement as a universal instruction to transfer tokens. Exchange support, snapshot rules and the blockchain on which a balance is held can affect the appropriate process.

The guide is the informational starting point for verifying those arrangements. The existence of a public migration should not make unsolicited messages or lookalike websites credible. A legitimate project announcement can be copied by an impersonator without changing its appearance very much.

KuCoin’s notice schedules CPOOL deposits and withdrawals to close at 04:00 UTC on November 16, followed by trading bots at 07:00 and the CPOOL/USDT market at 08:00. The exchange notes it will convert eligible balances automatically.

Recent findings suggest that its notice includes specific eligibility conditions: a minimum of 0.1 CPOOL and covered spot-account balances. Pending deposits or withdrawals at the snapshot are excluded. It also warns that later deposits of the old token will not be supported.

Industry observers note that these details show why the project deadline alone is insufficient. An exchange can stop accepting an asset months before the broader self-custody window ends. Its reopening schedule for the replacement asset is another separate milestone, which KuCoin says will be announced after the swap.

A holder exchanging 1,000 old tokens for 1,000 new tokens preserves the number of units in that transaction. The conversion does not establish the new market price, total supply or the holder’s percentage interest in the network’s token economy.

In a recent development, clearpool’s September expansion proposal paired the migration with treasury recapitalization and additional allocations. That document is background to the economic design; the November migration guide supplies the operational dates. The two should be read for their different purposes.

Industry observers note that newsBTC’s examination of Aave’s proposed division of lending revenue illustrates a related analytical point: an administrative parameter or token count is only one part of the underlying economics. Funding, incentives and realized activity still determine how a protocol develops.

In a recent development, clearpool has linked its broader plans to institutional credit and expansion toward the XRP Ledger. Completing a token conversion would be an operational milestone, while launching products and attracting borrowers would require separate evidence.

That distinction also appears in NewsBTC’s reporting on financing tokenized collateral. A working token or interface is one component; enforceable claims, usable liquidity and dependable servicing make the financial product useful.

For this week’s transition, the immediate questions are concrete: whether exchanges apply their published rules, when replacement balances appear and when the latest markets reopen. Those answers will reveal the quality of the migration more clearly than a change of ticker alone.

For traders relying on reading the charts, the current price of NVDA is running into another level that could decide whether the recovery has legs.

At around $159 on Monday, its weekly chart now places the $164.40 zone directly in the bulls' way.

According to recent reports, that level previously acted as support, a price where buyers stepped in. After the breakdown, it is turning into a level to watch as investors who bought earlier may look to sell once they get their money back. But it could mark a bounce point based on the longer timeframes—as it has for at least three times since September 2025.

According to recent reports, if Nvidia can reclaim $165 and hold above it, the next prominent resistance on the chart sits around $188 to $190. That would represent almost 20% upside from Monday's $159 price, although only about 16% from the breakout level, with possible selling pressure along the way.

Failure to clear $164.40 would put $152.62 back on the radar. Another break below that yellow support would weaken the case that last week's bounce marked a bottom.

The exponential moving averages, or EMAs, still offer some encouragement. Nvidia's 50-week EMA remains above its 200-week EMA, a bullish long-term configuration that gives more weight to recent prices but hasn't yet flipped bearish.

The shorter-term signals look less friendly. The Average Directional Index, or ADX, is around 23, suggesting a weakened trend (which is natural after the FUD episode). Its directional readings favor sellers. ADX measures trend strength, not direction by itself.

It has been revealed that the Relative Strength Index, or RSI, is near 31.6, barely above the conventional oversold threshold of 30. That can make a relief bounce more plausible, but oversold stocks can keep falling. Neither indicator confirms a reversal yet.

Nvidia's underlying business hasn't suddenly stopped growing. The chipmaker reported $96.2 billion in quarterly revenue in August, up 106% year over year, including $89 billion from its data center business.

Investors will also be watching profit margins and the enormous financing commitments tying Nvidia to the wider AI infrastructure boom.

According to recent reports, nvidia co-founder Jensen Huang resigned on November 12 amid reports of extramarital affairs involving Alice Huang, a businesswoman U.S. intelligence suspects of spying for China, and Nvidia executive Kimberly Powell. Reuters subsequently reported a third alleged relationship with another employee.

Chief Financial Officer Colette Kress is serving as interim CEO while an independent investigation into possible foreign-intelligence targeting continues. In a recent development, the Financial Times reported that Huang has spoken with allies about returning, while a petition calling for his reinstatement has attracted more than 178,000 signatures, including Elon Musk. The board has not revealed prepares to bring him back.

Sources indicate that for bulls, $164.40 remains the line to beat, and charts point to this outcome being quite possible. Assuming, of course, Nvidia's next big reveal is about chips and not a fourth love affair.

#825. Breaking: Bitcoin Miners Hijacked as Attackers Redirect BTC Through Luxor Breach

Breaking: Bitcoin Miners Hijacked as Attackers Redirect BTC Through Luxor Breach

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/bitcoin-miners-hijacked-as-attackers-redirect-btc-through-luxor-breach/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Bitcoin miners hijacked as mining infrastructure provider Luxor has confirmed a security breach involving its Commander management software, which allowed attackers to redirect computing power from more than a dozen customer accounts to another mining pool and change the addresses receiving their rewards.
  • Sources indicate that the incident left affected miners paying electricity costs while their machines continued working for someone else’s benefit.
  • The breach involved Commander, Luxor’s mining-management platform, which allows operators to monitor mining equipment and remotely adjust its settings.

Bitcoin miners hijacked as mining infrastructure provider Luxor has confirmed a security breach involving its Commander management software, which allowed attackers to redirect computing power from more than a dozen customer accounts to another mining pool and change the addresses receiving their rewards.

Sources indicate that the incident left affected miners paying electricity costs while their machines continued working for someone else’s benefit. Luxor said it detected the unauthorized activity on November 14, patched the software within two hours, and began restoring the original mining configurations. The company has also promised to reimburse affected customers in full.

The breach involved Commander, Luxor’s mining-management platform, which allows operators to monitor mining equipment and remotely adjust its settings.

Attackers used unauthorized access to change the mining pool configurations of affected machines and redirect their payout addresses. Instead of sending their computing power to the pools selected by their owners, the machines were pointed toward OCEAN, a Bitcoin mining pool where participants combine their hashrate and receive rewards based on their contributed work.

According to recent reports, this type of attack does not require criminals to physically access mining equipment or steal Bitcoin directly from people’ wallets. By changing the pool and payout settings, attackers can redirect the revenue generated by mining machines while their legitimate owners continue covering electricity and operating expenses.

In a recent development, the manufacturer also clarified that the incident was isolated to Commander. Its Luxor Pool and LuxOS services were not affected, and it reported no evidence that customer data had been leaked or extracted.

Blockchain activity indicates that the attackers managed to receive actual mining rewards during the incident.

According to recent reports, an address initially identified by mining host CoreX Hosting received three Bitcoin block-reward payments totaling approximately 0.243 BTC. At the time of reporting, the amount was valued at roughly $15,700.

OCEAN’s payout mechanism helps explain why rewards can arrive even after mining machines have stopped contributing. Its system allows previously submitted mining work to remain eligible for a share of subsequent block rewards over a rolling period. Consequently, payments can reach an address after the affected machines have already been returned to their original configurations.

The full financial impact remains unclear, and the identified payments do not establish the total amount of revenue diverted during the incident.

The incident may have affected considerably more computing power than the number of customer accounts confirmed by Luxor.

In a recent development, mining operators first raised concerns after noticing unauthorized changes to their equipment’s pool settings. CoreX Hosting reportedly identified the suspicious activity and helped alert other affected operators.

Recent findings suggest that the redirected hashrate subsequently dropped sharply, with reports indicating that it had fallen to approximately 100 petahashes per second. This suggested that most of the affected computing power had been restored or was no longer contributing to the suspicious pool.

Luxor CEO Nick Hansen described the intrusion as involving a sophisticated AI-enabled attack, warning that cryptocurrency businesses are facing increasingly advanced cybersecurity threats.

However, he did not explain precisely how artificial intelligence was used in the breach or disclose how the attackers initially gained access to Commander.

Sources indicate that hansen also mentioned Luxor had paused much of its new feature development to focus on strengthening its security infrastructure. The tech giant has reportedly acquired dedicated GPUs to run its own AI models for defensive security testing.

The warning comes amid growing concerns about the use of artificial intelligence in cyberattacks targeting cryptocurrency companies and blockchain infrastructure providers. AI tools can potentially help attackers identify vulnerabilities and automate parts of the exploitation process, although the specific role of AI in this incident has not been independently established.

According to recent reports, the incident highlights a security risk that extends beyond cryptocurrency exchanges and wallet providers. Mining management platforms also control access to valuable infrastructure and determine where the rewards generated by computing power are sent.

Even without directly stealing equipment or accessing miners’ existing Bitcoin balances, attackers who gain control of mining configurations can redirect future earnings and leave operators responsible for the associated costs.

Luxor’s compensation commitment addresses the immediate financial impact for affected customers, but the incident raises broader questions about access controls, monitoring systems, and the security of remotely managed mining operations.

Will Luxor’s promise to fully reimburse affected customers be enough to restore confidence in its mining management software?

#827. Vitalik Buterin Backs Faster Route to Quantum-Safe Ethereum With Newly introduced Proposal

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4 min read (849 words)
General

Vitalik Buterin Backs Faster Route to Quantum-Safe Ethereum With Newly introduced Proposal

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/vitalik-buterin-backs-faster-route-to-quantum-safe-ethereum-with-new-proposal/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has thrown his support behind leanPCS, a cryptographic technique that could help the blockchain prepare for future quantum computing threats without significantly increasing transaction costs or on-chain data requirements.
  • Buterin’s change of position centers on EIP-8288, a draft proposal designed to combine large digital signatures and cryptographic proofs into a shared mathematical proof.
  • In a November 16 post on X, Buterin described his change of view, writing that he had gone from considering leanPCS “total bull” to becoming “a total bull” on the approach.

Ethereum co-founder Vitalik Buterin has thrown his support behind leanPCS, a cryptographic technique that could help the blockchain prepare for future quantum computing threats without significantly increasing transaction costs or on-chain data requirements.

Buterin’s change of position centers on EIP-8288, a draft proposal designed to combine large digital signatures and cryptographic proofs into a shared mathematical proof. Instead of requiring Ethereum to store every quantum-resistant signature individually, the approach would allow computers to aggregate verification data before transactions are added to the blockchain.

In a November 16 post on X, Buterin described his change of view, writing that he had gone from considering leanPCS “total bull” to becoming “a total bull” on the approach.

The proposal addresses one of Ethereum’s biggest potential challenges in preparing for quantum-resistant cryptography: the significantly larger size of the signatures and proofs that would replace today’s cryptographic standards.

Buterin’s endorsement reflects growing confidence in a method that could make Ethereum’s transition toward quantum resistance more practical.

In a recent development, current Ethereum signatures typically occupy around 65 bytes. By comparison, some quantum-resistant alternatives could require between 1,000 and 6,000 bytes, according to Buterin. Certain cryptographic proofs used by privacy applications could also expand from a few hundred bytes to approximately 128 kilobytes.

Storing this additional information directly on Ethereum would consume considerably more block space. That could increase the cost of transactions and make it more expensive for consumers to interact with decentralized applications.

The approach relies on polynomial commitment schemes, mathematical tools used in cryptographic proof systems. By standardizing a shared verification component, different proof systems could use the same underlying mechanism without requiring developers to adopt an identical architecture.

Buterin believes this could provide Ethereum with a faster route toward supporting quantum-resistant accounts and more advanced cryptographic applications.

In a recent development, under the design, users would continue submitting signatures or cryptographic proofs to demonstrate that transactions and other operations are valid. However, rather than storing every large signature individually, network participants could combine multiple verification results into aggregated proofs.

In a recent development, ethereum would only need to retain the transaction instructions and sufficient information to verify the aggregated result. The full collection of bulky signatures and proofs would not need to be permanently stored on-chain.

The benefits could also extend beyond wallet security. Privacy applications that rely on zero-knowledge proofs could use the same approach to demonstrate that transactions follow the required rules without revealing sensitive information.

By reducing the amount of data that needs to be recorded individually, proof aggregation could make more advanced cryptographic features practical without placing the entire storage burden on Ethereum customers.

EIP-8288 outlines three possible approaches to handling the larger signatures and proofs required by quantum-resistant systems.

Industry observers note that the first, leanSPHINCS, is the most specialized option. It would support a particular family of hash-based quantum-resistant signatures, offering a relatively straightforward path toward protecting Ethereum accounts. However, its functionality would be limited to that signature system.

At the other end of the spectrum is leanSTARK, a more general approach that could support different signature schemes, privacy applications, and more complex verification processes. Its implementation would require Ethereum developers to agree on a upcoming programming language for the programs being verified.

That decision could represent a substantial architectural change for Ethereum, potentially extending beyond its existing Ethereum Virtual Machine (EVM) framework.

In a recent development, this is the approach Buterin now favors, arguing that it could be introduced considerably sooner. The broader leanSTARK framework could potentially follow later, allowing Ethereum to expand its cryptographic capabilities over time.

Buterin described the opportunity as a route toward a “cryptographic proof singularity” much sooner than developers had previously expected.

Buterin’s latest endorsement comes as Ethereum developers increasingly prioritize protection against potential quantum computing threats.

The Ethereum Foundation established a dedicated post-quantum research team earlier in 2026, while developers have been exploring changes to account authentication, validator keys, and privacy-related cryptography.

EIP-8288 could become an important component of this broader effort by addressing the additional data and verification costs associated with quantum-resistant systems.

Industry observers note that however, the proposal remains a draft, and its reference implementation is unfinished. Buterin’s support does not mean that leanPCS has been approved for deployment or assigned a mainnet activation date.

If the approach proves practical, it could help the network adopt stronger cryptographic protections while limiting the impact on transaction fees and blockchain storage requirements.

Do you think leanPCS could significantly accelerate Ethereum’s transition toward quantum-resistant security?

Saylor’s Strategy Keeps Buying Bitcoin, Adding 'A Little Orange' Through the Dip.

Strategy kept buying Bitcoin through a brutal market stretch, adding 485 BTC worth roughly $33.4 million and repurchasing $228 million of its preferred stock, as chairman Michael Saylor urged the market to rally with a characteristically cheeky nudge.

Sources indicate that the company disclosed the purchase in a filing Monday. The modest addition, small by the standards of a firm that once bought tens of thousands of coins at a time, lifted Strategy’s total holdings to 850,849 BTC as of Nov. 15, alongside $4.9 billion in U.S. dollar assets.

Strategy, the largest corporate holder of Bitcoin, remains far ahead of any other treasury tech giant.

Sources indicate that the buy caps a stretch of smaller, steadier accumulation paired with stock buybacks. Strategy recently added $82 million in Bitcoin while repurchasing $188 million of its STRC preferred shares, part of a shift toward what it calls a capital-management approach, buying back stock when it views the shares as undervalued rather than relentlessly stacking coins.

Bitcoin has slid sharply in recent days, trading well below the six-figure highs it touched earlier in the cycle, and the downturn has squeezed Bitcoin treasury firms whose valuations rise and fall with the asset.

Saylor, undeterred, posted the holdings patch to X alongside the firm’s trademark Bitcoin tracker, and followed it with a quip aimed at the slumping market: “This dip could use a little orange,” a nod to Bitcoin’s signature color.

It has been revealed that the purchase lands during a precarious moment for the treasury-organization model Strategy pioneered. Index provider MSCI has finalized rules that could eject Bitcoin treasury firms like Strategy from its widely tracked equity indexes, classifying companies whose balance sheets are dominated by a single asset as “non-operating” and therefore ineligible.

Removal would force index-tracking funds to sell the affected shares, potentially pressuring prices and shrinking the premium these firms have long commanded over the value of their Bitcoin.

For now, Strategy is doing what it has always done, buying Bitcoin and talking it up, even as the market tests its conviction.

The combination of a small purchase and a sizable buyback underscores the balancing act: keep accumulating, defend the stock, and weather a downturn that has turned the once-unstoppable treasury trade into a far more fraught proposition.

#830. German Bundestag Lets Customs Freeze Crypto Over €100,000 Without a Criminal Case as the Bill Goes to the Bundesrat

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 4 min read (742 words)
General

German Bundestag Lets Customs Freeze Crypto Over €100,000 Without a Criminal Case as the Bill Goes to the Bundesrat

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/german-bundestag-crypto-over-100000

💡 Key Takeaways
  • The German Bundestag on Thursday approved a government bill that would let customs freeze cryptocurrency and other assets worth more than €100,000 when their lawful origin appears implausible, without first opening a criminal case.
  • The Bundestag passed the Customs Financial Justice Act, a Finance Ministry overhaul to strengthen the customs administration and fight financial crime, on Nov.
  • It has been revealed that crypto is covered expressly, using the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets definition, but it is not singled out.

The German Bundestag on Thursday approved a government bill that would let customs freeze cryptocurrency and other assets worth more than €100,000 when their lawful origin appears implausible, without first opening a criminal case. Permanent confiscation would still take a finance-court judgment. The measure still needs the Bundesrat’s consent before a planned Jan. 1, 2027 start, and the timing of that upper-house vote remains unclear.

The Bundestag passed the Customs Financial Justice Act, a Finance Ministry overhaul to strengthen the customs administration and fight financial crime, on Nov. 12. The federal government introduced the bill on Sept. 30. The Finance Committee recommended passage on Nov. 11, with the Christian Democrats, Social Democrats and Alternative for Germany in favor, The Left opposed and the Greens abstaining.

It has been revealed that crypto is covered expressly, using the European Union’s Markets in Crypto-Assets definition, but it is not singled out. The same administrative procedure applies to cash, cars, real estate and other property. It reaches only “significant” assets: generally those worth more than €100,000, or more than €50,000 if the asset must be entered in a public register, such as vehicles or land. Because crypto is not registered that way, the €100,000 threshold applies. Customs may estimate the value, and closely related items can be treated as one asset.

Customs offices — not Germany’s Financial Intelligence Unit, which the same bill strengthens separately — may freeze those assets for up to 30 days without a criminal case if there are factual indications the origin is not lawful, meaning lawful acquisition “does not appear plausible.” A finance court may extend that hold once by 150 days. That extension is decided by a single judge, without a hearing, in an order that cannot be appealed. Filing a confiscation application stops the clock until the court rules, so the often-cited 180-day period is not a hard cap.

Permanent confiscation still requires a finance-court panel to be convinced the origin is unlawful. The committee shifted that decision away from a single judge. Owners must be told they are not required to produce records, and anything they do provide may be used in tax and criminal cases. The official justification states mere silence, or a denial of knowledge, will as a rule not be enough to prevent confiscation.

Finance Minister Lars Klingbeil stated in August that if suspects cannot show assets were legally acquired, “the Porsche or the Rolex are gone for now.” In Thursday’s debate, Social Democrat Ingo Vogel told the Bundestag that criminally acquired assets do not enjoy constitutional property protection, and that the bill is “no automatic confiscation” and “no blanket reversal of the burden of proof.”.

The Bundesrat, in an earlier comment, had asked for a true burden-of-proof reversal and for the court extension to run up to 12 months, citing, among other things, “crypto concealment structures.” The government refused the fuller reversal and did not adopt the longer hold in the bill the Bundestag approved.

Germany’s Federal Bar Association opposes the bill, warning that vague terms and missing paperwork, including for inherited assets, should not be treated as proof of illegality. The German Bar Association also rejected the government draft. The Blockchain Bundesverband, commenting on the ministry draft, noted the law needed to distinguish custodial, self-custodied and decentralized arrangements, because with a self-custodied wallet control “regularly lies with the holder of the private key,” and state access then exists only through measures against the person, not through third parties. The bill itself is silent on how, or whether, customs could take self-custodied keys. A freeze of crypto would be carried out by attachment under the Tax Code.

According to recent reports, the government expects about €308 million a year in extra revenue from 2028 from the procedure as a whole, not from crypto alone. The Greens argued that figure is a sliver of Germany’s estimated €100 billion annual money-laundering volume.

The new power is separate from an earlier criminal case. In 2024, Saxony’s prosecutors, with the Federal Criminal Police Office, sold about 49,858 bitcoin from the Movie2k case between June 19 and July 12, for €2.64 billion. That sale was an emergency liquidation in a criminal proceeding, not an exercise of the administrative tool the Bundestag has now approved.

  • Solana officially exits “mainnet beta” label it carried for more than six years, marking a latest milestone in the blockchain’s development since its launch in March 2020.
  • The Solana Foundation announced the change on November 16, explaining that the beta label no longer reflected the network’s current status.

Solana officially exits “mainnet beta” label it carried for more than six years, marking a latest milestone in the blockchain’s development since its launch in March 2020. The network will now operate under the Solana Mainnet name, while a new shared protocol designation, Solana 1.0, will provide a common reference for its underlying rules.

The Solana Foundation announced the change on November 16, explaining that the beta label no longer reflected the network’s current status. Solana has been processing live transactions and supporting applications since its genesis block, making the designation increasingly outdated.

The upgrade does not introduce an immediate change for consumers. SOL balances, wallets, accounts, applications, and transaction histories will remain unaffected, and no action is required from token holders.

The removal of the beta designation represents a change in how Solana identifies its network rather than a new blockchain launch.

Since March 2020, the network has operated under the name Solana Mainnet Beta. The foundation remarked the label remained in place despite the blockchain functioning as a live production network throughout its development. Under the latest system, the blockchain will simply be referred to as Solana Mainnet. Solana 1.0 will serve as a shared version number describing the network’s protocol rules.

In a recent development, this distinction is important because Solana relies on different validator software implementations, each with its own development schedule and version numbers. Previously, these individual releases could make it harder for developers and infrastructure operators to identify which network rules were supported across different clients.

The latest protocol version provides a common reference point, allowing operators to track network changes without relying on the release number of a particular software implementation.

The decision to retire the beta label follows several infrastructure improvements intended to strengthen Solana’s performance and reliability.

One of the most significant developments is Alpenglow, a consensus upgrade activated on the network in October. The upgrade changes how validators reach agreement and aims to reduce transaction finality to approximately 150 milliseconds, compared with the previous 12.8 seconds.

Transaction finality refers to the point at which the network considers a transaction settled. Faster finality can improve the experience for applications that depend on rapid confirmations, including trading platforms and other real-time services. Another key development is Firedancer, an independently developed validator client created by Jump Crypto. It provides an alternative to Agave, the network’s existing client implementation.

Running multiple independent clients can improve network resilience by reducing reliance on a single codebase. If one implementation experiences a software glitch, the presence of another can help limit the potential impact on the broader network.

Solana’s infrastructure developments come as the network maintains significant activity across decentralized finance and digital asset markets.

Recent findings suggest that according to DefiLlama figures, approximately $4.66 billion was deposited in Solana-based decentralized finance applications. The network also held around $14 billion in circulating stablecoins. Solana-based decentralized exchanges processed approximately $1.28 billion in trading volume over the 24 hours preceding the report.

These figures highlight the scale of the ecosystem operating on the blockchain, which now supports a broad range of financial applications and digital assets.

Despite the network’s milestone, SOL was trading near $70 at the time of the report, down approximately 3% over 24 hours. The naming change itself does not introduce any direct improvement to transaction costs or speed, meaning the token’s market performance will continue to depend on broader market conditions and developments across the ecosystem.

Solana’s decision to retire the beta label marks a symbolic milestone, but the introduction of shared protocol versioning also has practical implications for the network’s technical development.

Industry observers note that for everyday people, the transition requires no action. Existing SOL holdings, accounts, applications, and transaction records will remain exactly as they were. Developers and infrastructure operators, however, will need to pay attention to the new versioning system. Validator and RPC operators should check which Agave and Firedancer releases support each protocol rollout, while application developers will need to continue monitoring relevant software and infrastructure updates.

The change also reflects Solana’s growing emphasis on independent client implementations and coordinated network upgrades. As the ecosystem expands, having a shared protocol reference could make it easier for different development teams to work toward the same technical standards.

According to recent reports, after more than six years under the mainnet beta designation, Solana is now presenting itself as a mature production network. Whether its latest infrastructure improvements translate into sustained growth will depend on continued adoption, developer activity, and the network’s ability to maintain reliability as usage increases.

Will upgrades such as Alpenglow and Firedancer help Solana strengthen its position against competing blockchain networks?

'Tokenization Is Not the Finish Line': Jupiter to Let Customers Borrow Against Bullish Shares.

Jupiter, the largest trading platform on Solana, is bringing Bullish's shares onchain as collateral, as part of a push to put tokenized assets to work.

It has been revealed that the firm will launch a dedicated, permissioned market on its lending platform, Jupiter Lend, starting with Bullish's NYSE-listed BLSH stock, Jupiter tweeted on Monday. More issuer tokens will follow, though the market won't be available in all jurisdictions, it added.

A NYSE-listed organization is bringing its own shares directly to Jupiter Lend.

Today at Breakpoint, we declared our partnership with @Bullish to launch a dedicated, permissioned $BLSH market.

For the first time, Issuer Tokens can be used as collateral inside Solana’s… pic.twitter.com/rWWqwOcWmK.

— Jupiter (@JupiterExchange) November 16, 2026.

Unlike many tokenized stocks, which give holders a claim on a share, Bullish's issuer-sponsored token "is itself the share," Jupiter COO Kash Dhanda noted in a presentation at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London.

It has been revealed that people will be able to borrow against them with fully onchain liquidations in an "institutional-grade lending market," and integrations with qualified custodians, he said. Bullish acquired Equiniti, one of the world's largest transfer agents, earlier this year, Dhanda noted.

Dhanda framed the announcements around what he called the "post-tokenization era." Most tokenized assets today are "parked, not productive," he said.

Of the roughly $460 billion in tokenized assets tracked by data platform RWA.xyz, only about $39.5 billion is actually onchain and can be moved off the issuer's platform, and just $3.4 billion is used in DeFi, according to DeFiLlama, Dhanda said, a "utilization gap" of 99%.

"There is this myth, and this is the thing that's misunderstood: 'If you put it on chain, they will come'," he remarked. "This is not the field of dreams," he added, arguing that, "Tokenization is not the finish line. It is actually the starting line.".

Jupiter launched two other products alongside the Bullish market. The Jupiter Global Passport lets customers verify their identity to buy permissioned assets, while keeping their information as private as possible using zero-knowledge data sharing, Dhanda remarked. It is live with KYC verification, with onchain credit scores and proof of wealth to follow, and the firm is exploring licenses in different jurisdictions.

Industry observers note that jupiter Liquidity Services, meanwhile, will help asset issuers design their markets, seed initial capital, find market makers and integrate with Jupiter's routing so that their tokens are available across the platforms that use it. "You integrate once, you will be available everywhere," Dhanda mentioned.

"Shallow credit markets don't drive liquidity on chain," he added. "If you cannot do more with your onchain asset than you can do with the off-chain version of it, you're probably not going to switch.".

Jupiter notes it has handled more than $500 billion in trading volume so far this year and paid out $162 million in yield. The Breakpoint announcements follow the firm's launch last week of token baskets, yield vaults and a rebuilt portfolio, and come as other venues bring tokenized stocks to Solana. Trading platform Formation has notified the SEC of prepares to trade tokenized U.S. stocks on the network.

Jupiter powers token swaps on The Information Exchange, Decrypt's trading platform.

#835. Kava Lend Exploit Drains $3.8M in KAVA as Token Price Plunges Nearly 40%

Kava Lend Exploit Drains $3.8M in KAVA as Token Price Plunges Nearly 40%

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinist.com/kava-lend-exploit-drains-3-8m-in-kava-as-token-price-plunges-nearly-40/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Kava Lend, the decentralized lending protocol operating on the Kava blockchain, has suffered an exploit that allowed an attacker to drain approximately 55.2 million KAVA tokens, worth around $3.76 million before the incident.
  • According to recent reports, the exploit occurred late Friday, November 13, and involved manipulating a largely inactive BUSD lending market to artificially inflate the value of deposited collateral.
  • It has been revealed that approximately 49.2 million of the stolen tokens were subsequently transferred to BNB Chain through LayerZero, where most were sold for roughly $2.1 million in BNB and USDT.

Kava Lend, the decentralized lending protocol operating on the Kava blockchain, has suffered an exploit that allowed an attacker to drain approximately 55.2 million KAVA tokens, worth around $3.76 million before the incident. The attack triggered a sharp sell-off, sending KAVA down nearly 40% as concerns spread across the ecosystem.

According to recent reports, the exploit occurred late Friday, November 13, and involved manipulating a largely inactive BUSD lending market to artificially inflate the value of deposited collateral. The attacker then repeatedly borrowed KAVA against the inflated deposits, according to on-chain data reviewed by The Block.

It has been revealed that approximately 49.2 million of the stolen tokens were subsequently transferred to BNB Chain through LayerZero, where most were sold for roughly $2.1 million in BNB and USDT. Kava confirmed the incident but stated it was contained within Kava Lend and did not involve an unlimited token mint.

The attack exploited a weakness in Kava Lend’s BUSD market, which had very little activity and liquidity before the incident. BUSD, the Binance-branded stablecoin issued by Paxos, has not been minted since 2023. However, its market remained operational on Kava Lend, creating an opportunity for the attacker to manipulate the protocol’s calculations.

Sources indicate that according to the public source code, Kava Lend calculates deposit interest using the market’s net supply. Although the system prevents calculations when that figure reaches exactly zero, it does not adequately account for extremely small positive values. The attacker reportedly used a small BUSD loan to reduce the market’s net supply to an almost negligible amount. This caused the protocol to dramatically overestimate the value of deposits, multiplying their recorded value by approximately 243,000 times.

According to recent reports, as a result, collateral deposited by the attacker was treated as worth roughly 1.25 billion BUSD, despite its actual value being substantially lower. The inflated collateral then allowed the attacker to borrow large quantities of KAVA from the lending pool.

After manipulating the BUSD market, the attacker borrowed KAVA 127 times, using a second account to clear individual loans and bypass the protocol’s borrowing limits.

On-chain activity suggests the operation was prepared in advance. The attacker had reportedly conducted repeated deposit and borrowing transactions in the BUSD market beginning November 8, several days before the exploit. The consequences became visible when Kava Lend’s pooled account, which held approximately 55.33 million KAVA before the incident, was left with just 0.19 KAVA.

At around 4:59 a.m. ET on Saturday, the attacker began transferring the stolen tokens to BNB Chain through Kava’s LayerZero bridge. Approximately 49.2 million KAVA was moved across the network, with most of it sold within an hour. The transactions generated roughly 3,006.5 BNB and 231,557 USDT, worth approximately $2.09 million combined. Another 4.58 million KAVA was distributed across five addresses that had not been identified publicly.

The exploit triggered an immediate reaction across the Kava ecosystem, with KAVA experiencing a sharp decline in market value.

The token was trading near $0.042 at the time of the report, representing a drop of approximately 39% over 24 hours. Before the attack, KAVA was valued at around $0.068, placing the 55.2 million drained tokens at approximately $3.76 million.

Several partner exchanges also suspended KAVA deposits and withdrawals as a precautionary measure. Kava described the exchange restrictions as standard security measures following the incident.

According to recent reports, the team additionally announced that it had paused the Axelar bridge to reduce potential risks while investigating the situation. Although the stolen tokens were transferred through LayerZero rather than Axelar, the decision was presented as a precaution.

According to recent reports, kava stated that the incident was isolated to Kava Lend and emphasized that it did not involve an infinite mint. However, the project had not published an official loss assessment or a complete post-incident report at the time.

The incident highlights the risks associated with poorly maintained lending markets and vulnerabilities in the calculations used by decentralized finance protocols.

Dormant markets can remain exposed even when their underlying assets have little liquidity or trading activity. In this case, an extremely small net supply value allowed the attacker to manipulate collateral calculations and borrow tokens against deposits that were significantly overvalued.

For Kava, the immediate priorities will be completing its investigation, assessing the impact on owners, and explaining how the vulnerability will be addressed. The recovery of KAVA’s market value may also depend on whether the team can restore confidence in the protocol and provide greater clarity about potential losses.

Are dormant lending markets becoming a major security weakness for DeFi protocols, and should platforms disable markets with little or no activity?

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Solana Drops 'Mainnet Beta' After Six Years: Here's What 1.0 Is All About.
  • Solana is officially out of beta, more than six years after launching a blockchain that has been handling real money the whole time.
  • Industry observers note that the Solana Foundation on Monday retired the “mainnet beta” label and introduced Solana 1.0, a shared version number for the network's underlying rules.

Solana Drops 'Mainnet Beta' After Six Years: Here's What 1.0 Is All About.

Solana is officially out of beta, more than six years after launching a blockchain that has been handling real money the whole time.

Industry observers note that the Solana Foundation on Monday retired the “mainnet beta” label and introduced Solana 1.0, a shared version number for the network's underlying rules. The change is primarily about how developers and validator operators coordinate software updates, not a fresh boost to transaction speed or any other meaningful improvement over what users already have.

Solana debuted its mainnet beta on March 16, 2020, and kept the experimental-sounding name even as consumers traded tokens, built applications, and moved assets across the chain.

According to recent reports, nothing happens to those assets now. “Your SOL, accounts, assets, applications, and transaction history remain the same,” the Foundation said. People don't need to swap tokens, move wallets or install anything to keep using the network.

According to recent reports, solana has two major validator clients: Agave, developed by Anza, and Firedancer, built independently by Jump Crypto. Each has its own code, release schedule and version numbers, which can make it harder to tell whether different software releases support the same network features.

Solana 1.0 creates a common reference point for the protocol itself. An Agave release and a Firedancer release can support the same protocol version without sharing a software version number.

It has been revealed that that distinction matters as the network relies on more than one software implementation. A bug in one client need not affect every validator, although software diversity alone cannot guarantee the network will stay online.

“Announcing a protocol version does not activate every associated improvement at once,” the Foundation warned. Operators still need to check whether their particular software supports a planned upgrade and follow its activation instructions.

According to recent reports, the Foundation stated it coordinated the change with Anza and the Firedancer team. Its announcement does not describe a new voting system or a change in who governs Solana; the network's governance process for proposals remains separate.

The Foundation credits engineering work that preceded Monday's announcement, particularly Alpenglow and Firedancer. Solana's Alpenglow upgrade went live on October 21, replacing the system validators had used to reach agreement since launch.

According to recent reports, alpenglow targets transaction finality of roughly 150 milliseconds, compared with about 12.8 seconds previously. Finality is the point at which a transaction is considered settled; that improvement came from the October upgrade, not from calling the network 1.0.

Sources indicate that firedancer also reached mainnet in 2025, giving validators a separately developed alternative to Agave. That reduces dependence on a single codebase, though the extent of the protection depends on how widely different clients are actually used.

Solana has reasons to be careful with promises of reliability. Its network went offline for nearly five hours in February 2024, following an outage lasting almost 19 hours a year earlier.

Documentation and block explorers will gradually adopt the upcoming mainnet name, according to the Foundation. Its upgrade tracker still lists Agave 4.4 as planned for November and Agave 4.5 for December, each with its own release and activation requirements.

Nvidia earnings could determine whether Wall Street’s AI trade stages a recovery or faces another wave of selling. The chipmaker is preparing to report its fiscal third-quarter 2027 results on November 17, with analysts expecting revenue of nearly $109 billion. However, strong financial results may not be enough to satisfy investors. Concerns surrounding AI spending, rising memory costs and leadership uncertainty have increased the pressure on the company. With Nvidia shares facing renewed volatility, can its latest earnings restore confidence in AI stocks, or is Wall Street preparing for another sell-off?

According to recent reports, nvidia faces exceptionally high expectations heading into its latest earnings report. Wall Street analysts expect the company to generate approximately $108.85 billion in revenue and $2.47 in adjusted earnings per share for fiscal Q3 2027. That would represent revenue growth of roughly 91% from $57.01 billion reported in the same quarter last year.

The firm had previously guided for third-quarter revenue of $108 billion, plus or minus 2%, putting its official forecast broadly in line with analyst expectations. The previous quarter provides a strong benchmark. Nvidia reported $96.2 billion in Q2 FY2027 revenue, up 106% year over year, while adjusted earnings reached $2.22 per share. Its Data Center business generated $89 billion, accounting for the overwhelming majority of quarterly revenue.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia’s Data Center business remains the biggest driver of its valuation, making this segment the most vital part of the upcoming earnings report. Analyst estimates put fiscal Q3 Data Center revenue at approximately $101.8 billion. Recent findings suggest that investors will also examine the company’s Vera Rubin platform, which is expected to become an increasingly notable contributor to future revenue. Sources indicate that the bigger question is whether hyperscalers and AI companies will continue spending aggressively on computing capacity. Microsoft, Amazon, Google and other major technology companies remain crucial customers in the AI infrastructure cycle.

If Nvidia signals that demand remains strong into fiscal 2028, it could support sentiment across the semiconductor sector. Any indication of slower orders or delayed infrastructure spending, however, could pressure not only NVDA but also AMD, Broadcom and other AI-linked stocks.

Recent findings suggest that nvidia’s earnings call will face another notable test: whether rising costs and business uncertainty are beginning to affect its growth outlook. The organization previously guided for a non-GAAP gross margin of approximately 74% in fiscal Q3. However, management also warned that higher memory costs could push margins lower in the following quarter, with a projected range of 71%–72% for Q4 FY2027.

In a recent development, china exposure is another issue investors will monitor. Nvidia’s previous Q3 revenue outlook did not assume any Data Center compute revenue from China, leaving investors to assess how much additional growth could come from other markets.

Leadership uncertainty adds another layer to the earnings event. Recent reports surrounding Jensen Huang’s departure and the organization’s leadership transition have increased investor concerns ahead of the results. Interim leadership will need to reassure investors about product execution, customer relationships and the company’s long-term strategy.

The earnings call could therefore matter as much as the financial numbers. Investors will be looking for clear answers on future demand, margins and management’s confidence in the AI growth cycle.

#839. DTCC, Barclays Say Tokenization's Real Prize Is Unlocking Idle Collateral

DTCC, Barclays Say Tokenization's Real Prize Is Unlocking Idle Collateral

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read | Sumber: https://decrypt.co/383316/dtcc-barclays-say-tokenizations-real-prize-is-unlocking-idle-collateral

💡 Key Takeaways
  • DTCC, Barclays Say Tokenization's Real Prize Is Unlocking Idle Collateral.
  • The biggest payoff from tokenizing traditional assets won't come from simply putting them onchain, but from putting idle collateral to work, according to executives at the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) and Barclays.
  • "You can tokenize an asset, but if you can't do anything with it, what's the point?" Val Wooton, DTCC's global head of equities solutions, said at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London.

DTCC, Barclays Say Tokenization's Real Prize Is Unlocking Idle Collateral.

The biggest payoff from tokenizing traditional assets won't come from simply putting them onchain, but from putting idle collateral to work, according to executives at the Depository Trust & Clearing Corporation (DTCC) and Barclays.

"You can tokenize an asset, but if you can't do anything with it, what's the point?" Val Wooton, DTCC's global head of equities solutions, said at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London. "For me, it really is around collateral and liquidity.".

Scott Lucas, head of digital assets at Barclays, agreed. A lot of collateral sits "relatively idle" at central securities depositories, he remarked, and much of the early value for banks will come from moving it more efficiently between their own accounts, before extending that to clients. "There's a lot of money in good housekeeping," he added.

The pair spoke on a panel days after DTCC confirmed that its tokenization service will connect to Solana, with tokenized assets expected on the network in the second half of 2027.

The service, which introduced on October 28, can tokenize assets held at DTCC's depository, starting with Russell 1000 stocks, ETFs tracking major indexes, and U.S. Treasury bills and bonds, Wooton said. The tokens carry the same legal and economic rights as traditionally held securities, and adding Solana reflects DTCC's strategy of being "open," "interoperable" and "multi-network," he added.

Wooton said the biggest opportunity lies in "liquidity optimization," which he said could save "millions, if not billions" of dollars by letting firms move assets that are currently stuck when markets are closed.

Large financial institutions today over-fund and over-collateralize every day because they treat collateral as "just in case," he stated. Moving assets onchain, around the clock, would let firms manage collateral "just in time," freeing up "a significant amount of balance sheet" to put to other uses. He added that the ability to move assets and settle them atomically could be "extremely powerful" in times of market stress.

Lucas pointed to Barclays' participation in DTCC's tokenization launch last month, one of the bank's first public moves into the space, and described the efficiency gains from managing its own collateral as good housekeeping.

Barclays is also working with Ironlight on tokenized structured products, Lucas stated, though he stressed "it's not a done deal." He added that he would like to see Solana adopted by other central securities depositories around the world, building a shared infrastructure layer across Asia-Pacific, Europe and the United States.

Industry observers note that both executives stated adoption remains early. Wooton said the industry is "still in the crawl stage," and that traditional and digital rails will exist side by side "for quite a long time," though DTCC's clients are already tokenizing assets daily.

According to recent reports, lucas remarked he tries to stay "healthily skeptical" about the speed of adoption while making sure Barclays is ready for its clients. At a recent traditional finance conference in Miami, he said, "every institution we met had money on the table," making investments and building products, a shift from a year earlier, when most were still asking questions.

Barclays has been gradually expanding its crypto activities. The bank invested in U.S. stablecoin startup Ubyx earlier this year and has reportedly weighed a push into tokenized deposits and stablecoin payments, according to Bloomberg. It was also among the investors backing crypto custodian Copper in 2022.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Harvard Management Manufacturer left its stake in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust unchanged at 3,044,612 shares in the third quarter, a position valued at $144.1 million as of Sept.
  • In a recent development, the university’s endowment manager disclosed the holding in a Form 13F filed Friday, covering the quarter ended Sept.
  • In a recent development, the same 3,044,612 shares were worth $101.4 million on June 30 and $117.0 million on March 31, so the position rose in value during the third quarter as bitcoin recovered, then gave back a large share of that gain after the quarter ended.

Harvard Management Manufacturer left its stake in BlackRock’s iShares Bitcoin Trust unchanged at 3,044,612 shares in the third quarter, a position valued at $144.1 million as of Sept. 30 and now worth about $110.6 million after bitcoin’s slide.

In a recent development, the university’s endowment manager disclosed the holding in a Form 13F filed Friday, covering the quarter ended Sept. 30. The share count is the same one Harvard reported on June 30 and on March 31. At 10:40 a.m. ET Monday, IBIT traded at $36.32, putting the stake at about $110.6 million, a paper decline of roughly $33.6 million, or 23%, from the value in the filing. The Sept. 30 close of $47.34 matches the price implied by the reported value.

In a recent development, the same 3,044,612 shares were worth $101.4 million on June 30 and $117.0 million on March 31, so the position rose in value during the third quarter as bitcoin recovered, then gave back a large share of that gain after the quarter ended. Even after the November slide, the stake is still worth more than it was at midyear.

IBIT was Harvard’s eighth-largest position among 18 holdings in a 13F portfolio valued at $3.95 billion, or about 3.6% of that publicly disclosed book of U.S. securities, which does not include the rest of the endowment. The largest holding was Space Exploration Technologies, reported at $1.29 billion. Taiwan Semiconductor Manufacturing was second, at $616.5 million. That ranking is a sharp change from late 2025, when the bitcoin ETF was Harvard’s largest publicly disclosed position.

Harvard first reported an IBIT position in its filing for the quarter ended June 30, 2025: 1,906,000 shares worth $116.7 million. It had not listed the fund in earlier 13Fs, including the report for March 31, 2025. By Sept. 30, 2025, Harvard had tripled the stake to 6,813,612 shares, valued at $442.9 million, making IBIT its largest public holding.

The endowment trimmed that position by about 21% in the fourth quarter of 2025, to 5,353,612 shares worth $265.8 million, and opened a first stake in BlackRock’s iShares Ethereum Trust of 3,870,900 shares, valued at $86.8 million. It cut the bitcoin ETF again in the first quarter of 2026, by about 2.31 million shares, or 43%, to the 3,044,612 shares it still reported on Sept. 30, and sold the Ethereum fund entirely. The latest filing lists no other bitcoin or crypto ETFs. The remaining IBIT position is still larger, in share terms, than the 1.91 million shares Harvard first disclosed.

It has been revealed that harvard’s gold ETFs are now much larger than its bitcoin position. The same 13F lists 1,161,000 shares of SPDR Gold Shares worth $442.2 million, the portfolio’s third-largest holding, and 1,980,085 shares of the iShares Gold Trust worth $154.6 million. Combined, the two gold funds were valued at $596.8 million, more than four times the IBIT stake. The iShares Gold Trust share count was unchanged from June 30. The SPDR Gold Shares position jumped from 58,862 shares at midyear.

Bitcoin traded near $64,200 as of 10:40 a.m. ET Monday, down about 17% in November from an Oct. 31 close near $77,400, and down about 23% from about $83,550 at the end of September. Since the quarter closed, U.S. spot bitcoin ETFs have been seeing heavy redemptions. IBIT bled about $2 billion over nine straight sessions through mid-November, and the funds as a group extended their outflow streak to seven sessions through Friday, losing about $1.91 billion since Nov. 5.

Recent findings suggest that the 13F is a snapshot of holdings as of Sept. 30. It does not show whether Harvard bought or sold any IBIT shares in October or November.

#841. Supreme Court Ends Custodia Bank’s Fight for a Fed Master Account, Leaving the Fed Free to Deny Crypto Banks Access

Supreme Court Ends Custodia Bank’s Fight for a Fed Master Account, Leaving the Fed Free to Deny Crypto Banks Access

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read | Sumber: https://bitcoinmagazine.com/news/supreme-court-ends-custodia-fed-master

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that the U.S.
  • Federal Reserve Board of Governors, No.
  • Recent findings suggest that A master account is a bank’s account at a Federal Reserve Bank, and the entry point to Fedwire and other payment services.

Industry observers note that the U.S. Supreme Court on Monday denied Custodia Bank’s petition to review the Federal Reserve’s refusal to give the Wyoming bitcoin bank a master account, ending chief executive Caitlin Long’s years-long fight for direct access to the central bank’s payment rails.

The case, Custodia Bank, Inc. v. Federal Reserve Board of Governors, No. 26-62, is listed under “certiorari denied” on the Court’s Monday order list. The denial leaves in place a Tenth Circuit ruling that regional Federal Reserve Banks have discretion to reject even eligible applicants, and it closes the last court path Custodia had to force the Fed’s hand.

Recent findings suggest that A master account is a bank’s account at a Federal Reserve Bank, and the entry point to Fedwire and other payment services. Without one, a state-chartered bank has to rely on a correspondent institution to move money.

Recent findings suggest that custodia is a Wyoming special purpose depository institution, a charter that bars it from making loans and requires dollar deposits to be fully reserved in liquid assets. After receiving that charter, it applied for a master account at the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City in October 2020. In January 2021, the Kansas City Fed confirmed the bank was legally eligible and told it there were “no showstoppers.” In August 2021, Custodia also applied for Federal Reserve membership.

According to recent reports, while those requests sat pending, the Board of Governors in August 2022 published guidelines for evaluating master-account applications. The rules put firms that are neither federally insured nor supervised by a federal banking agency into “Tier 3,” the group that “generally receive[s] the strictest level of review.” Custodia fell into that bucket.

On January 27, 2023, the Kansas City Fed denied the master account, citing an “unprecedented” business model “narrowly focused on crypto-asset activities” and concluding the risks were “highly likely” to be “inconsistent with safe and sound banking practices.” The same day, the Board denied Custodia’s membership application, saying approval “would be inconsistent with the financial, managerial, and corporate powers factors.”.

Custodia had already sued the Fed and the Kansas City Fed in June 2022 over the delay. On March 29, 2024, U.S. District Judge Scott W. Skavdahl in Wyoming ruled that the Federal Reserve Act gives Reserve Banks discretion to grant or deny master accounts, dismissed Custodia’s Administrative Procedure Act claim for lack of a final agency action, and granted the Kansas City Fed summary judgment.

The Tenth Circuit affirmed on October 31, 2025, in a 2-1 decision Bitcoin Magazine covered at the time. Judge David Ebel, joined by Judge Veronica Rossman, held that Section 342 of the Federal Reserve Act, which notes a Reserve Bank “may receive” deposits, is discretionary, and that the Monetary Control Act of 1980’s instruction that Fed services “shall be available” to nonmember banks is a pricing rule, not a right to an account.

In a recent development, tymkovich dissented. “We are bound by the ordinary language of the statute and, in my view, shall means shall,” he wrote. The 1980 law, he said, “mandates access to the Fed’s payment services for all nonmember depository institutions.” On March 13, 2026, the full Tenth Circuit denied rehearing, with Judges Hartz, Tymkovich and Eid voting to grant. Being denied a master account, Tymkovich wrote in that later dissent, is “akin to a death sentence.”.

Sources indicate that custodia’s July petition, filed by Kannon Shanmugam, asked whether the Monetary Control Act “gives presidents of regional Federal Reserve Banks discretionary authority to deny master accounts” to legally eligible nonmember banks. The Board and the Kansas City Fed opposed review. The Court distributed the case for its Nov. 13 conference and turned it down today.

Sources indicate that the practical effect is that a state charter, even one that makes a bank legally eligible, does not guarantee a door into the Fed’s payment system. Crypto-focused banks and other novel charters now have little judicial recourse, at least in the Tenth Circuit, if a Reserve Bank turns them away. Critics have long described that pattern of exclusion, and of banks cutting off crypto firms, as Operation Choke Point 2.0.

Neither Custodia nor Long had commented on the Supreme Court’s denial as of 10:07 a.m. ET Monday.

  • Former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson is sticking to his doubts about Bitcoin, telling a room full of crypto developers that he still can't see who is in charge of the world's largest cryptocurrency.
  • "As far as I can see, nobody knows who's in charge, apart from Yakimoto Nakasori, and I don't know where to find him," Johnson said at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London, deliberately mangling the name of Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto.

'Nobody Knows Who's in Charge': Boris Johnson Stands by Bitcoin Skepticism at Breakpoint.

Former UK Prime Minister Boris Johnson is sticking to his doubts about Bitcoin, telling a room full of crypto developers that he still can't see who is in charge of the world's largest cryptocurrency.

"As far as I can see, nobody knows who's in charge, apart from Yakimoto Nakasori, and I don't know where to find him," Johnson said at Solana's Breakpoint conference in London, deliberately mangling the name of Bitcoin's pseudonymous creator, Satoshi Nakamoto. "If six billion got stolen from some cryptocurrency, I wouldn't know who to apply to, or how to get the money back. That's my problem.".

Johnson was asked about a column he wrote in March for the Daily Mail, in which he called Bitcoin a "giant Ponzi scheme." The column drew pushback from the crypto industry, including Strategy executive chairman Michael Saylor, who tweeted that Bitcoin has no issuer, promoter or guaranteed return.

It has been revealed that bitcoin is not a Ponzi scheme. A Ponzi requires a central operator promising returns and paying early investors with funds from later ones. Bitcoin has no issuer, no promoter, and no guaranteed return—just an open, decentralized monetary network driven by code and market demand.

— Michael Saylor (@saylor) March 13, 2026.

On stage, Johnson admitted he is "not a great crypto buff" and holds little, if any, crypto himself. His view was shaped by a man he met in his Oxfordshire village who had lost thousands and kept paying more in the hope of recovering his losses, he remarked. "If the search for the greater fool had reached the wilds of South Oxfordshire, then probably there was something not quite right about this thing," Johnson said.

He also questioned the name itself, noting that "crypto" comes from the Greek for "hidden." "I don't think it's a good sell to tell people that this thing is concealed," he noted.

Recent findings suggest that johnson drew a sharp line between Bitcoin and the technology behind it. "Please don't think that my Luddite anxiety about crypto in any way means that I wish to slow down the development of blockchain, or the lead that London should rightly have in that sort of technology," he mentioned. When it comes to blockchain and tokenizing assets, the UK has "got to be at the forefront," he added.

Industry observers note that moderator Gareth Jenkinson, head of multimedia at The Block, pushed back when Johnson suggested Bitcoin was valuable to drug dealers, arguing that blockchains are far more traceable than cash. Asked by Johnson who guarantees Bitcoin, Jenkinson replied: "No one has to guarantee it. That's the beauty of the protocol.".

Recent findings suggest that lord Ross Kempsell, a Conservative member of the House of Lords who previously worked for Johnson, stated more than 8% of UK adults now hold some form of crypto asset, and that institutional adoption of blockchains is growing in the City of London. That ownership figure has fallen, however: the Financial Conduct Authority's latest consumer research, conducted in August and September 2025, found 8% of UK adults own crypto, down from 12% in 2024, though still double the level in 2021.

Sources indicate that the UK is "on the precipice of creating a lot of regulation" for the sector, Kempsell mentioned, pointing to the FCA's work on its regulatory perimeter and the Bank of England's coming stablecoin framework. "I share Boris's anxieties about the risks," he said, but within that perimeter, "there's a lot of scope here for a high growth industry.".

In June, the FCA finalized its rulebook for crypto firms ahead of a mandatory regime due to take effect in late 2027, days after the Bank of England eased its stablecoin rules, scrapping planned individual holding caps in favor of a £40 billion issuance limit per coin. The Bank has since been handed a legal duty to foster stablecoin innovation, and it has set out a shared vision for tokenization with the FCA.

Kempsell also argued that being outside the EU's Markets in Crypto-Assets (MiCA) regulation allows the UK to set its own rules for crypto. The EU itself is set to revise MiCA in 2027 to cover foreign stablecoin issuers.
