Solana has officially retired its six-year-old “mainnet beta” designation, with the network’s foundation saying the rebranding highlights the significant strides made since the blockchain first introduced in March 2020.

“Solana 1.0 recognizes the progress on network performance, resilience, and developer experience,” the Solana foundation wrote in a Monday statement. “That progress continues with this simplification of nomenclature.”.

The foundation emphasized that Solana has operated as a fully live network since its launch, arguing that retaining the beta designation had become outdated. It noted that the label, traditionally associated with technology still in its early testing stages, no longer accurately represented a blockchain already processing transactions and hosting active applications.

According to the Solana Foundation, the reclassification requires no action from users. Existing SOL holdings, account balances, and transaction histories will remain unchanged despite the protocol’s transition to version 1.0.

The foundation also advised developers and validator operators to stick to the specific instructions accompanying software releases, stressing that the new protocol designation does not mean all network upgrades or improvements become active automatically.

Recent findings suggest that solana’s move to protocol version 1.0 comes as the network continues pursuing major infrastructure improvements, with Alpenglow and Firedancer among its most closely watched developments. Both initiatives aim to strengthen Solana’s performance, reliability, and ability to support growing on-chain activity.

Recent findings suggest that the first major milestone is Alpenglow, Solana’s fresh consensus protocol, which went live on mainnet on October 21. The upgrade targets transaction finality of approximately 150 milliseconds, a significant improvement from the previous 12.8-second timeframe. Transaction finality refers to the moment a blockchain permanently confirms a transaction, meaning it is considered settled and cannot be reversed under normal network conditions. Faster finality could make Solana more attractive for payments, decentralized finance, and institutional applications that require near-instant transaction settlement.

Meanwhile, Firedancer brings another important improvement through an independently developed validator client built by Jump Crypto. It provides an alternative to Solana’s existing Agave client, reducing the network’s dependence on a single software implementation. This client diversity could strengthen network resilience by limiting the risk that a bug affecting one implementation disrupts the entire blockchain.

The foundation added that the rebranding establishes a unified system for tracking Solana’s updates, allowing developers, validators, and infrastructure providers to identify protocol changes consistently, regardless of the software client they use.

Vitalik Buterin now favors leanPCS as a potentially faster route for EIP-8288.

leanPCS could enable STARK verification at an estimated 20,000–40,000 gas.

EIP-8288 remains a draft, with leanPCS integration and its reference implementation unfinished.

Ethereum’s quantum-safe upgrade may have found a faster route forward, but the technical work isn’t finished.

Vitalik Buterin has shifted his support toward leanPCS under EIP-8288, arguing it could deliver much of leanSTARK’s flexibility without forcing developers to standardize a newly introduced instruction-set architecture first.

That’s a significant change in direction. It isn’t a completed upgrade, though.

EIP-8288 aims to reduce the amount of cryptographic data Ethereum must carry on-chain. Instead of publishing every signature or proof, nodes aggregate verification results into STARK proofs, which can then be aggregated further.

The chain ultimately receives compact claims and a master proof, rather than every underlying cryptographic object.

The motivation is becoming harder to ignore. Current 65-byte ECDSA signatures could grow to 1–6 kilobytes under proposed quantum-safe schemes.

It has been revealed that over the past few weeks I've gone from thinking leanPCS is total bull to being a total bull. So let me explain some of these buzzwords in more detail.At the core, 8288 is about hyper-scaling data and execution for any computation that needs to get performed on a piece of data….

According to recent reports, meanwhile, zero-knowledge proofs could expand from roughly 200–1,000 bytes to around 128 kilobytes when using STARKs. Putting all that data on-chain isn’t a practical scaling strategy.

Buterin’s latest explanation separates three approaches. leanSPHINCS supports a specific hash-based signature scheme, offering quantum-safe accounts with a proposed cost of 4,096 gas for 64 bytes.

Industry observers note that leanSTARK is more flexible. Customers could prove almost any computation, but Ethereum would first need to agree on a programming language or instruction-set architecture. That’s a difficult standard to lock in.

leanPCS offers a middle path. A polynomial commitment scheme proves a statement about a polynomial, and Buterin estimates STARK verification through this mechanism could cost around 20,000–40,000 gas.

Sources indicate that it may require more claims on-chain than leanSTARK. In exchange, developers retain greater flexibility over off-chain proof systems.

Sources indicate that the published EIP-8288 draft presently specifies leanSPHINCS and reserves leanSTARK, while leanPCS isn’t yet included as a verification mode. Its reference implementation remains listed as TBD, and no activation date is confirmed.

That gap matters. An endorsement isn’t a specification, and a specification isn’t a working network upgrade.

For now, Ethereum’s quantum-safe upgrade has a potentially faster technical direction, but leanPCS still needs formal integration, implementation and approval before it can become part of the network.

From $2 to $60,000: The Eternal “Bitcoin Is a Scam” Timeline

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 2 min read | Sumber: https://zycrypto.com/from-2-to-60000-the-eternal-bitcoin-is-a-scam-timeline/

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Industry observers note that as Bitcoin hurtles toward the $60k support level, critics are having a field day once again, calling it a scam and a pyramid scheme, among other things.
  • The post documents that every major price drop has been met with triumphant celebrations over the digital currency’s demise.
  • Industry observers note that bitcoin first experienced a major crash in 2011 when it dropped to $2.

Industry observers note that as Bitcoin hurtles toward the $60k support level, critics are having a field day once again, calling it a scam and a pyramid scheme, among other things. However, one analyst noted that the digital currency has fallen every 4 years or so over the last 3 cycles, and the digital asset is simply following established trends.

The post documents that every major price drop has been met with triumphant celebrations over the digital currency’s demise. BTC has already dropped 50% from its all-time high (ATH) of $126.5k set roughly a year ago. While naysayers are having a field day right now, seasoned investors understand that the premier digital currency has a history of recovering well in the years that follow.

Industry observers note that bitcoin first experienced a major crash in 2011 when it dropped to $2. It was the first time it happened on such a noticeable scale, and many legacy analysts quickly declared it “dead” or a scam. However, Bitcoin recovered well and experienced a major bull run two years later that propelled it above $1,000 for a short while. This represented a 500x price increase.

In a recent development, afterward, Bitcoin started to cool off again, and in 2015, the premier digital asset crashed to $250, sparking another episode of critics calling it a scam. However, the digital asset once again started to rise strongly two years after this occurrence and reached as high as $19,500 in late 2017, representing a 78x increase.

Sources indicate that however, 2018 proved brutal for the cryptocurrency, and it dropped to sub-$3,000 levels near the end of the calendar year. Once again, the naysayers, led by Peter Schiff, were quick to declare it dead. The cryptocurrency remained on the defensive for about a year before beginning a major price recovery. By the end of 2021, Bitcoin had risen to $69k, representing a 23x price increase.

The 2022 bear market, like clockwork, soon followed, and the digital asset dropped to $15k, once again triggering critics. However, the bearish scenario eventually ended, and Bitcoin started to recover strongly in early 2024, resulting in a major price boom that pushed the cryptocurrency to $126.5k by October 2025, representing an 8.4x gain. Now, the digital currency is struggling above $60k and may likely fall even further below the key support. Critics are active, and in all practical purposes, this is peak FUD season.

Bitcoin’s recent troubles align with previous cycles, and it is crucial for long-term investors to stay patient and avoid panic selling.

XRP is struggling to reclaim $1, but its derivatives market is showing an increasingly unusual setup. Traders betting against the token are now paying funding fees to maintain their positions. This creates an interesting possibility for the XRP price prediction. If buying pressure returns, bearish traders could face mounting losses and forced liquidations.

However, the market is not quite ready for a bullish victory lap. Open interest is falling, long positions have already suffered heavy liquidations, and XRP still needs to reclaim vital resistance levels.

It has been revealed that XRP traded around $0.95, following another difficult session for the crypto market. Meanwhile, its futures market is flashing a rate that dropped in aggregated funding to -0.0068% every eight hours, equivalent to roughly -7.4% annually.

Negative funding means short sellers pay long traders to maintain their perpetual futures positions. In other words, bears are effectively paying a premium to maintain their bearish exposure.

Recent findings suggest that hyperliquid demonstrated an even more pronounced imbalance, with XRP funding reaching approximately -10.2% annually. The figures suggest bearish positioning has become increasingly expensive across several derivatives markets.

However, there is another side to this trade. XRP open interest declined 5.74% over 24 hours to approximately $1.97 billion, so traders are reducing leverage rather than aggressively opening fresh positions.

Industry observers note that while XRP traders debate whether another recovery is coming, Bitcoin Hyper ($HYPER) is approaching an notable milestone of its own. The Bitcoin Layer 2 project has raised more than $33.2 million during its presale, with its token presently priced at just $0.0136.

The presale is scheduled to conclude on November 26, leaving a narrowing window before its anticipated token launch. Buyers choosing the staking option are also being offered an advertised 35% APY during the presale period.

Bitcoin Hyper aims to bring faster Bitcoin transactions and decentralized applications to a new Layer 2 environment. Its architecture combines Solana Virtual Machine execution with zero-knowledge proofs and Bitcoin settlement.

Industry observers note that the project has already introduced testnet components, including its explorer, wallet, faucet, and bridge. With the presale approaching its scheduled conclusion, the remaining allocation and upcoming launch milestone could attract additional attention from traders looking beyond established crypto networks.

Industry observers note that the immediate question is whether bearish positioning has become sufficiently expensive to trigger an unexpected reversal. A negative funding rate alone cannot confirm a short squeeze. XRP needs to attract fresh spot buyers, recover momentum, and force short sellers to close their positions.

The first key hurdle remains $1.00. Reclaiming this psychological level could encourage sidelined buyers to return and create additional pressure on leveraged shorts.

A sustained move above $1.00 would put $1.10 within reach, followed by a potential test of $1.20 if short liquidations accelerate.

According to recent reports, however, the bearish scenario remains firmly in play. Losing the recent $0.89 low could expose XRP to another decline toward $0.80, particularly if Bitcoin continues weakening.

For now, the XRP price prediction hinges on whether negative funding translates into actual buying pressure. Bears are paying longs, but bulls still need to deliver the rally. If they do, the same traders betting against XRP could become the fuel behind its next recovery.

In a recent development, while millions of players recently logged into World of Warcraft: Forever, Blizzard’s ambitious reimagining of classic Azeroth that launched globally on November 4, 2026, another, far stranger virtual world has been quietly humming along on a Cardano MMORPG via its privacy-focused Midnight network. It’s called Midnight City, and it proudly bills itself as “the first AI MMORPG that plays itself.”.

Industry observers note that the premise is delightfully hands-off. Instead of creating a character and spending hours clicking through quests, you claim an AI agent, give it some direction, and then largely step back. The agent lives, works, fights, gathers resources, crafts, trades, and forms relationships around the clock in a persistent city.

This MMORPG launch on Cardano comes as ADA crypto trades around $0.15, down 1.3% over the past 24 hours, following a brutal seven-day stretch in which it fell more than -12%.

The gates to Midnight City are open. 🌆🕛A living city populated by autonomous AI agents — generating real transactions, real activity, and real proof generation on Midnight.Step inside and watch rational privacy in motion.Explore the districts.Inspect transactions.Toggle… pic.twitter.com/e19sHNotcC.

In a recent development, you can check in, nudge it, or intervene when something vital happens, but the world keeps turning whether you’re online or not. Official materials describe agents that hold jobs, accumulate gear, chat with one another, and generate real activity on the Midnight blockchain. Privacy is built in via zero-knowledge tech, and the longer-term vision includes agents holding their own wallets to trade and earn privately on consumers’ behalf.

Charles Hoskinson recently gave the project a playful shout-out on X, noting how Midnight City seems to be gathering Cardano’s memecoin community under one virtual roof, tagging favorites like Snek, Hosky, and others in a lighthearted “where’s my love” moment.

Sources indicate that the official site (midnight.city) currently demonstrates open beta status with limited usernames, free-to-play access, and live stats ticking away: thousands of agents online, resources being gathered, and citizens accumulating. It’s less a traditional MMO and more a living simulation mixed with an autonomous economic experiment.

Almost certainly not in the traditional sense. WoW’s cultural footprint, subscription model, and pure entertainment gravity are in another league. But “as significant” doesn’t have to mean the same kind of big.

If Midnight City successfully turns autonomous agents into a compelling, privacy-preserving playground, complete with real economic activity, emergent stories, and that addictive “my agent did what while I was away?” loop, it could carve out a meaningful niche in the emerging agentic and blockchain-gaming space.

It has been revealed that it won’t replace raiding Molten Core with your guild, but it might become the place where a different kind of player parks their digital life. For now, the gates are open, the agents are queuing, and the city is already moving.

It has been revealed that whether it grows into something substantial or remains a fascinating experiment will depend on how well the AI, the economy, and the privacy tech actually deliver. In the meantime, it’s hard not to smile at the idea of Cardano’s memecoins and AI citizens sharing a virtual neighborhood while the rest of the gaming world queues for classic-plus raids.

According to recent reports, as of mid-November 2026, Cardano is trading near $0.15–$0.152, according to CoinGecko data. The token remains in a clear short-term downtrend, sitting well below its 50-day and 200-day moving averages.

Daily RSI has dropped into oversold territory around 27–28, a level that has occasionally preceded relief bounces. However, MACD remains negative, and price continues to print lower highs, indicating that sellers still control the broader structure.

In a recent development, key support is clustered near $0.143–$0.146, while immediate resistance sits around $0.158–$0.165. A sustained break and daily close above the $0.18–$0.20 zone would be needed to meaningfully improve the technical outlook. Until then, the bias stays bearish with limited upside conviction.
